Sports.title: Scandal-hit Fifa President Gianni Infantino accused of taking undeclared second salary worth millions
Sports.content:
Next

SCANDAL-HIT Fifa President Gianni Infantino has been accused of taking an undeclared second salary worth millions.

The Times reported that Infantino has been receiving two separate salaries – one from Fifa in Switzerland and another from a World Cup organising company in the USA.



The latter was not declared by FIFA and is said to be worth millions of dollars.

Since Infantino was elected as its president in 2016, Fifa has committed to publishing his salary, bonus and allowances — and that of the general secretary — every year.



The revelations are likely to increase the scrutiny on Infantino, 56, who has been under pressure to resign since The Times revealed in July his plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

In 2024, Infantino was stated by Fifa’s annual report as earning £3.88m.



However, a financial return filed with the United States’ Internal Revenue Service by the company set up to organise the World Cup, FWC2026 US Inc, for that year shows Infantino was paid a further $1.76m (£1.3m) that was not publicly disclosed by Fifa in its annual report.

Infantino was reportedly paid similar sums – or even more – in 2025 and 2026.

Miguel Maduro, the former chairman of Fifa’s governance committee, said the failure to make the extra payments public was “a clear violation of Fifa’s statutes” and needed independent investigation.

In more bad news for Infantino, former Spurs defender Ramon Vega has said he wants to stand against the Fifa president.



As European football’s top brass prepared to meet in Berlin to plot the next move in their fight against the world governing body, ex-Switzerland centre-back Vega, 55, became the first to actually put his head above the parapet.

Vega accused Infantino and the current Fifa leadership of “demoralising” the game, blasting that “weak governance has damaged Fifa’s credibility and eroded trust across the global football family.

“We must stop this conflict from escalating.”

Sports.title: Gabriel Magalhaes opens up over heartbreaking penalty miss vs PSG as Arsenal star makes defiant vow for future spotkicks
Sports.content:
Next

GABRIEL MAGALHAES felt the ultimate heartbreak of missing the decisive penalty in last season’s Champions League final – but has vowed to step up again if needed.

The towering Arsenal defender, 28, blasted his spot kick over the bar to hand Paris Saint-Germain their second successive European crown last May.



Gabriel isn’t exactly known for his ability from 12 yards out and had never even taken a penalty for Arsenal before that day.

But he still volunteered to step up as the Gunners’ fifth penalty taker in Budapest.



His miss denied Arsenal a historic double and left him on the verge of tears, but Gabriel has promised that he would do it all again if he needs to this season.

He said: “Of course, if I have another penalty, I will be there to take it. My team-mates helped me a lot.



“Of course, I was sad, and I didn’t want to miss a penalty, but I have learned from it and if I have another opportunity, I will be ready to take it.”

Arsenal’s players rallied round Gabriel following his miss five months ago, immediately trying to lift his spirits back up.

But it was a player on the other team that was first to put an arm around Gabriel, his compatriot Marquinhos.

The PSG captain’s touching moment earned him the inaugural UEFA Respect: Beyond the Game Award in August.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But Gabriel needed even more help from his Brazil team-mates during the World Cup to help him move past the heartache.

The defender added: “In football everything can happen. In the final, after the penalty, they [my team-mates] grabbed me.

“Of course I was sad and I just wanted to forget that moment. After that I had the World Cup and the Brazilian players and the coach said a lot of positive things to me.

“Like Marquinhos did when he was there and he helped me a lot because it’s not easy when you miss a penalty in the final and they helped me a lot by saying a lot of positive things to me.”



The Gunners play their first home Champions League game since that defeat to PSG on Tuesday night when they host Gabriel’s former club Lille at the Emirates.

Mikel Arteta was the man who brought Gabriel to North London from Lille, signing him in 2020 for just £26m.

The Arsenal chief has developed Gabriel into one of the best defenders in Europe and reckons that last season’s penalty despair is a testament to how he has transformed in the last six years.

Arteta said: “I think Gabi’s transformation since he joined from Lille has been incredible to witness.



“I’m so proud of what he’s done and the manner that he’s done it.

“First of all, his personal transformation and then the way he has evolved all the qualities that he already had to become one of the big leaders of the team and of the club. He certainly deserves that.

“That also comes with responsibility, he took that responsibility and in that moment it did not go the right way but I’m sure if we had the opportunity to do it again then he would do it again.”

Gabriel has been shouldering the responsibility of Arsenal’s back line so far this season, helping bed in Ezri Konsa in the absence of the injured William Saliba.

The 24-time Brazil cap has become one of the most well-respected defenders around, earning a spot in the past three PFA Team of the Year squads in a row.



After recovering from his nightmare in Budapest, Gabriel now has his eyes on using that heartbreak as motivation to go another step further and lifting the Champions League.

He said: “We are very motivated, and we want to attack every trophy.

“Now we will have another opportunity to win in the Champions League, and play at home, and we are ready to go.”

Sports.title: ‘I love this part’ – Michael Carrick lays down gauntlet to Man Utd flops as he battles to save job against Simeone & Co
Sports.content:
Next

MICHAEL CARRICK wants to see who is up for the fight at Manchester United — as he battles to save his job.

The under-pressure Red Devils boss claims he is learning who wants to be at Old Trafford “for the long term”.



But Carrick’s own future looks bleak unless he can spark a turnaround — starting in the Champions League at Atletico Madrid tomorrow.

Carrick, who has overseen United’s worst league start in 40 years, said: “I love this part when it’s not quite going for you, you see who’s really there.



“You see within the players, the squad, the club, who wants to be here for the long term and really attached to it and really means something.

“The supporters are there, they want it, they’re desperate for it, and we’ve got to give them something.

“So you’ve got to sometimes embrace the challenges to get to where you want to be, and we’re right there now in the middle of it.

“But I totally believe that we’ll come through it.”

United have picked up just six points from six Prem games this season under Carrick and sit 13th in the table.

Old Trafford fans booed their team at three separate stages during Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Carrick added: “I understand when it’s not going too well, there’s a real kind of clamour and a real feeling of ‘it’s a disaster and everything needs to be changed’.

“I kind of get that, but that’s not in our mindset, that’s certainly not in my mindset.

“To achieve anything really, you’ve got to be able to deal with things that are difficult, you’ve got to overcome things, that’s just part of it. I did it throughout my career, and it’s just the way it is.

“We need to do something about it now and accept the reality and win games, of course we do.

“The last three goals we’ve probably conceded were all goals where you can definitely do something about that, we know that, the boys know that, and that’s had a major impact on what the league all of a sudden looks like.



“So that wasn’t happening last season, and can be the difference.

“There was going to be a period when it was going to become a little bit more challenging and a little bit sticky.

“Football and building something takes a journey and you’ve got to overcome things.”

Atletico boss Diego Simeone will celebrate his 15th anniversary as their manager in December.



And Carrick highlighted that long-serving managers have suffered rough spells.

He explained: “I’m sitting here [against] a coach that’s been here a long, long time and I’m sure there’s times when there have been waves when it hasn’t quite gone to plan.

“They’ve had huge successes and winning leagues and being around the late stages of the Champions League, but there’ve been times when it hasn’t gone quite to plan.

“We’ve got teams in our league that have had success, but it hasn’t necessarily all been in one direction.”



Kobbie Mainoo and Luke Shaw are out of tomorrow’s clash against Atletico through injury.

Carrick confirmed: “They’ve not travelled. Both picked up issues in the game on Saturday, so we’re kind of working through that to see what that looks like.”

Sports.title: Michael Carrick insists no Man Utd player is ‘undroppable’ amid Bruno Fernandes’ flagging form
Sports.content:

MICHAEL CARRICK has stressed no Manchester United player is “undroppable” amid Bruno Fernandes’ flagging form.

Fernandes has been carrying an injury over the past month but has clocked up 90 minutes in seven of United’s eight games.



The 32-year-old played in three of Portugal‘s four Nations League games during the recent internationals but was rested for the 2-1 win away to Norway.

Fernandes is the reigning Professional Footballers’ Association and Football Writers’ Association Player of the Year but he has underperformed regularly so far this term.



“Listen, this is not on Bruno, this line, so don’t use it for that,” Carrick insisted. “But nobody’s guaranteed a place in the team.

“Don’t take that as, ‘oh, so then that’s on on Bruno’. I don’t mean that, that’s just in in general.

“There’s a level of performance, there’s a level of behaviour, there’s a level of understanding that we need as a group and as a squad and as a team to perform.

“And all the boys know that, they understand that, they’ve got their own standards and they want to achieve things and they want to be the best.

“So I think that’s pretty clear and it has to be like that.”

“He was carrying something,” Carrick acknowledged. “It happens a lot, people don’t maybe realise it, but it happens a lot, players play with issues.

Sports.title: Andy Burnham under pressure to reveal full extent of Man City links with club’s tycoon owners
Sports.content:
Next

ANDY Burnham is facing calls to reveal the full extent of his Manchester City links after his former mayoral office issued a mealy-mouthed defence.

The PM bowed to pressure to publish meetings with the club’s owners after fury over his defence of the UAE tycoons.



He said he had held one significant meeting with City’s chairman while mayor of Greater Manchester.

Mr Burnham was mayor while City were breaching the Premier League’s financial regulations.



The PM also conceded that he attended a handful of City games, including Vincent Kompany’s testimonial, where he spoke to the chairman informally in the stands.

In a statement, Greater Manchester Combined Authority said: “In his capacity as Mayor, he was a guest of Manchester City FC at home matches on a small number of occasions, including attending Vincent Kompany’s testimonial match in September 2019, where he met the Chairman informally in the stands. These have been declared in the usual way.”



But shadow sports minister Louie French said footie fans deserved more of an explanation. He accused the PM of hiding behind the authority and said he must take full responsibility.

Mr French said: “We have been given precious little information about these meetings, what was discussed and what may have been agreed.



“If Burnham has nothing to hide, why is he being so tight-lipped?

“His bizarre intervention in defence of Man City’s owners has raised serious concerns among fans. It’s time for the Prime Minister to come clean about his relationship with City Football Group so the public can make their own conclusions.”

City were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018.

The club denied wrongdoing and appealed against the verdict.

Mr Burnham last month said he would be “really concerned” if City’s Abu Dhabi owners sold the club after the finding.



He credited them with being “a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester”.

Downing Street later sought to clarify the PM’s comments, saying he considered the judgment serious and believed those responsible should face the consequences where wrongdoing was established.

Mr Burnham said he would “put out there” everything he had done to work with the club’s owners as mayor in an interview with the Rest Is Politics podcast.

Sports.title: Man City stars used to flog £3bn Abu Dhabi housing development for club’s owners despite fury over cheating scandal
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER City stars are being used to flog a £3billion Abu Dhabi luxury housing development despite the furore over the cheating scandal.

Erling Haaland has bagged a waterfront mansion and is among players in a website video promoting the “Manchester City Yas residence”.



City executives also ­feature in the ads.

A Premier League panel found the club guilty of “sham” football deals.



Star striker Haaland and former manger Pep Guardiola were among those featured in a glittering launch bash last Thursday at the Etihad Stadium in the United Arab Emirates’ capital.

Last night football author John-Paul O’Neill said: “It all seems very brazen and indicative of the stance they are taking and the contempt the club holds for the investigation. They are sticking two fingers up and saying, ‘So what, we’ll just carry on as we are’.



“The whole set-up of the massive investment in City is about promoting the UAE. It’s purely business, purely marketing.”

Football campaigner Mickey Ambrose, an ex-Chelsea and Charlton player, added: “It’s quite rich for City to be flogging luxury houses in Abu Dhabi following the guilty verdicts. Who says cheaters don’t prosper? The supporters must be so disappointed by the whole thing.”

Haaland, who scored in Sunday’s 3-0 over Liverpool, has bought a five-bedroom villa worth at least £1.9million on the complex by developers Ohana.

He also appeared in a video shown to more than 4,000 VIPs, brokers, and government officials at the spectacular event.



Other City stars to have featured in promotional videos and photos include Phil Foden, Nico O’Reilly and Mateo Kovacic, plus former ­forward Omar Marmoush who has been sold to Spurs.

Smiling on screen, Haaland said: “I’m so happy to tell you I’m joining the Ohana Manchester City project and we will be neighbours in Abu Dhabi. I just got a house and so did my father.

“By the way, you might have seen him there — hello, Dad. See you guys soon and enjoy.”



Haaland’s father, former City player Alf-Inge Haaland, 53, then appeared live on stage.

As property owners, he and his son get an automatic ten-year United Arab Emirates visa under local investment rules.

The announcement, seen in a YouTube video, also features Guardiola taking centre stage as the project’s official brand ambassador.

It comes at a hugely sensitive moment for the club, found to have artificially inflated its revenue by almost £900million between 2009 and 2018 through “sham” sponsorship deals linked to Abu Dhabi.

City have appealed against the verdict and claim to have “irrefutable evidence” proving their innocence.



The club is majority-owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan through the Abu Dhabi United Group.

The mega-rich firm also owns the £365million Co-op Live Arena, and swathes of luxury apartment blocks across the east of Manchester after being given a “sweetheart deal” by authorities.

The 1.67million-square- metre complex on Abu Dhabi’s Yas Island will boast its own Manchester City Training Academy, a dedicated City Lounge and the team’s logo and branding throughout.



It will have an ultra-modern fitness centre, with rooms for cryotherapy, oxygen therapy and hydrotherapy.

There will be rooftop football pitches and match-viewing rooms.

A computer-generated image of the development showed the Manchester City Sports Clubhouse with a giant club crest on its roof.

The development will include restaurants, tennis and basketball courts, cycling and jogging routes, private beach access and a canal-side promenade.

A skate park, climbing walls, parkour park, karting arena and bike arena are also being built, with the first phase set for completion in 2029.



Prices for more than 2,000 properties range from £770,000 to more than £7.25million.

The glitzy launch included pyrotechnics, dancers, freestyle footballers in City kits and even an appearance by club mascots Moonchester and Moonbeam.

Guardiola came on stage saying: “It’s a pleasure to be here, my ­second home.”



During a Q&A session, he said: “In professional sport, we understand that performance depends on more than training. Recovery, balance and well-being are just as important, and those principles matter in everyday life too.

“Manchester City Yas Residences by Ohana places sport and wellness at the heart of the community, giving residents opportunities to stay active, recharge and spend time together. I am pleased to join Ohana Development as its official brand ambassador for this unique community.”

Husein Salem, boss of Ohana Development, said: “Welcoming Pep Guardiola as the project’s official brand ambassador adds a meaningful dimension to this vision.”

City announced its partnership with Ohana on its website in September.

That month it emerged an independent panel set up by the Premier League had found them guilty of breaching financial rules between 2009 — a year after being bought by ADUG — and 2018.



Using the word “sham” eight times, the panel said the club arranged “sham contracts” as well as “relying on sham agreements”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

City were first informed of the verdicts in July.

They had an aggressive approach in the summer transfer window, which saw seven senior signings arrive at the Etihad Stadium at a cost of more than £450million.

Sports.title: Coventry 4 Newcastle 1: Toon blown away in thrashing as Frank Lampard’s Sky Blues run riot to seal back-to-back wins
Sports.content:
Next

COVENTRY CITY fans waited 9,310 DAYS to witness a home Premier League goal – and they were rewarded with FOUR of them on an outstanding night.

Jack Rudoni, Sidiki Cherif, Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni sensationally gave Frank Lampard’s City lift-off at home in a thunderous display against Newcastle United – and showed that they can no longer be considered whipping boys.



Striker Rudoni was two months off being born when John Hartson scored the previous Premier League goal for Coventry on home turf 25 years ago.

That came in a 1-0 win over Sunderland on April 16, 2001 – shortly before their long hiatus in the Football League began – but it occurred at the demolished Highfield Road.



Rudoni’s clever penalty on six minutes is the first goal notched at a raucous Coventry Building Society Arena.

And in the second half, Cherif and substitutes Simms and Mfuni got in on the act in a well-deserved and well-earned victory over the Toon Army.

The momentum earned from the away win at Nottingham Forest had not been halted despite the three-week international break.

Given that both sides have their defensive vulnerabilities, this had all the makings of being a high-scoring, entertaining and end-to-end clash, and so it proved.

Nobody in the opening five matches of this campaign had faced more shots on their goal than Newcastle (97), while Coventry (87) had only fared marginally better.

On an unseasonably mild autumnal night, the first shot that the Toon Army faced was from 12 yards on six minutes as they gave away a penalty in sloppy, careless fashion.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek did not deal with the relatively straightforward ball into the box and then tripped up Cherif, who had leapt high in the air to avoid injury.

Referee John Brooks awarded the pen straightaway – VAR backed up his decision, deeming there to be “significant contact” – and from the spot, Rudoni scored with composure, fooling Hornicek in the process.

The Englishman, 25, ran over to the corner flag and unveiled a white shirt underneath his Sky Blue one that read: Get well soon, Nan.

A whole generation of Coventry fans had waited so long to witness that special moment and boy did they celebrate it properly.

Teenager Cherif had a chance to double that lead on 28 minutes but the finish was weak and comfortable for Czech Hornicek.



That came at the end of a breakaway move that started after Newcastle’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo unexplainably, remarkably dummied the ball in the six-yard box when he should have shot on target or tested Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth.

Only the Belgian forward will really know what on earth he was doing in that moment of madness.

Why let it roll through his legs? Had there been an incorrect call from a teammate?



How foolish he must have felt – and Fernandez-Pardo would have felt even sillier when he failed to score with two minutes left of the first half.

Though he did all the hard work by skipping round the keeper, his strike towards an empty net hit the hip of Bobby Thomas, who recovered well after losing out in the foot race.

Three minutes after the restart, Guinean-born Frenchman Cherif, 19, scored a goal he will always remember – a delightful finish outside the box that went through the legs of Newcastle defender Sven Botman to delight the home punters.

Poached from Turkish giants Fenerbahçe for £21million, Cherif looks quite the player and this was some way to mark a first Prem start.



Newcastle needed a spark from somewhere – Rushworth almost conceded an own goal on 56 minutes but recovered possession, and then Joe Willock blazed over the bar before the hour mark.

Hope of salvaging at least a point came from an unlikely source – Botman produced an unstoppable left-footed strike on 70 minutes that would normally come from a centre forward, not a central defender.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But the Geordies, stopped at every turn by gallant home defending, squandered the chance to go fourth in the table following their first loss to Coventry since October 1999.

Simms gave Lampard some breathing space when his strike deflected off Malick Thiaw on 81 minutes and then Mfuni’s well-hit effort sealed a wonderful night for this Sky Blue part of the Midlands.

Sports.title: Coventry thump Newcastle for first home win to move out of drop zone
Sports.content:
Coventry made it back-to-back Premier League wins with a thumping 4-1 home victory over Newcastle to move Frank Lampard's side out of the relegation zone.

Goals from Jack Rudoni, teenager Sidiki Cherif and substitutes Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni gave the Sky Blues their first home win of the season.

A stunning Sven Botman strike had given Newcastle hope of a comeback in the 70th minute, but Simms restored the hosts' two-goal lead with his first touch 11 minutes later before Mfuni superbly added a fourth to become Coventry's youngest-ever Premier League goalscorer.

A night of firsts for Coventry… First home win of the season

First PL home win in 25 years

First PL home goals of the season

First career penalty goal for Jack Rudoni

First Coventry goal for Sidiki Cherif

Ellis Simms scored with his first touch

First senior goal for Stephen Mfuni

The visitors, who suffered a second consecutive 4-1 away defeat, made a nightmare start at the CBS Arena as goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek brought down summer signing Cherif to allow Rudoni to hit a sixth-minute penalty opener.

Newcastle responded well to falling behind but were wasteful as Matias Fernandez-Pardo missed two big chances, with his one-on-one opportunity cleared off the line by Bobby Thomas.

Coventry then punished their profligacy immediately after the restart as Cherif fantastically doubled the lead in the 48th minute with the 19-year-old's powerful low strike from just outside the box, his first goal for the club.

Botman's goal, however, was even better as he thundered home from long range, but Coventry hit back through Simm's deflected strike three minutes and 15 seconds after he came off the bench.

Eighteen-year-old summer signing Mfuni, who joined from Manchester City on loan, then hit his first senior goal in the 86th minute to cap off a fine evening for Lampard's side.

Coventry can make it three victories in a row when they visit winless Tottenham next Monday, live on Sky Sports, while Newcastle aim to bounce back against Aston Villa at home on Saturday, also live on Sky Sports.

Carra: Newcastle have been 'beaten up' in their last two away games

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher speaking on Monday Night Football:

"Every manager has their own way, but when you think of the lack of physicality in that [Newcastle] team, it might be a case where you leave one of the strikers out and go with an extra body in midfield.

"It's a young team, and it isn't as physically powerful as a lot of the teams in the Premier League.

"And in their last two away games, they've been beaten up twice - and that's got to stop very quickly."

Jaissle apologises to fans

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matthias Jaissle apologises to the travelling Newcastle fans

Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle speaking to Sky Sports:

"We're frustrated. It's a feeling you don't want to have on a Monday evening after a match where you should win.

"We can only apologise to the fans who came here; they deserve a different result.

"We need to analyse it, clearly. There were bits that were good, but in both boxes, to defend our own goal, we need to improve and also score goals. The opportunities were there, but the desire and hunger to finish the attacks was missing.

"We need to improve on the things we can control, and that's a lot right now."

Lampard: We played like the team we want to be

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Frank Lampard says his Coventry side delivered a 'complete performance'

Coventry boss Frank Lampard speaking to Sky Sports:

"We played like the team we want to be here. There's so much spirit and energy. We know we're going to have to suffer at times in games; we have to understand what the level is.

"But the work ethic from the team, the belief, then you get what you deserve, which is great finishes. We haven't had that rub of the green, which might have helped us nick a few more points.

"As a complete performance, we've got to keep our feet on the ground because it's only one game and we need 30 more of those. But it's a great feeling for the players."

Story of the match in stats

6: COVENTRY GOAL! Rudoni scores from the spot after Newcastle goalkeeper Hornicek brought down Cherif.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Rudoni scores Coventry's first Premier League home goal for more than 25 years

29: BIG CHANCES AT BOTH ENDS! Fernandez-Pardo dummies at the front post rather than going for goal himself, which allows Coventry to break through Cherif, but he shoots straight at the goalkeeper.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matias Fernandez-Pardo and Sidiki Cherif squander chances in quick succession

31: NEWCASTLE GO CLOSE! Jacob Murphy hooks the ball back across goal, but Thomas does well to get ahead of Fernandez-Pardo to clear before he can head home.

43: WHAT A CHANCE FOR NEWCASTLE! Thomas to the rescue again as he rushes back to clear Fernandez-Pardo's shot off the line after he had rounded the goalkeeper.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bobby Thomas blocks Fernandez-Pardo's shot to keep Coventry in front

48: COVENTRY GOAL! Minutes into the second half, Coventry double their lead through a fine Cherif strike from just outside the box.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cherif puts Coventry 2-0 in front with a wonderful strike

55: IT SHOULD BE THREE-NIL! Cherif misses a glorious close-range chance to grab his second as he fires wide after a poor Malick Thiaw clearance.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sven Botman scores a screamer to pull one back for Newcastle

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ellis Simms restores the Sky Blues' two-goal lead following a Joelinton blunder

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stephen Mfuni makes it four for the Sky Blues

Analysis: Coventry teach Newcastle a lesson in finishing

Sky Sports' Ron Walker:

On a night where they faced the Premier League's second-highest xG overperformers, it was Coventry who taught Newcastle a lesson in finishing at the CBS Arena.

It was one they had learned the hard way too, with the worst shot conversion of any team in the league coming into Monday's game and just one of 51 shots finding the back of the net to date.

Image: Coventry celebrate Rudoni's opener that set them on their way to their first home win of the season

But football is a funny old game. A 4-1 scoreline suggests Newcastle were outplayed, which could not be further from the truth, though they were certainly outfought.

Where Coventry stood resilient - even clearing off their own line from Fernandez-Pardo once he had rounded Carl Rushworth - Newcastle caused too many of their own problems, and, for once, the Sky Blues took full advantage.

Three superb finishes, and an early penalty, saw them to their first Premier League home win in more than 9,000 days, but their finishing was still not Coventry's most impressive quality on the night.

That fortitude, digging in after taking an early lead and hanging on after Botman's wonder strike had given Newcastle a glimmer of hope at 2-1, was what won them the day and, on fight at least, that was enough to crown them worthy winners.

They have already needed that mental strength to bounce back from four goalless and pointless games to start their Premier League return, and, in a league as punishing as this, that could be what decides whether they will stay there come May.

Sports.title: Renshaw stars as Australia close in on first Test victory in Durban
Sports.content:
Matt Renshaw continued to hog centre stage as Australia pushed closer to winning the first Test against South Africa in Durban.

Renshaw added a second-innings knock of 82 to his game-shaping 190 and was not finished there. After Australia declared with a lead of 420, the occasional off-spinner picked up his maiden Test wicket as the Proteas laboured to 102-4.

South Africa captain Temba Bavuma was his victim, caught off bat and pad by Nic Maddinson for just one. Josh Hazlewood had already got the ball rolling, dismissing Ryan Rickelton and David Bedingham, with Pat Cummins adding Tristan Stubbs before the close on day four.

Aiden Markram will resume on 45 not out alongside Wiaan Mulder but the odds are stacked against the hosts salvaging the game on day five. Australia were without Steve Smith's brilliance at slip after he was hit on the helmet by Anrich Nortje and was subsequently replaced in the field pending further assessments.

Renshaw's second innings bore almost no relation to his first. The 190 came at a strike-rate of 47. The 82 came at 82, with seven fours and two sixes in it.

Then it took a freak moment to end it. The ball went through Keshav Maharaj's hands more than once and off his own head before it stayed put, by which time the bowler was flat on the pitch.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Renshaw was caught and bowled by Keshav Maharaj in bizarre fashion after the decision was reviewed

Renshaw was on for twin centuries when it happened. Instead he finished with 272 runs for the match, which is close to the most any Australian has made against South Africa.

Three more runs would have put him level with Phillip Hughes, who made twin tons on this ground in 2009. Nine more and he would have passed David Warner's pair of centuries in Cape Town in 2014. Bradman's 299 not out was 28 away.

Nobody else in the Australian order got past 48. Maddinson stopped there, Marnus Labuschagne on 37, Smith on 27 and Alex Carey on 24.

Captain Cummins hurries things along for Australia

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Australia captain Pat Cummins smashed three sixes from four balls

Australia resumed on 33-0 and never looked like batting for time. They were 174-4 at lunch and 280 in front, with Maddinson's 48 from 38 balls setting the rate.

Labuschagne then produced the day's statistical curiosity. He made 37 from 58 balls, exactly what he managed in the first innings, which is only the 12th known instance of a batter matching his runs and his balls faced in both innings of a men's Test.

But Smith's 27 was the innings Nortje will remember. The bouncer that hit him on the helmet arrived on the fourth ball he faced and Smith answered by taking 14 off one Nortje over.

Cricket Australia said he was being assessed for concussion and he will be monitored for 24 hours.

Cummins made the rest a formality. His 32 not out took just a dozen balls, with Simon Harmer conceding three of his four sixes inside one over. The declaration came shortly before tea on 314-6.

Markram the last line of resistance for hosts

South Africa were left 421 to win, which no side in Test history has managed.

West Indies' 418 against Australia in Antigua in 2003 is still the mark and the best at this ground is 336, chased by Australia in 1950.

Batting out the day is the realistic hope and the record there is thin. Just two sides in the last 13 years have lasted 140 overs to save a Test.

Rickelton pulled at a short one in the fourth over and Carey took the catch, two runs made with Hazlewood again the bowler who had him.

Markram and Bedingham put on 66 in 19.4 overs before Hazlewood pinned Bedingham in front for 46. He was 49 first time round, so twice in the match he got into the forties and no further.

Image: South Africa's Aiden Markram was 45no at stumps

Three wickets went down for 13 runs from there and South Africa were 86-4, scoring across the innings at 2.48 an over.

Markram has needed 115 balls for his 45 not out and he was dropped on the way, on 15, when the chance hit Carey on the elbow and ran away past slip.

Among players still active, only Kusal Mendis of Sri Lanka averages more than Markram's 45.56 in a fourth innings. His 136 won the World Test Championship final against these same opponents at Lord's.

He has been in this position at this ground before, too. He made 143 here in 2018 chasing 417 against Australia, 340 minutes of work that still ended in defeat.

He will be hoping that something miraculous can happen on Tuesday with Australia needing six wickets to win and South Africa still requiring 319 runs.

Sports.title: Suljovic apologises but faces probe over inciting jeers and alleged sexist comments
Sports.content:
Mensur Suljovic has been referred to the Darts Regulation Authority for his incitement of jeers against Ross Smith in their clash at the Swiss Darts Trophy; he has also been referred over his alleged sexist comments in an interview about the incident; the Austrian has issued an apology

Mensur Suljovic referred to darts regulator for inciting jeers against Ross Smith and alleged sexist comments as Austrian issues apology

Mensur Suljovic encouraged the crowd to boo Ross Smith as he stepped up to take his match-winning darts - before then winning the match himself (credit - PDC)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Mensur Suljovic's crowd incitement during his match against Ross Smith and his alleged sexist comments in his on-stage interview regarding the incident have been referred to the Darts Regulation Authority.

The Austrian encouraged the crowd to boo the Englishman during a last-leg decider in their third-round clash at the Swiss Darts Trophy on Sunday afternoon.

He was later asked about the incident in an on-stage interview and used an allegedly sexist comment to describe how Smith reacted.

Suljovic said: "Ross Smith is one of the best players in the world - what's the bloke complaining about? He's got to play his game; otherwise, he's welcome to go home.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Suljovic beat Joe Cullen in the second round of the World Championship and 'The Rockstar' was not happy with the Austrian

"Women, women - they're always complaining, sorry. Sorry, you don't do that. I fully accept him as one of the very best darts players.

"OK, I've been riling up the crowd a bit, just like in Germany - I need your support. I need you; without you, I can't achieve anything. Thank you, thank you very much!

"What's he complaining about? When I'm in England, everyone's against me; everywhere I go.

"And now, all of a sudden, he's complaining? He might as well just stay at home."

Suljovic apologises over incident

On Monday afternoon, Suljovic subsequently issued an apology.

"I would like to comment once again on my match against Ross Smith and the interview that followed," he said.

"The emotions got the better of me in that moment. I wanted to get the crowd behind me and, in doing so, I didn't properly realise that Ross was throwing for the match.

"Looking back, I understand that the timing was unfortunate and was perceived as unfair. I would like to apologise to Ross for that.

"Ross is, in my opinion, one of the best darts players in the world, and I have great respect for him and his achievements.

"My comment about women during the interview was also completely inappropriate. I should never have said something like that. I would like to sincerely apologise to all women for those remarks.

"Darts thrives on emotion, but fairness and respect are just as important. Yesterday, I let my emotions get the better of me.

"I'm sorry for that."

In a statement, the PDC confirmed "the matter on stage and interview has now been referred to the Darts Regulation Authority" and issued "no further comment".

The incident between Suljovic and Smith explained

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Suljovic responds to accusations of deliberately playing slowly against Cullen and reveals why the referee told him off

Suljovic and Smith were locked at 5-5 in their best-of-11-legs clash on Sunday afternoon, with Smith having two match darts at double 18 when Suljovic gestured to the crowd to increase the volume of boos, prompting the Englishman to miss the target and hand his opponent a chance to steal the match.

Suljovic then nailed double 10 with his final dart to complete the checkout and seal victory.

His antics had left Smith frustrated, with the Englishman later taking to X to share his thoughts following the defeat.

"I don't blame Mensur for me losing that game," Smith wrote. "I missed two match darts. Simple as that.

"Obviously, it's impossible for me to know what he's doing behind my back when I'm throwing apart from the crowd's response.

"Karma will come around."

Suljovic is no stranger to controversial incidents. The Austrian denied intentionally provoking Joe Cullen during a World Championship clash last December.

Cullen branded his opponent's pace of play as "cheating" and "not darts" after becoming frustrated by the length of time he was taking to retrieve his darts and celebrate, with referee Kirk Bevans even forced to intervene.

Webster: There is a time and place for it and it was 'poor form'

Sky Sports Darts' Mark Webster on the incident between Smith and Suljovic (speaking before the apology)...

"Obviously with regards to the weekend, it was poor form for Mensur Suljovic.

"I think every player can use the crowd to their advantage, but there's a time to do it, isn't there?

"It's not while the player's throwing, particularly not on match darts.

"Fair play to Ross, he came out and said he didn't even see it and it didn't put him off, he still should have won the game.

"Mensur kind of doubled down on it as well. Like I said, get the crowd involved, players do it, it's part of the game now, but not on match darts and geeing them up when he's on match darts.

"He has used tactics in the past, hasn't he, in terms of slowing players down.

"That's fine, it's not against the rules, but sort of egging on the crowd when Ross on match darts wasn't good.

"I'm sure the DRA will get involved now, it's not good sportsmanship, is it? Rightly so, he should get fined.

"As long as he recognises that he's done wrong, he hasn't at the minute, but when he recognises that he's done wrong, it's the timing of it, isn't it, that's the poorest.

"I'm sure he'll realise and a fine will come his way. He should learn from it and he should never do it again, not on match darts."

Sports.title: Saracens sack academy player involved in Stokes-Atkinson fracas after new incident
Sports.content:
Saracens have sacked Totoa Auvaa with immediate effect after an incident over the weekend - four months after the forward was involved in the nightclub altercation that preceded Ben Stokes' retirement from international cricket.

The 21-year-old Samoan, a member of the club's Senior Men's Academy, was involved in an incident in St Albans on Saturday night.

Saracens confirmed on Monday evening Auvaa had left the club following an internal investigation.

"Saracens can confirm that Totoa Auvaa, a member of the Senior Men's Academy, has left the club with immediate effect," a club statement said.

"Following an incident this weekend, the club has determined that his conduct falls short of the standards expected of everyone who represents Saracens, both on and off the pitch.

"We take our responsibilities to our supporters, young people and partners seriously and we remain committed to upholding the standards of our conduct expected across the club.

"We will not be making any further comment on this matter."

The club has not said what happened.

Image: Ben Stokes announced his retirement from international cricket earlier this year

Auvaa escaped punishment following the nightclub incident in June which led to cricketers Stokes and Gus Atkinson being dropped by England for the second Test against New Zealand.

Saracens called the events "regrettable" while describing themselves as "supportive" of the player.

Separate Saracens and England cricket nights out had converged on two pubs before Stokes, Atkinson and Auvaa ended up in the VIP area of the Rex Rooms nightclub in the early hours of Monday June 8.

The two players had broken a midnight curfew while celebrating a first Test win over New Zealand at Lord's and both were dropped for the second Test.

An England and Wales Cricket Board investigation cleared Stokes and Atkinson of violent conduct, finding they had been blameless victims of "unprovoked attacks".

Stokes and Atkinson were given formal written warnings for breaching their central contracts before returning for the third Test at Trent Bridge, where Stokes resigned the captaincy and announced his retirement from international cricket.

Atkinson has remained in the England set-up and has since been awarded another central contract.

Sports.title: World heavyweight title will be on the line for Fury vs AJ
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will fight for the WBA world heavyweight championship when they box on December 11, confirmed Frank Warren.

British rivals Fury and Joshua will meet in a long-awaited showdown at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff and now the WBA 'super' or primary title will be on the line.

It is a surprise move as the WBA already has a 'regular' titlist in Murat Gassiev who expected to be elevated to full champion after Oleksandr Usyk vacated the belt.

Both Fury and Joshua previously lost their world title belts to Usyk. Now they have the chance to reclaim a championship they have held in years gone by.

"That is the case at the moment. That's going to be on the line," Warren, who promotes Fury, told Sky Sports News.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' John Dennen spoke to Dana White about what we can expect from the Fury vs Joshua fight

"Whoever wins that, they've got a version of the belt and the objective, after Usyk vacated all the belts, is to find out who's the best, who's going to hold all the belts, who's going to be the No 1 heavyweight.

"I'm sure Usyk will be back in next year as well. It's going to be really, really exciting times."

Warren is staging the Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley rematch on Saturday for the WBO heavyweight title. He would like to put the Dubois-Wardley winner in with the Fury-Joshua victor next year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joshua has made the bold prediction he will knock out Fury in a round. Watch his previous explosive first-round KOs

"These guys are all looking to unify the titles and get involved in massive, massive fights in 2027. We made it at Queensberry [Promotions] our mantra to make these fights happen. We've got three of the four heavyweight champions on our roster and we're going to make unification fights next year," Warren said.

"And it would be really, really good for the winner of Tyson and AJ to be involved in that. There are some fabulous fights to be made and the heavyweight division as I keep telling everybody is on fire. You've got some fabulous fights.

"[Dubois-Wardley] will set some big stuff up for the new year."

Dubois welcomes Fury or AJ

WBO heavyweight champion Dubois told Sky Sports News: "If they feed me one of them [Fury or AJ], I'll fight them. Nice appetiser. I'm ready for whoever they throw at me after this.

"I'll gladly take on the winner of that. I will stake my claim and take on the world, the belts and everything else that comes along with it."

Sports.title: Four Super League clubs show support for NRL deal after Leigh criticism
Sports.content:
A vote on a partnership between the National Rugby League (NRL) and Super League is close; it is understood the NRL would want to increase Super League to 15 teams and add London Broncos into the competition for 2027

Leeds Rhinos, St Helens, Hull KR, Hull FC release statements in support of NRL investment after Leigh Leopards owner comes out against deal

NRL supremo Peter V'Landys would like to see London Broncos in Super League

Leeds Rhinos, St Helens, Hull KR and Hull FC have released statements in favour of the NRL's investment in Super League after Leigh Leopards owner Derek Beaumont came out against the deal on social media.

Talks have been ongoing for months regarding the Australian competition's potential future involvement in Super League to bring alignment between the top two rugby league competitions in the world.

As a requirement of the deal, it is understood the NRL would want London Broncos added to the top flight as the 15th team from the 2027 season onwards which has been a potential sticking point for some clubs, with Leigh Leopards owner Derek Beaumont taking to social media to say he is against the deal because of that particular point.

Beaumont said it is "just not right to put London in Super League".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On The Bench podcast, Kris Radlinski and Karl Fitzpatrick discuss the possibility of the NRL merging with the Super League

The Leigh owner's particular grievance is that London finished 16th in the gradings, outside of the automatic Super League spots.

Not only that, if they were to be added to Super League, he would want a similar process to take place to the one that saw Toulouse Olympique and York Knights elevated in 2026. Their applications went through an independent panel.

However, other clubs see the partnership as a "landmark" and "defining" moment for the sport.

A deadline for the deal to go through is reportedly at the end of this week at which clubs will vote on whether they want the partnership to take place.

Beaumont said on Sunday that he would vote against the deal. Since then, Leeds, St Helens and both Hull clubs have released statements to confirm they are in favour of the partnership, the two Hull teams releasing a symbolic joint statement in a show of solidarity between the city rivals.

Sports.title: Coventry land long-awaited home win as Mfuni seals rout of Newcastle
Sports.content:
If ever validation is needed for attack being the best form of defence, Frank Lampard can call this game up on Wyscout. Coventry climbed out of the relegation zone to the heady heights of 14th place after their second successive win showcased the benefits of their manager’s willingness to balance risk with reward.

Jack Rudoni’s early penalty underscored a sense of positivity that was enhanced by an even quicker goal at the start of the second half from Sidiki Cherif and not unduly dimmed by Sven Botman’s howitzer making it 2-1.

Late goals from the substitutes Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni allowed promoted Coventry to pull away from a Newcastle side who, after a strong start to the season, also lost their last away game at Leeds by this scoreline.

Newcastle could have gone fourth in the Premier League with victory but despite missing several chances they could not argue with the defeat. As their manager, Matthias Jaissle, said: “There were elements in both boxes where we need to step up and do better. Those fine margins can make all the difference.”

Even when Botman had reduced the deficit with 20 minutes remaining and Newcastle threatened to take charge, Coventry left two or three players up on the halfway line. It could be perceived as a bold and brave move and Lampard, who wants supporters to be entertained throughout this first season back in the elite since 2000/01, deserves credit. On other days they might come unstuck but here it was a case of he who dares wins.

Not that he was ready to take the plaudits. “It probably means I didn’t manage to scream well enough to tell one or two of them to get back,” the Coventry manager said. “But at times we do certainly leave one or two players up the pitch because I think it will occupy their defenders. And in this [kind of] game of transition, sometimes you can defend with eight players.”

View image in fullscreen Frank Lampard is delighted by Coventry’s win. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters

It was 25 years since John Hartson had last scored a home Premier League goal for Coventry. So there was a momentous feel to the occasion when Rudoni stepped up to take his penalty in the sixth minute.

After three weeks of international football had left Sky Blues fans longing for more following their victory at Nottingham Forest, the atmosphere went up another notch when Lukas Hornicek, hesitant when coming out to palm the ball away from Ephron Mason-Clark, brought Cherif down as they contested the loose ball.

Coventry, for all their summer signings, feel very united after 18 successful months under Lampard, culminating in their Championship triumph. This sense of community was underlined as Rudoni lifted his shirt to show the message “Get well soon Nan” after scoring his penalty.

Rudoni’s grandmother is in hospital after suffering a heart attack. “He’s such a great lad,” Lampard said. “I’ve been there for him. He’s so close with his family. So I’m pleased he could have that moment for them.”

Newcastle had plenty of space and ball just about every time they attacked. But the risk-and-reward strategy meant Coventry were dangerous in the extreme on the transition.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

They had Bobby Thomas to thank for denying Newcastle twice shortly before the interval. Firstly the centre-back headed off the line after Jacob Murphy turned Harvey Barnes’s superb cross past Carl Rushworth.

Then when Matias Fernandez-Pardo raced clear, rounded Rushworth and shot goalwards, Thomas had recovered sufficiently to clear. On his first Premier League start since signing from Fenerbahce for £21m in the summer, Cherif deputised for the suspended Taiwo Awoniyi.

The 19-year-old forward is evidently not the finished product but he has raw attributes from which Coventry can build. When Malick Thiaw headed out a long throw-in, Cherif swivelled to strike a crisp drive that swished through four pairs of plum-coloured stockings and beyond Hornicek’s grasping fingers.

View image in fullscreen Sidiki Cherif doubles Coventry’s lead with a rocket. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters

Then Cherif should have made the game safe. Botman miscued Brandon Thomas-Asante’s cross but unmarked from six yards out Cherif clunked his shot wide. That miss briefly appeared crucial as Botman was allowed to wander forwards unchallenged before belting a shot into the top corner of Rushworth’s goal.

Simms made it 3-1 in the 81st minute, however, after the excellent Thomas-Asante nicked the ball on the edge of the area for the striker to shoot home. There was still time for Thomas-Asante to fire against a post before victory was emphatically sealed when Mfuni twinkle-toed his way into the penalty area to strike in left-footed.

Sports.title: Winning is not enough for Manchester City to move on from this crisis | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring.

Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. But consider his assessment of Manchester City’s 3-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday.

“It was tough,” he said. “It was hard but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone. [It’s] important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about, and the thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That’s the only thing we can do.”

Strip away the context and he could be talking about an injury crisis, or perhaps the resignation of a manager or a suspension to a key player. The tropes are familiar: it was hard but we stuck together and so we prevailed. “You want to win games, it’s as simple as that,” he went on. “Perform well, play good football and win games. This was a mental battle, [it’s] never easy coming back from internationals.”

But of course this wasn’t really about coming back from internationals; that’s not what made this difficult for City. This was about the verdict of the independent panel looking into the charges brought against City, the fact that the club have been found guilty of the greatest act of sustained cheating in the history of English football. Nobody knows what’s coming next.

The gravity of the situation still seems to have not dawned on many in football. City, as is their right, continue to maintain their innocence and have appealed. The propaganda battle goes on. But this is no longer about whether the financial regulations were fair. If City had objected to the regulations they had every opportunity to raise objections and vote against them. They did not. They agreed to the regulations, and while everybody else played to them, they did not.

The excuse that they only spent what others did but that they operated under stricter controls because of a lack of historic success is not merely irrelevant but entirely bogus: in the nine years under investigation, City’s net spending on transfers, before taking into account wages, was over £1.2bn ($1.6bn), around 50% more than any other Premier League side. And for all their talk of being proud disruptors, of rebels taking on the “red cartel”, that spending transformed City into the most dominant side English football has ever known, with six league titles in seven years. They are, precisely, an argument for why spending controls are necessary.

None of that, of course, is Haaland’s fault. He is a footballer offered a very competitive salary to play alongside very good players for a very good manager for a club for which his father played. This is another of football’s absurdities: it’s always the manager and players who end up becoming the faces of the institution, being quizzed about things that have very little to do with them as the executives and directors responsible lurk away from public scrutiny.

“My message to the players since we were together three days ago, when they all came back from their national teams, has been quite clear,” Enzo Maresca said. “Guys, the noise will always be there so it’s about how we learn to deal with the noise and it’s our duty to make our noise. Our noise is to win games in the way we did today and to be happy.”

Which on the one hand is absurd: nobody knows whether the three points City claimed at Anfield will still be theirs by Christmas. Nobody knows what division they will be playing in next season. Nobody knows how bad the sanction could be. And this is not some unfortunate event that has befallen City; this is the direct consequence of the actions of their directors. But on the other, what else can players and managers do? How else can they respond to this situation other than by being professional and trying to win games, even if none of it ultimately means anything?

What this is emphatically not, though, is just another football crisis from which City can move on by winning football matches. This is a crisis unlike anything English football has ever known, and it is one with which football’s language is struggling to cope.

Sports.title: Carrick promises Manchester United will ‘come out fighting’ after sticky start
Sports.content:
Manchester United have endured their worst league start in 40 years but Michael Carrick insists he is “loving it”. United arrived in Madrid without Kobbie Mainoo and Luke Shaw, who both picked up knocks in the draw against Tottenham at the weekend, and with the coach admitting that his team are in “a spot”, but he vowed that they would “come out fighting”.

Despite collecting just six points in the Premier League so far, Carrick claimed he did not feel under pressure and backed his captain, Bruno Fernandes, who he revealed was still “carrying something”, to rediscover his form. As he talked about building, there was a reminder too of the fact that Arsenal, the champions, finished “seventh or eighth” in Mikel Arteta’s first two seasons.

“To do something good, to do something great, you have got to be able to do something difficult,” said Carrick, whose side take on Atlético Madrid at the Metropolitano Stadium in the second round of games in the Champions League league phase on Tuesday.

“We hoped for a lot more, we expected a lot more, and we are where we are,” Carrick added. “I was aware that, winning as many as we had [last season], it was going to get more challenging, stickier. I understand that when it is not going well there is a real clamour and a feeling that it’s a disaster, that it’s all wrong and that everything needs to be changed. I kind of get that, but that’s not our mindset and it’s certainly not mine. You have to deal with things and overcome them. That is what I did throughout my career. We have to accept reality but we are building and you can’t lose sight of the journey.”

On the pressure he is under, Carrick said: “It depends on how you define ‘pressure’. There is our own expectation: we know what we want, what we are capable of and that comes from us. I don’t look outside. I don’t feel the pressure from that at all.

“I’m pretty good at shutting off, to be honest; closing off and living a little bit in my bubble. And I think that’s what we do as a group. We look after each other, we all know what’s out there and it’s about managing it, controlling it and staying focused on what we can do. It is about us wanting to succeed, to win. That’s the drive. There is no negativity. It’s also fine lines sometimes. We are hugely confident and we have confidence in each other. I have the utmost confidence in the boys that we can win a lot of games.

“[That’s] because I know them, I know how much they care, I know how strong the group is. And, anyway, you’ve got no choice: that’s why we’re here. We’re here to test ourselves and that’s the opportunity that’s in front of us. If you haven’t got that little bit in you where maybe it’s a little bit crazy times but you actually love the challenge and really want to dig deep to find the answers, then this is not the place for you.”

View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick backed Bruno Fernandes to rediscover his form from last season. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

Despite the poor domestic start, which also included exiting the Carabao Cup against Brighton at Old Trafford, Carrick’s side did win their Champions League opener convincingly against Sabah last month.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“We need to do something about it now and accept the reality,” Carrick said. “I love this part of it: sometimes when it’s not quite going for you, you see who’s really there. You see within the group, the squad, the club, who’s really there and who wants to be there for the long term, [who] is really attached to it and [for whom it] really means something. The supporters are there: they know what they want, they’re desperate for it, and we’ve got to give them something. You have to embrace the challenge. I totally believe that we’ll work through it.”

Asked if he believed that Fernandes could recover his form, Carrick said: “I think it’s pretty obvious to say that he can, yeah. I mean, he’s a top player, Bruno. Sometimes things don’t quite go for you, but he’s done some incredible things for this football club and he will do the same in the future, there’s no doubt about that. I’ve seen that a lot was made of [his fitness]. He was carrying something.

“People don’t maybe realise it, but it happens a lot: players play with issues. I probably played 80% of the games with some sort of issue. It’s not ideal, but it’s manageable. Bruno was able to play the games; that’s the commitment he that he has. He’s pretty much over it. It’s not a major deal, he’s in good shape and he was really bright [in training] this morning, looking forward to the game.”

Sports.title: Ronaldo’s Asian Champions League match delayed by missile alert in Riyadh
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr had their Asian Champions League match delayed by an hour on Monday after the Saudi-led military coalition said it had intercepted a missile fired by the Houthis towards Riyadh.

Saudi Arabia has recently come under a series of attacks from the Iran-backed group, with strikes on oil facilities, tankers and transport hubs – including a string of lethal hits on Riyadh’s international airport.

There was a sparse crowd in the stands of Alawwal Park for the game against Uzbekistan’s Neftchi Fergana, which was scheduled for kick-off at 9.15pm local time.

The stadium announcer said the situation was safe, that the match would be played, and asked spectators to remain in their seats. However, the television channel broadcasting the match announced a one-hour delay.

Shortly before the sound of explosions was reported in Riyadh. At the same time, Riyadh residents received an alert on their phones stating: “The region is exposed to a hostile aerial threat. Please remain calm and stay at home or in a safe place, away from windows and doors, and continue to follow civil defence instructions.”

Subsequently the coalition announced the “interception and destruction” of a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis in a statement on X.

This incident did not seem to affect Ronaldo, who scored the 981st goal of his career just before half-time, as the Saudi Arabian champions secured a 3-1 win.

Sports.title: Hincapié and Zubimendi out after warm-down injuries but Arsenal get Saliba boost
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has admitted frustration after Piero Hincapié and Martín Zubimendi sustained ankle injuries during the warm-down after Arsenal’s win against Leeds on Saturday.

Both are due to have scans on Monday to determine the extent of the damage, although Arteta said they would miss the Champions League game at home to Lille on Tuesday and that Hincapié’s injury “looks a little bit more serious”.

“We had a training session planned after the game for the players,” the manager said. “They didn’t have enough minutes to get everybody in the right rhythm and in two very unfortunate actions, we lost two players.”

Arteta described it as “far from ideal” but dismissed suggestions he would change the post-match routine. “When they have to play, they have no rhythm, and when you ask them to play, they’re going to have no impact in the game,” he said. “That could happen at the Emirates; it never happened in the seven years I was here. It could happen the next day in the training session, and that has happened before, and hopefully it happens now and doesn’t happen again. What can you do? If I knew I had a crystal ball clear, I’d say: ‘Guys, go in the Jacuzzi, everybody, I’ll see you tomorrow.’”

Hincapié and Zubimendi were expected to feature against Lille having not started in the Premier League this season. Arteta seemed disappointed with Illan Meslier and his staff after the reserve goalkeeper gave Hincapié a piggyback off the pitch rather than waiting for a stretcher.

“That’s something else not to discuss here,” he said. “Today they’re going to have a further scan and probably tomorrow we’ll know more and then we’ll see how they’re going to go. Piero’s one looks a little bit more serious, I think, but we’ll have to wait and see.”

There was better news for Arsenal as William Saliba has resumed training on his own as he recovers from a back injury sustained at the World Cup. Arteta would not be drawn on when the France defender could be back and is determined not to rush his recovery. “We’re still talking about weeks,” he said.

Gabriel Magalhães is likely to be partnered by Ezri Konsa again against the Brazil defender’s former club on Tuesday. Gabriel insisted he would not hesitate to take another penalty in a shootout despite missing the crucial spot-kick in the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain. “I was sad, and I didn’t want to miss a penalty, but I have learned from this and if I have another opportunity, I will be ready to take it,” he said.
