Arteta has challenged Bukayo Saka to score more goals after the forward found the net five times in his past four England appearances and revealed that they had been working on rotating him into more central areas to finish moves.

“He has been getting in great positions, getting shots, getting one-touch finishes and tap-ins,” he said. “That is the kind of unpredictability we have with that player, otherwise we know how the opponent is going to defend him. He is doing well. He could have had another four or five goals by now, easily. But if he continues like that, we know. When he talks about scoring a certain amount of goals, he … He needs to be thinking about scoring a certain amount of goals per game. If that shifts, that mentality, he will get into those positions and score more goals.”

Sports.title: Football regulator to recommend cost controls in landmark report with 94% of clubs making loss
Sports.content:
The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) is to recommend clubs introduce greater cost controls in its long-awaited State of the Game report, to be published on Tuesday.

The 250-page draft report, with a final version to follow in the spring after an eight-week public consultation beginning this week, will paint a damning picture of the financial state of English men’s football, including the stark finding that 94% of the top 116 clubs are loss-making.

The report will include a series of recommendations for the regulator and clubs to improve sustainability, with the IFR chair, David Kogan, and chief executive, Richard Monks, to provide more details at a press ­conference in Manchester on Tuesday.

That event is likely to be dominated by questions about whether the regulator could force the sale of Manchester City if the mass guilty verdicts of an independent commission are upheld on appeal.

As administrators of an enhanced owners, directors and senior executives test the IFR has powers to assess the suitability of owners and executives “where there is clear evidence of wrongdoing by individuals”.

The State of the Game report sprung out of the Football Governance Act, which created the IFR, which has taken almost 18 months to produce the most detailed study ever of the football industry and its finances.

EFL clubs have been waiting for the report in the hope that it will give them greater impetus as they continue to negotiate with the Premier League over a new financial ­settlement, although it may not ­necessarily do so given details that may emerge of extravagant and unsustainable spending by many lower-division clubs.

The Premier League has offered a new deal to the EFL worth £180m a year over 10 years, a significant increase from the current £150m figure, but the EFL wants £207m a year and the option to renegotiate after five years.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The EFL has also proposed the creation of a new so-called “lifeboat fund” for clubs in financial distress.

The IFR has powers to impose a settlement on the leagues if they cannot agree themselves. Both sides are likely to seize on elements of the report to bolster their arguments.

Sports.title: Grounded: Rayo Vallecano’s paper planes bring club’s crisis into the open
Sports.content:
It took 147 days for Rayo Vallecano to walk out for a competitive game on the Avenida de Albufera and 24 minutes and 56 seconds for them to walk off again. Half of those had been spent watching thousands of paper planes touch down on the turf, play suspended while a message was delivered, over and over, until it was impossible to avoid. Forced from their home, the team from the barrio had been away for five months. On the bright Saturday afternoon that they came back, there were just 13 minutes of football, a fans’ protest instead forcing the abandonment of their match with Athletic Club, the latest episode in a never-ending story.

The last time there had been a league game here was a victory over Villarreal in May. A lot has happened since: little Rayo, Rayo Vallecano, had played a European final, 11,000 fans heading to Leipzig where, as the banner perfectly put it, they knew no greater victory than being with you in defeat. Iñigo Pérez, the manager who took them there, had departed. And Óscar Trejo, the man who gave up the armband over treatment of staff – the best thing he could do as captain was to stop being captain – had retired and been immortalised the way the barrio does best: in graffiti four storeys high. Then, in late July, the Madrid government suspended the agreement that allows them to use the ground in return for €81,784 (£69,094) a year.

The cup, the coach and the captain were not coming back. As a new season began, nor were any of them. Rayo’s president, Raúl Martín Presa, said he was furious with the council, locking the gates to keep their technicians out and accusing them of condemning the club to segunda. But when the report described the ground as unsafe and unhealthy, Rayo’s fans knew they were right: they had been saying so for years, relieved to be finally heard. The ground’s upkeep was the tenants’ responsibility but – like so much else – it had been abandoned, left to ruin. They were furious with the president they believe condemns them to a fate far worse that relegation, a man they could not despise more and who despises them back, of whom they ask just one thing, as often as they can: for him to leave.

View image in fullscreen Talk of the town: Raúl Martín Presa (centre) was all smiles despite the protests against him. Photograph: Europa Press Sports/Europa Press/Getty Images

They are not alone. Last season players had complained about conditions, forced to train at Getafe and play at Leganés; as the new season began they would have to do so again. After a long summer and three home games played 20km south, where 4,280, 4,529, and 3,742 came to see Alavés, Racing and Espanyol, respectively – collectively fewer than in a single afternoon in Vallecas – they were finally back. Leganés had been left three-quarters empty, boycotted by supporters, but in football terms it had been good to them, which sums Rayo up: all wrong but somehow all right. Last season’s victory over Atlético there was followed up by two wins and a draw this season. Yet this is home. Besides, down at Rayo, in the heart of the self-styled independent republic of Vallekas, the football is the least of it, striker Sergio Camello says; it’s about what they stand for. And this weekend they were going to make another stand.

They could not have chosen a better opponent: Athletic’s fans are allies, supporters packed into the bars around the ground and the plaza in front of the Mercado de Numancia alongside Rayo’s fans, singing in the sunshine. The protest had been planned from the start; what they probably did not plan for was the way it ended. On surfaces all around the stadium, green stickers proclaimed “SOS Rayo Vallecano”. Presa’s image appeared on walls and scarves with familiar Mickey Mouse ears. From bags they handed out little plastic balls in many colours. And from boxes they handed out flyers.

View image in fullscreen ‘It is the day to protest. It is the day to single out Presa.’ One of hundreds of protest flyers that eventually became a paper plane. Photograph: MARISCAL/EPA

Printed on grey A4, the sheets declared: “Today is a day to protest.” After “years of putting up with this”, they had reached a “point of no return”. And so, in the 13th minute, everyone was invited to chant “Presa, go now!” Then to turn the paper into a plane and fly it on to the field. On the back of the sheet were handy, Ikea-style instructions for those who did not know how to fold a paper plane.

An Athletic corner arrived with perfect timing, setting it all up. The whistles started bang on the 13th minute and so did the planes, swooping in from all three stands. The referee, José María Sánchez Martínez, stopped the game and shrugged, which he did a lot. Small, multicoloured plastic balls came down too, bouncing and rolling across the pitch, while a banner unfurled in the main stand declared the ball in Presa’s court (which is precisely their problem). An announcement was made, a first warning, two more strikes and they were out. For now, they would play on but not until the pitch was clear.

Ballboys dashed across, applauded all the way, to do what ballboys do: pick up the balls. Planes were pushed off the pitch. Players kicked about among themselves. And, after a pause of eight minutes and 43 seconds, Sánchez Martínez, satisfied now, sent them back over to take the corner, Pathé Ciss congratulating a ballboy on a job well done as he returned to his position. The corner came in, Yuri Berchiche volleyed just wide, shot flashing past the post, and then the planes came down again. Two touches, strike two. This time, the referee took them off. The stadium clock had rolled on but now it was reset as they headed down the tunnel to chants of “Presa, go now!”

They had been out there 24 minutes and 56 seconds but it might as well have been half-time. In the shadows of the narrow corridor under the stand, conversations unfolded. In the sunshine, so did the tinfoil, supporters happily eating the sandwiches meant for the break. Half an hour after kick-off, there was an announcement: they would begin again in 20 minutes. And if more objects are thrown, the match would be abandoned. From the tunnel, Isi Palazón and Óscar Valentín came out to speak to fans behind the goal. This was bad: if it happens again, the game is over. This was good, a plan forming: if it happens again, the game is over. A clear protocol, postponement easily forced, a statement made more visible, more powerful than ever before.

View image in fullscreen Rayo supporters protest with a banner that reads ‘Presa, go now’. Photograph: Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images

Thirty-eight minutes and 16 seconds after kick-off, the players reappeared, Athletic first. Sánchez Martínez bounced the ball, said it is flat, swapped it over, and gave it to Emil Audero, whose goal-kick would be the new kick-off, 43 minutes since the first time. From behind him, someone started a countdown: five, four, three … As the ball flew into the air, so did more paper planes. Sánchez Martínez shrugged, looked at the end, a hint of defiance. Leaning against his post at the other end, Unai Simón watched it all happen.

Sánchez Martínez called over the captains, then the coaches. A circle formed on the pitch: the referee, his assistant, two captains, two managers, a delegate, La Liga’s match director, the security adviser and a police officer. The Rayo coach, Beñat San José, translated for Edin Terzic, whispering in his ear. Terzic nodded. Álvaro García argued, but there was nothing he could do. The referee’s hands were tied, the police wanted to go, and at nine minutes to three, 49 minutes and 18 seconds after the game started, he signalled towards the tunnel. They had played 13 minutes.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Rayo’s players departed, Ivan Balliu first, to applause. The referee stood, hands on his hips, a disapproving parent who had sent the kids to their room. Athletic’s players went to their fans in the far corner, then back towards Rayo’s supporters, who chanted: “Athletic! Athletic!” Iñaki Williams and Simón were the last off. They stopped for photos with the ballboys. Williams gave someone his shirt, Simón handed over his gloves. As they reached the tunnel, Williams signed someone’s shirt. As they disappeared, the stadium launched into the Vida Pirata, usually a victory song.

View image in fullscreen Athletic players wait on the pitch (left) as the referee makes the decision to abandon the match (right). Photograph: Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images

They may not have won, may never win, but many wonder what they had left to lose. They were not planning to get it postponed, an opportunity opening instead, but they might next time. Presa says he will never leave, even if they fall to the third tier, but what if they do it again and again? At what point does someone step in? The club attack the “ultras” – that old get-out clause – and call the rest of the ground “victims”, but that is not how the rest of the ground sees it, flying their paper planes and happily heading off into the afternoon. Even Athletic’s supporters, their big day out brought to an early end, were on side. They joined Rayo fans in the bars while down in the offices, there were negotiations over when to replay the game, probably behind closed doors: Athletic wanted to return the following morning but that was rejected and so at 4.23pm on Saturday their bus pulled out for Barajas, applauded up Payaso Fofo street and right on to Avenida Albufera, still none the wiser.

Thank you for your feedback.

Rayo’s supporters’ association called this “the inevitable consequence of exhaustion, frustration and anger” after “15 years of abandonment of the facilities, chaotic management, a loss of identity and a continuous contempt for employees and fans, as well as the club and its values”. They called Presa “dictatorial”; the protest, by contrast, “peaceful and democratic, necessary”.

“An unsustainable situation has reached its limit,” the captain Valentín posts. “This has got worse and worse bit by bit for too long without anyone doing anything to stop it getting this far. We have to listen to and understand the fans’ discontent. We need to find a way to bring everyone together for the common good and the good of Rayo Vallecano above all. That’s the only way we will ever live great moments together again.”

Sports.title: Daniel Maldini finds his feet at Cagliari after years in family’s Serie A shadow
Sports.content:
The abundance could not last for ever. Serie A’s first goalless draw of this season arrived in its 54th match, ironically between two of its more prolific teams. Perhaps things might have ended differently between Como and Roma if the division’s leading scorer, Donyell Malen, had not earned a red card at the start of the second half.

A missed opportunity for both sides? Roma started brighter and hit the post through Lorenzo Pellegrini. Como dominated absolutely after the red card, with 80% of possession, but could not make pressure count.

In the end, it was a result each team could live with. Returning from this season’s first international break, Como and Roma remain the most likely contenders to challenge Inter. But a couple of more surprising teams are making their presence felt near the top of the table. Lazio’s 3-1 win over Monza on Sunday kept them level with the Nerazzurri in first place. An astonishing feat at a time when their fans won’t even come to home games.

And then there is Cagliari. The Sardinians have finished in the upper half of Serie A only once in the last 30 years. Champions of Italy in 1970, they have scarcely made it into another title conversation since. But they began this season with four wins from five matches, their best start to a top-flight campaign for more than half a century.

Should we have seen this coming? Cagliari ended last season strongly. The first signs of a project coming together under Fabio Pisacane, a popular former player who returned as assistant coach in 2022 and then worked with the academy for two years before leading the first team in 2025.

An extraordinary individual, who earned the Guardian’s first-ever Player of the Year award in 2016, Pisacane lived with Guillain-Barré syndrome as a teenager, becoming paralysed and spending 20 days in a coma, but recovered and ascended Italian football’s lower divisions to make his Serie A debut at 30. Along the way, he made headlines for reporting an attempt by a Ravenna director to bribe him to throw a match in the third tier. None of which necessarily meant he would succeed as a manager. Pisacane has shown himself to be a canny tactician

View image in fullscreen Fabio Pisacane has risen from the ranks and shown himself to be an adept tactician. Photograph: Gianluca Zuddas/LaPresse/AP

“I’ve worked with many great coaches in my career,” said the Cagliari midfielder Harry Winks in a recent interview. “Coach Pisacane is certainly at the very top level … Since I arrived here, he has already improved everyone, myself included. I really enjoy working with him; I think he can reach the very top of the sport.”

OK, pause. Readers less acquainted with Cagliari’s story might need a moment to process that the person speaking is indeed Harry Winks, the former England international, previously of Tottenham and Leicester. Now 30 years old and enjoying his life and his football on the beautiful island of Sardinia.

If I mention now that he has been playing with Yerry Mina at Cagliari, you might get the image of a team of Premier League castoffs, chucked together for one last sun-soaked hurrah. That would be the wrong impression. Most of Cagliari’s regulars are 25 and younger, including the pair who combined to carve open Juventus’s defence on Sunday night.

View image in fullscreen Blast from the past: Yerry Mina and Harry Winks (not pictured) may be at Cagliari but the team is far from just a place for players to wind down their careers. Photograph: Gianluca Zuddas/LaPresse/Shutterstock

There was not much more than 15 minutes gone when Daniel Maldini cut in from the left. His initial shot from the corner of the box looked optimistic but it pinged back on to him from a defender and then to his teammate Paul Mendy, who held off a marker brilliantly and returned the ball to Maldini for a close-range finish. A fourth consecutive Serie A game with a goal for the forward, and an excellent way to celebrate his 25th birthday.

To say that these have been a rollercoaster few weeks would be some understatement. Maldini had his driving licence confiscated last month after crashing his car and failing a breathalyser test in an incident that was reported to have left five people with minor injuries. Subsequent hospital tests for narcotics returned negative, and he was called up to the first Italy squad since Roberto Mancini’s reappointment as national team manager.

Maldini’s individual performances for the Azzurri were a mixed bag, but he lined up with his Cagliari teammate Alessandro Romano for the 3-1 home win over Turkey. It was the first time in more than half a century – since 1972 – that two of the club’s players have started a competitive game together for Italy.

In both cases, the opportunity was well earned. Maldini, son of the great Milan defender Paolo, has often been dismissed by his critics as “un raccomandato” – someone who owes their opportunities to knowing the right people. Or, in his case, being part of the right family. Not just a nepo baby but a nepo grandbaby, whose grandfather Cesare won a European Cup with Milan and whose dad repeated that feat five times more. Those are big shoes to fill. Daniel, who grew up in Milan’s academy and made his senior debut for them as long ago as 2020, never cut it at San Siro and has bounced since then from Spezia to Empoli, Monza, Atalanta and Lazio without ever finding his stride.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Quick Guide Serie A results Show Genoa 2-1 Fiorentina, Inter 3-0 Parma, Napoli 3-0 Frosinone, Como 0-0 Roma, Lazio 3-1 Monza, Lecce 1-2 Bologna, Sassuolo 1-1 Milan, Cagliari 1-1 Juventus Monday: Atalanta v Venezia (5.30pm BST), Torino v Udinese (7.45pm BST) Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

But Pisacane has been adamant from the start about the player’s potential, highlighting the way he connects lines of midfield and attack. The manager has not been shy about addressing shortcomings, too, stressing that Maldini needs to be more consistent in his application.

Plainly, he is not at the height of the previous two generations. Even the current scoring run has included a degree of fortune. Maldini’s goal against Udinese was facilitated by defending that Benny Hill could have considered a bit much. But there is a player in there, and Pisacane has been getting the best of him in a system that allows freedom to move between the wing and a more conventional No 10’s space.

It is a similar story all throughout the team of individuals thriving in roles that suit them. Winks’s unshowy work in front of the defence allows the 20-year-old Romano, more freedom to get up and down the pitch. The 19-year-old Mendy is growing in confidence as a target man.

And goalkeeper Elia Caprile has been magnificent. He helped Cagliari cling on to a point, after Juventus came to life in the second half. He had made saves from Edon Zhegrova already before Randal Kolo Muani equalised from Kerim Alajbegovic’s cross. Glanced across him at close range, there was little the keeper could have done on the goal. Moments later, Juventus hit the crossbar and Caprile held Nick Woltemade’s follow-up. There was then a brilliant stop from Muani’s point-blank volley, though the forward was in an offside position.

View image in fullscreen Elia Caprile is all smiles after winning player of the match for his efforts against Juventus. Photograph: Gianluca Zuddas/LaPresse/Shutterstock

The game ended 1-1, and Pisacane said Juventus deserved at least that much. He and Luciano Spalletti were both shown red cards after the final whistle for a post-game scuffle that was hard to parse. They clasped hands at first, but the Juventus manager was shouting angry words from the start and appeared to react to the way Pisacane put a hand on his elbow, though none of these gestures looked violent in any obvious way. Spalletti later said he had been praising Pisacane for his player’s cleverness at time-wasting. Pisacane, for his part, seemed bemused, overheard asking: “What did I do?”

It all looked like a storm in a teacup. But we might answer Pisacane’s question another way. What he has done is take Cagliari to six wins and a draw from their last eight matches, dating to last season. Only Roma have picked up more points in that stretch.

Sports.title: Emotional Cristiano Ronaldo makes heartfelt gesture after match delayed amid Saudi Arabia attacks
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo was visibly emotional ahead of Al Nassr's AFC Champions League Elite match which had its kick-off delayed.

The start of the match against Uzbek champions Neftchi Fergana was pushed back 20 minutes due to a security alert.



2 Cristiano Ronaldo scored as Al Nassr won their delayed clash with Neftchi after appearing an emotional figure pre-match Credit: AFP

The clash on Monday at Alawwal Park had been scheduled to begin at 9.15pm local time in the Saudi Arabian kick-off.

However, the alert caused the match to be delayed until the necessary safety protocols and inspections had been carried out.

Supporters were permitted to remain in their seats whilst they waited for the action to get underway.



Ronaldo's emotional gesture

Pre-match, Ronaldo was spotted kissing his shirt prior to the delayed kick-off against Neftchi.

The iconic forward kissed the swords and palm trees, representing the Saudi Arabian coat of arms, on his jersey.



He was also pictured holding the shirt up to his face to cover his eyes in an emotional moment, which seemingly saw him pay his respects to those who have lost their lives in recent missile attacks in the country.

Once the match was underway, the 41-year-old was on the scoresheet, as Ronaldo doubled Al Nassr's lead before half-time after Angelo Gabriel had opened the scoring.



Neftchi would pull one back after the interval before a red card saw the visitors reduced to 10 men.

They would later score an own goal as Al Nassr ran out 3-1 winners.

And after the match, Ronaldo made sure to celebrate Saudi Arabia again, waving and wearing the nation's flag on the pitch.

Saudi Arabia attacks

Al Nassr and Ronaldo's emotional win over Neftchi followed multiple attacks on airports in Saudi Arabia.

The Iran-backed Yemeni group Houthi carried out four attacks in as many days between Thursday and Sunday.



A total of 16 people have been killed and more than 300 injured as a result of the strikes.

Al Nassr released a statement on their social media channels as they shared their condolences with those who had been killed or injured.

The club wrote: "Our thoughts and prayers are with all the martyrs and the injured.

"May Allah have mercy on our martyrs and grant a swift recovery to the injured."



2 Ronaldo and Al Nassr returned to action following the attacks on Saudi Arabia and managed to win on an emotional night Credit: AFP

Al Nassr's victory marked their first win of this season's league phase after losing their opener to Al Ain last month.

Meanwhile, Ronaldo has now scored five goals in nine matches across all competitions this season.

Those include a strike against Al Diriyah on Friday, his first outing since being suspended by the Portuguese FA.



The five-time Ballon d'Or winner left the recent national team camp early amid a falling out with manager Jorge Jesus.

Sports.title: Man City players and fans should be respected – they are the wrong targets for the boo boys
Sports.content:
Man City players and fans should be respected – they are the wrong targets for the boo boys

Manchester City fans have been backed for their response to the club's guilty verdict on their return to action.

The travelling supporters, who were joyous throughout, were rewarded with a 3-0 victory away at Liverpool on Sunday.



4 Man City were targeted by boos and jeers against Liverpool but the fans and players ended up leaving the happiest on Sunday Credit: Getty

It came in City's first match since they were found guilty of all charges against them in their Financial Fair Play (FFP) case.

Whilst the club have since appealed against the ruling, their players were booed by the Anfield crowd as they came out to warm-up and throughout the entirety of the match.

Their fans were also targeted, who responded with jeers of their own as they displayed inflatable bananas in the away end.



Meanwhile, the players' wild celebrations as they romped to victory against Liverpool have also been called into question.

Man City celebrations defended

It has since been argued that they were being 'smug' by celebrating their win amid the ongoing scandal.



However, talkSPORT's Adrian Durham, Dean Ashton and Sam Matterface have defended the current players as well as the fans for their behaviour.

Discussing the claims on Kick Off, Durham admitted: "These City players, I think, should be respected.



"With what’s happened, those players could have downed tools, refused to play, demanded moves in January and let it affect them, but they didn’t.

"They showed that players and fans are the wrong targets for the boo boys, in my opinion. They’re going to all have to take the punishment, whatever it is, but what are they meant to do?"

City were first charged in February 2023 for alleged breaches of the Premier League's FFP rules between 2009 and 2018.

4 City made a winning return in their first match since the guilty verdict, beating Liverpool 3-0 in emphatic fashion at Anfield Credit: Getty



Ashton agreed, adding: "They’re trying to clear their name for something they haven’t done. They wouldn’t have been involved in it.

"You want to play football, play for the best you can, try and win trophies.

"So now, they’re going to get pelters from supporters, going up against that and almost justify why they’re allowed to play and celebrate.

"I expected nothing less than for them to celebrate at Anfield."

Goals from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki in the second half secured all three points against the 10-man Reds.



City are next in Premier League action at home to Ipswich Town on Saturday following a visit from Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday.

4 Visiting fans have been told they were right to adopt a siege mentality at Anfield Credit: Getty

Man City fans right to back team

Ashton and Durham's stance was echoed by Matterface, who said: "I don’t think you can blame the current crop of Man City players for the ills of the past if they fail to win their appeal.

"What you can’t do is go at other supporters for airing their frustrations. There isn’t any other vehicle for them to be able to do that.



"So they do that in the manner they believe to be the loudest, which is boo the players and opponents.

"They want to show their distaste for what’s happened. You also can’t blame the City fans, it’s nothing to do with them!"

Meanwhile, Durham continued: "What are they meant to do, say we want to lose?! It baffles me how people have responded to what the City fans did.

"It’s a galvanising thing, a siege mentality. They’ll stick together. Erling Haaland said stick together. Pep Guardiola said stick together. What are you going to do?!"



4 City are now three points clear at the top of the Premier League Credit: Getty

Ashton even admitted he feels sympathy for the City supporters, who saw their side win three Premier League titles during the period in which their FFP breaches took place.

Amid their appeal, the club have continued to protest their innocence, with Matterface exclaiming: "They’re being told that they’re innocent by their owners."

Durham then concluded: "And until that road is closed off, there’s nothing else the fans can do.



"I thought the Liverpool fans should have spent more time and energy on supporting their own team. The Liverpool players weren’t supported enough I don’t think."

Sports.title: Leicester takeover deadline extended with £200m asking price questioned
Sports.content:
Leicester City have extended the deadline for a takeover of the club to Friday, October 16, talkSPORT understands.

The Foxes had initially given prospective buyers until September 14 to complete a deal to buy the club.

3 Prospective buyers have until Friday to wrap up a deal to buy the Foxes after the initial deadline was extended by over a month Credit: Getty

However, an extension has been made due to interested parties seeking more time to conclude their purchase.

At least one American consortium are showing interest in buying Leicester.

Meanwhile, Scottish-Indian businessman Neil Lal claims to be in the race.

Lal has yet to enter the process of a takeover with the relevant stakeholders, though.

But Leicester's current asking price could still prove to be a stumbling block for any prospective buyer.

The owners' valuation of over £200million, plus inherited debt, is being viewed as steep by those who have enquired about a deal so far.

King Power's Leicester reign

King Power have owned the Foxes for 16 years after purchasing the club back in August 2010.

Chairman Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha has been in the role since 2018 after taking over from his late father, Vichai.

Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha bought the club from Milan Mandaric and remained chairman until his tragic death in a helicopter crash eight years later.

Under King Power's ownership, Leicester clinched promotion back to the Premier League in 2014 following a 10-year absence from the top-flight.

3 King Power and Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha are looking to sell Leicester, but prosepective buyers have doubts over his valuation Credit: Getty

The club went on to win the title two years later under Claudio Ranieri despite being 5000-1 outsiders.

Leicester also won the FA Cup for the first time in their history in 2021.

However, recent seasons have seen the club struggle on the pitch, suffering two relegations from the Premier League in three years.

Last term saw the Foxes drop into the third-tier for the first time in 17 years after a second-successive relegation at the end of last season.

Russell Martin's side currently sit 17th in League One after winning just two of their opening eight matches.

Their latest defeat to Peterborough United on Saturday has left the Leicester boss under mounting pressure.

3 Martin's side have made a slow start in League One this season Credit: Getty

Martin has been warned his days in charge are numbered following the 3-1 home loss.

The Foxes boss was appointed this summer on a three-year deal through to 2029.

Sports.title: Emmanuel Petit backs Arsene Wenger for FIFA President – but there could be one key issue
Sports.content:
Emmanuel Petit backs Arsene Wenger for FIFA President – but there could be one key issue

Arsene Wenger has been endorsed for the FIFA presidency by one of his former Arsenal players.

However, talkSPORT's Simon Jordan doubts he will win the upcoming election.



4 Wenger has been urged to challenge for the FIFA presidency in March with Infantino still running for election Credit: Getty

The 77th FIFA Congress will be held in Rabat, Morocco in March, with a presidential election also taking place at the summit.

Incumbent president Gianni Infantino is running for re-election despite losing the support of multiple national federations.

The FA is amongst those to have pulled their backing for Infantino following his failed FIFA Forward Enterprise plans to sell private equity in tournaments such as the World Cup.



Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega is the only other confirmed candidate.

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is also considering challenging Infantino in the election, though.



Wenger backed for FIFA presidency

Meanwhile, there have been calls for Wenger to enter the race, a suggestion which Emmanuel Petit supports.

Speaking on Monday's White & Jordan, his fellow Frenchman was asked about the clamour for his former Gunners boss to run for the FIFA presidency.



Petit explained: "When he was a manager, Arsene, I had a huge respect and we have a long relationship between us.

"But when he was a manager, I remember how many times he was fighting against UEFA or FIFA for any decisions and he was always protecting the club interest and the players.

"Now that he stopped and joined FIFA, maybe he’s playing a role actually. Keeping his head down and not making any noise, trying to walk step by step until the top.

4 Wenger has worked with FIFA since 2019 as chief of global football development Credit: Getty



"That’s probably his strategy because I was very surprised when he joined FIFA, but now he represents himself.

"He was so close to Infantino since he arrived at FIFA, that I’m quite surprised. Now, maybe I understand why he joined FIFA, for this moment.

"I think if you want to change something in football then you need to get on top of it, to get the power to change it.

"(Michel) Platini tried to do that and he was kicked off very easily. So I don’t know, but I’m very happy he’s putting his name on the next election because Infantino, the door is over there."



Wenger has worked with FIFA as their chief of global football development since 2019.

He took on the role after leaving Arsenal the previous year following a tenure which spanned almost 22 years.

4 Petit won a Premier League title under Wenger at Arsenal Credit: Getty

The 76-year-old has faced criticism at times, though, notably for his radical proposals which included moving the World Cup to two-year cycle.



Petit continued: "I think he has the knowledge of football, he’s intelligent as well, he knows how FIFA is running now, he knows everybody that’s important as well in this institution and I think he’s got some ideas.

"Not the ones he presented as soon as he came into FIFA, he wanted to get a World Cup every two seasons, but I think it’s probably a strategy from him to get into the top of it and to change things.

"I hope, but I’m not a kid, I’m not stupid, I’m not naive. I know that the system won’t change, but if Arsene can replace Infantino, he was a manager in football, Infantino knows nothing."

Jordan doubts Wenger will run

But Jordan is not convinced Wenger will put himself forward.

The former Crystal Palace chairman admitted: "As much as we might think that Wenger could potentially fulfil that role, I think it would destroy any influence they then had over the football side of the operation that he has supposedly been running for them.



4 Infantino is set to run for re-election in March at the 77th FIFA Congress Credit: Getty

"Which is developed with the next generation of footballers and the way that money is distributed around the federations.

"I don’t think Infantino is going anywhere anytime soon and if you haven’t done him in by now, I don’t think you’re going to do him in by February."

When asked by Petit if Wenger has a chance, he replied: "I don’t think he is going to put himself forward."



Candidates must submit their nominations for the election by November 18.

They must also have the support of at least five FIFA member nations.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi names Max Dowman, Arsenal target and Crystal Palace signing among 10 future stars
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has updated his list of football's 10 future stars with Arsenal's Max Dowman among two Premier League players named.

Shortly after his emotional farewell to international football, the 39-year-old has fittingly picked the youngsters who he believes will shape the game's next generation.

6 Messi bid farewell to the international scene shortly after netting his 126th and final goal for Argentina Credit: Getty

Messi has previously highlighted the likes of Trent Alexander-Arnold, Phil Foden, Jadon Sancho and Mason Mount as his top wonderkids.

Six years on from his original list, the Inter Miami superstar is now in his third iteration of naming the young stars he is tipping for the top.

Messi’s 10 future stars he believes are football's ‘next chapter’

Can Uzun

The Eintracht Frankfurt midfielder is one of the more senior names on Messi's list despite still only being at the tender age of 20.

The German-born 10-cap Turkey international has scored 19 goals and provided 12 assists in 65 Bundesliga matches thus far in his career.

Tomás Aranda

Messi has named just one of his compatriots in his new list, with Boca Juniors talent Aranda earning rave reviews back in Argentina.

The 19-year-old only made his professional debut in January but was handed his senior international debut five months later.

Aranda had registered one assist in six league games for his club since the World Cup before he fractured a fibula in his right leg.

6 Aranda is one of Argentina's brightest young talents and is said to be wanted by several Premier League giants Credit: Getty

Max Dowman

The future of Arsenal is fresh from receiving three Guinness World Record certificates as a reward for his historic debut season.

The teenager, who made his senior debut in August 2025, became the Premier League’s youngest ever goalscorer last year en route to helping the Gunners win their first top-flight title for 22 years.

Dowman, who was drafted into first-team training at age 14, has been tipped by Simon Jordan to become a world-beater like Lamine Yamal.

6 Dowman became the youngest ever Premier League winner in May Credit: Getty

The England Under-19 international, whose heroics last season have seen John Terry and Henry Winter already compare him to Messi and Kaka, has already made an imperious start to the new campaign.

The 16-year-old earned the Carabao Cup Player of the Round award following his two goals against Ipswich last month, which saw him join an exclusive club alongside Wayne Rooney.

Gilberto Mora

The 17-year-old Mexican, one of the breakout stars at Liga MX club Tijuana, has been strongly linked with both Arsenal and Liverpool.

The attacking midfielder underlined his status as his country's top talent by starting the 3-2 defeat against England at the Azteca in July.

In the round before, Mora became the youngest starter in a World Cup knockout tie after Pele, across the four appearances he made.

Since returning from the tournament, he has scored five goals and registered an assist in seven outings for his boyhood club.

6 Gilberto Mora made four appearances for Mexico at the World Cup - including against England - and recently scored his first senior international goal Credit: Getty

Zavier Gozo

The 19-year-old has been rewarded for making the step up to the Premier League with his first senior appearance for the US national team.

Crystal Palace signed the highly-rated American prospect from Real Salt Lake for a reported £11.1million in August.

Gozo, who made his MLS debut as a 16-year-old in October 2023, scored six goals in RSL's first 16 league games of the year.

He endured a baptism of fire on his Premier League bow by coming off the bench in the 4-1 defeat to Manchester City, and has also enjoyed a late cameo in the 3-2 loss to Ipswich Town last month.

6 Gozo made his senior United States debut in the 4-1 win over Peru last month and is trying to break into Crystal Palace's first team Credit: Getty

Jesús Rodríguez

The 20-year-old is hoping to go from strength to strength under Arsenal and Chelsea legend Cesc Fabregas at Como in Italy.

The two-cap Spain international started the club's first Serie A game of the season but has since had to make do with a substitute role.

Rodriguez is still waiting on his first goal contribution across four outings, and was even sent-off for Spain's Under-21s last month.

The ex-Real Betis talent, who scored twice and registered nine assists in 31 Serie A games last year, set up Mario Martin's goal for 12-0 against San Marino before he saw red a few minutes later.

Kees Smit

Earlier this year, Manchester United legend Rio Ferdinand told talkSPORT that he didn't want his old club to miss out on Smit.

The 20-year-old Netherlands midfielder had previously been named as one of the stars to watch in Europe at the start of last season.

talkSPORT even revealed that Newcastle and Crystal Palace were competing with Real Madrid to sign the AZ Alkmaar star.

However, no summer move to the Premier League transpired, and Smit has registered two assists in five Eredivisie matches this term.

6 Smit was a surprise omission from the Netherlands' World Cup squad after his impressive season Credit: Getty

Chloe Sarwie

Messi also named three future stars of women's football in his list, with Chelsea's Sarwie the headline selection for England fans.

The 17-year-old made seven senior appearances for Chelsea last season and was in the Lionesses squad for the Under-20 World Cup.

Giovanna Waksman

The Brazilian youth international only joined OL Lyonnes in March, having first come through the ranks at Botafogo in her homeland.

The 17-year-old is still waiting for her first senior appearance at club level this season but is in double digits for goals for Brazil's U17s.

Lotta Wrede

The 18-year-old has made three appearances in the Frauen-Bundesliga this season with her childhood Hamburg outfit.

The club's No.32 has also scored three times in nine appearances for Germany's Under-19s and has been linked with a move to Barcelona.

Sports.title: ‘It’s a pity’ – Emmanuel Petit explains Arsenal relationship as fans make complaints known
Sports.content:
Emmanuel Petit has voiced his disappointment over the growing disconnect between Arsenal and its supporters.

The Frenchman appeared on talkSPORT's White and Jordan to discuss all things Gunners, where he enjoyed a trophy-laden three-year stint between 1997 and 2000.

4 Petit made 118 appearances and scored 11 goals for Arsenal but now feels there is a disconnect building between the club and fans Credit: Getty

Petit became a club icon in north London as his all-action midfield displays helped deliver Premier League and FA Cup glory.

While the 56-year-old also enjoyed huge success at first club Monaco, as well as stints at Barcelona and London rivals Chelsea, he remains a popular figure at Arsenal.

However, the former midfielder believes his old team may be losing touch with their fanbase.

Premier League clubs have come in for increased criticism in recent years over rising ticket prices, with Arsenal no exception.

Ahead of the 2026/27 campaign, the Gunners announced a 3.9 per cent average increase on season tickets - the fifth year in a row that the Premier League champions have increased their prices.

And Petit admitted he has become aware of this himself after a recent interaction with an Arsenal supporters' group, as he bemoaned the transactional relationship between club and fans.

Petit: Times have changed at Arsenal

Appearing on talkSPORT, Petit shared his experience visiting the Arsenal Fans Association in Denmark, where he joined up with former teammate and fellow icon Freddie Ljungberg to greet supporters.

But the 1998 World Cup winner revealed fans were growing disillusioned with the club, before admitting there is a similar feeling among their former players.

Petit said: “They are saying the same thing - that they are not fans anymore, they are customers. And the relationship they had before with Arsenal, it's not the same anymore.

“I said, 'Don't be surprised, because as former players, it's kind of the same with us'.

4 Petit enjoyed a League and FA Cup double in the 1997/98 season with the Gunners Credit: Getty

4 Despite rising ticket prices, Arsenal's fans continues to pack their 60,000 capacity Emirates Stadium Credit: Getty

Explaining why he feels a lack of connection with Arsenal, Petit explained that the club have never approached him over an ambassadorial role, but insisted he will never ask for opportunities.

He continued: "There are a few exceptions, with former Arsenal players that link with Arsenal and they do events around the world.

“I'm not asking Arsenal to call me tomorrow for that. But I've never received anything. They never asked me to do anything for them.

“Every time I represent Arsenal, it's because of the company [his talent agency], but nothing from the club.

"So it was a pity for me to hear that, because the fans are so important. They regard themselves as customers."

Sharing his disappointment over the fans' disillusionment, Petit said he was 'embarrassed' by Arsenal for keeping them at arm's length.

4 Petit shared his disappointment over Arsenal's lack of relationship with its fans Credit: talkSPORT

The Frenchman said: “For me, they are the most important pieces in the football industry. If there are no fans, no customers, no money at all, they are buying for everything.

“And that's what I said to them. I'm very happy and honoured to be in Copenhagen because of you, because of what you're doing with us, former players, we still live through your memories. And it's amazing.

“But the fact that they were so disappointed with the club, I felt embarrassed."

Urging Arsenal to do better, he added: “I understand it's a business. I understand there are customers. But I think at the end, this is not a common industry. Football matters.

“It’s different than a normal company because of the fans. So you have to take care of your fans. You have to protect them. You have to build something alongside the fans.

“And this is not happening anymore.”

Sports.title: Alvaro Arbeloa under intense pressure as Fulham manager after just six Premier League games
Sports.content:
Alvaro Arbeloa under intense pressure as Fulham manager after just six Premier League games

Alvaro Arbeloa is under intense pressure to save his job as Fulham manager.

The Spaniard is in trouble after just three months in charge at Craven Cottage.

3 Arbeloa has collected just two points from six matches as Fulham boss Credit: Getty

Arbeloa is yet to win a Premier League match as Cottagers boss, picking up just two points from their opening six matches.

Saturday's humbling late defeat at Ipswich Town also saw his side sink to the bottom of the table.

Arbeloa under pressure

talkSPORT understands this coming weekend's home meeting with Hull City is now a must-win fixture, despite the Tigers' good form - losing just once in six.

The following week's trip to fellow strugglers Coventry City is also seen as crucial to Arbeloa's future.

It comes after the 43-year-old signed a three-year deal as Marco Silva's successor back in July.

Silva left the club to join Portuguese giants Benfica in the summer following five years in charge in west London.

The role marks Arbeloa's second in senior management after five months as Real Madrid boss last season.

Across 28 matches in all competitions, Arbeloa collected 18 wins with Los Blancos.

However, losses to Chelsea, Sunderland, Crystal Palace and now Ipswich have piled the pressure on Arbeloa in his new job.

Fulham's only wins under their current boss have so far been in this season's Carabao Cup.

3 Arbeloa faces a must-win clash with Hull this weekend Credit: Getty

Victories over AFC Wimbledon and West Ham United have set up a fourth round tie with Palace later this month.

Arbeloa on 'unlucky' Fulham

Speaking during his post-match press conference on Saturday, Arbeloa told reporters: "We were a little bit unlucky, but we need to improve.

"It doesn’t matter if you concede in the first minute or the last. As a coach, I don’t like to concede goals.

"When you give the ball away so easily, the opposition will attack you, and we must change our mentality when we score.

"I am so happy with many things that my team are doing, and I know it is not easy for them.

"The most important thing is Fulham’s position, and we need points. It’s a massive game for us at home next week, and we need to be ready."

3 Fulham conceded a 92nd minute winner against Ipswich last time out Credit: Getty

This season marks Fulham's fifth successive campaign in the Premier League.

Since promotion in 2022, they have not finished lower than 13th in the table.

Sports.title: Where to watch Atletico Madrid v Manchester United plus talkSPORT commentary for blockbuster
Sports.content:
Where to watch Atletico Madrid v Manchester United plus talkSPORT commentary for blockbuster

Manchester United will hope to put their Premier League woes behind them as they prepare to face Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

The Red Devils beat Sabah 4-0 upon their return to the continental competition last month, while Atletico started the league phase with a 2-1 defeat to Liverpool.



3 Shaw was involved in the situation which seen Bentancur's being sent off for Tottenham Credit: Getty

This is an important match for under-pressure United boss Michael Carrick.

Carrick's men were held to another draw against Tottenham on Saturday in the Premier League despite Spurs being down to ten men.

Diego Simeone's side, meanwhile, have had a strong start to their domestic season having won their last four matches.



The Red Devils have never beaten Atletico, with two of their last four meetings resulting in victory for the Spanish side.

The United boss has also been hit with a double injury blow as Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo missed Manchester United training on Monday.



Shaw started Saturday's clash at Old Trafford but was replaced in stoppage time by Ayden Heaven.

Mainoo, who withdrew from England duty during the break, played the full 90 minutes at the weekend.



Also missing from Monday's session was Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui as they recover from their respective injuries.

United training squad for Atletico Goalkeepers: Lammens, Heaton, Mee Defenders: Maguire, De Ligt, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Martinez, Yoro, Heaven Midfielders: Mount, J. Fletcher, Tielemans, Baleba, Santos, Fernandes Forwards: Lacey, Zirkzee, Mbeumo, Rashford, Cunha, Amad

3 Simeone's men will be playing an English side in the Champions League for a second time this season Credit: AFP

Where to watch Atletico v Manchester United

This European tie will kick-off at 8pm on Tuesday, October 13.

It is being played at the Spanish outfit's home stadium of the Metropolitano Stadium.

The last clash between Atletico and United in Madrid came in February 2022, with the two teams drawing 1-1.



talkSPORT will be providing live commentary with Adrian Durham, alongside Ian Danter and former England captain Stuart Pearce.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 



For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Additionally, fans in the UK can watch the match on Prime Video - with build-up starting from 6:30pm.

Prime Video signed a new contract that means they will broadcast the top-pick Tuesday match through to the 2030/31 season.

The matches will be available to Prime Video members at no additional cost.



3 Mainoo played the full match after resting over the international break Credit: Getty

Manchester United 'fresh start'

Following their draw with Spurs, Carrick said: "We definitely had a tough spell in the game early on. That’s pretty obvious.

"The positive is that we worked through that, and the second half was much better.

"There are certainly things we can improve, but there are fine lines within that as well. We’ve got to stay positive and keep doing the right things.



"We’ve got games coming up, and we’ve got to be ready for them and embrace the challenge. It’s a big challenge, a great challenge, and we’re more than capable of winning games.

"We've got big games coming up and are looking forward to Tuesday now [at Atletico].

"A fresh start, a fresh game and we will go there looking forward to the game."

Sports.title: Britain's star cyclist - one half of GB's golden couple - is SENT HOME from World Championships in China over 'misconduct'
Sports.content:
Team GB cyclist Matthew Richardson has been sent home from the World Track Cycling Championships in Shanghai over allegations of misconduct.

Richardson, 27, switched allegiance from Australia to Britain after the last Olympics and had been expected to secure three medals in China this week after declaring himself the fastest cyclist in history.

Now instead he is in the process of leaving the country.

In a statement sent to Daily Mail Sport, a British Cycling spokesperson said: 'British Cycling can confirm that Matt Richardson has been withdrawn from the Great Britain Cycling Team squad for the upcoming 2026 Tissot UCI Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai, China.'

When approached by Daily Mail Sport about the misconduct allegations which are believed to have prompted Richardson's withdrawal, the organisation added that they would not be commenting further at this stage.

The Times reported Richardson is subject to an investigation into his behaviour, particularly towards teammates.

The investigation is said to have been prompted by a complaint from another rider.

Matthew Richardson has been withdrawn from the World Track Cycling Championships

Richardson's partner is fellow British cyclist Emma Finucane, who is also out in China

One rider who spoke to the Times said Richardson would not moderate his behaviour even when engaging with athletes from minority backgrounds.

British Cycling added to the Times: ‘British Cycling takes any allegations of harassment, bullying or discrimination extremely seriously.

'Where concerns are raised, they are investigated thoroughly through our established procedures.

'Out of fairness to anyone involved in an investigation, we would not comment on any ongoing process.’

Richardson is one half of Britain's cycling golden couple. He is in a long-term relationship with Emma Finucane, the star of Great Britain's women's team.

Richardson and Finucane live together in Manchester and have been dating since February 2024 after 'knowing each other for a long time'.

Richardson had been due to be one of four members of the men's sprint squad at the World Championships.

He had been due to join Harry Ledingham-Horn, Ed Lowe and Joe Truman in the squad.

Richardson had claimed three medals at the European Championships in Konya, Turkey, earlier this year.

Richardson and Finucane have joked about being 'the world's fastest household' on the track

The 27-year-old won gold in both the men's sprint and keirin events, as well as claiming silver in the team sprint with Truman and Hamish Turnbull.

Richardson had been due to make his comeback after he was injured during the Keirin World Series in July.

Last week, Richardson said he is 'lucky' to be walking after being wiped out by a rival in an incident, which ruled him out of the Commonwealth Games three months ago.

Richardson had been slammed off the track by Japanese cyclist Kento Suzuki while competing in the event July, leaving the velodrome in an ambulance.

The sprinter said he has not received an apology from Suzuki over the incident.

Richardson poses in a Union Jack flag after switching allegiance from Australia

Richardson's hopes of competing at the Commonwealth Games were ended in Japan

Join the discussion Should sports teams act faster on misconduct allegations, or risk damaging trust among athletes and fans?

He was favourite to win gold in Glasgow but never got to take part after the horrifying crash. He was unable to walk for four days after coming away with a broken scapula and a heavily bruised hip.

Richardson had been hoping to defend the title he won when competing for Australia in 2022, before he switched nationality to represent Britain, which he claimed was like 'Hogwarts' compared to 'High School'.

The Australian defector, who was born in the English town of Maidstone but moved to Perth at nine and went on to carve out a brilliant track career for Australia, caused a sensation by switching allegiance straight after winning two silvers and a bronze at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

He received a life ban for competing for Australia, but despite early bitter criticism back in the country that honed his cycling talent, he's since carved out a strikingly impressive career in GB and England skinsuits.

Sports.title: Paul Pogba in limbo: How the World Cup winner is still mulling his next move after his shock Monaco exit - as the ex-Man United star calls for Man City to hand over TWO Premier League titles
Sports.content:
Paul Pogba in limbo: How the World Cup winner is still mulling his next move after his shock Monaco exit - as the ex-Man United star calls for Man City to hand over TWO Premier League titles

Paul Pogba is strolling down the pit wall at Marina Bay Street Circuit in Singapore. Journalists begin to circle, and soon enough, the subject of Manchester City’s guilty verdict arises.

The Frenchman smirks, raises his hand, and responds: ‘I have nothing to say, to be honest.’

But Pogba does have something to say. Four years may have passed since the 33-year-old was last competing with the Cityzens for their biggest rivals, Manchester United, but the midfielder still has a vested interest in the outcome of their appeal against the club's conviction on 114 Premier League charges.

‘I just hope it doesn't affect the Premier League,’ Pogba continues. ‘Hopefully we can get two titles back.’

Pogba was once the main man at United, a key cog in two teams that went toe-to-toe with City at their very peak. But he came out on the wrong side of the fight to the juggernaut on both occasions, with the Red Devils coming second to their rivals in both the 2017-18 and 2020-21 campaigns.

Only the first of those near-misses came during the period in which City were found to have used 'sham' contracts and agreements to cook their books by around £900million. So whatever punishment does come City’s way, if there is one, Pogba can most likely only dream of one Premier League crown.

Paul Pogba spoke on the Man City guilty verdict while at Singapore Grand Prix on Sunday

These days the one-time World Cup winner isn’t competing for titles, though. He is a free agent, and has been since his Monaco contract was terminated in the summer, following an injury-ravaged spell in the principality.

Instead of strutting his stuff on the pitch, he now lives the glamorous life of an attendee of Formula One Grands Prix – as he was in Singapore on Sunday when asked about City – and fashion shows in the most stylish city in the world.

Pogba’s appearance in the Asian city-state was courtesy of his long-term sponsor Adidas, who he has been partnered with for over a decade, and followed on from his presence with wife Zulay at The Business of Fashion 500 Gala in Paris last week.

The former France international has long loved the world of fashion, constantly showcasing bold clothing choices away from his sporting career – some cool, and some questionable – and he even has his own apparel brand.

POGBA MDXCIII – 1593 in Roman numerals, which could refer to his birthdate of March 15, 1993 – was launched in October last year and is designed in Miami, with 'the finest artisans and manufacturers', and aims to 'redefine the codes of luxury sport, blending excellence, authenticity, and emotion'.

BOF 500 was part of the famous Paris Fashion Week, the most prestigious cohort of shows in the world of fashion – part of the ‘Big Four’ alongside Milan, London and New York – and Pogba rocked up sporting a sleek tuxedo, arm in arm with Zulay. He looked a million dollars and the smile on his face suggested he felt the same way.

Pogba is living a truly lavish life of extravagance, and if he were to step away from football altogether, he wouldn’t be short of avenues to go down. That said, he has not let it be known that he has plans to hang up his boots.

The midfielder, who was once deemed one of the best in the world, was trying to revive his career when he signed for Monaco on an initial two-year deal. He broke down once the move was confirmed, with this his first step toward redemption after serving an 18-month doping ban.

Pogba (pictured scoring against Man City in 2018) was part of a Man United team who twice finished second to rivals City

Pogba is without a club after having his Monaco contract terminated during the summer

His first game for the club came a mammoth 808 days after he last laced up his boots for his previous club, Juventus. That was due to a four-year suspension he was initially handed while at the Italian club after testing positive for the prohibited substance DHEA – a ban which sent one of football's biggest names into the wilderness.

Pogba had admitted to Juventus that he took some nutritional supplements, supposedly supplied to him by a Miami-based doctor, but was totally unaware that they contained testosterone, which led to his ban.

In the year that followed, the former Man United and Juventus star kept a low profile. That was until October 2024, when his ban was slashed to 18 months. From the darkness, Pogba could then see the light.

The reduction meant Pogba was free to return to professional football, and he did so with Monaco. But after only featuring in six games during one season at the club, while earning £44,000 a week, his contract was cut short.

After everything he has been through, he is back to square one.

A career in Europe doesn’t seem to be on the cards for Pogba, nor does a venture to Saudi Arabia. However, the MLS appears to be the most likely destination at the time of writing. Daily Mail Sport understands Pogba was offered to clubs within the league back in August.

Interest from across the pond isn’t new; Pogba previously held talks with DC United, while David Beckham’s Inter Miami – home to Lionel Messi – have also been linked to the midfielder in the past.

There have also been rumours about a new life in the Big Apple, with Pogba linked with a move to New York City FC, where Frank Lampard went to retire following his 13-year trophy-laden stint at Chelsea. Nevertheless, Pogba has yet to have had any concrete talks with a new suitor.

The 33-year-old was last week spotted at aParis Fashion Week event with wife Zulay

Pogba has launched a new clothing brand last year and has long held an interest in the world of fashion

Meanwhile, as the rumour mill continues to spin, Pogba, who enjoyed two spells at United and made over 230 appearances for the club – scoring 39 times and providing 51 assists – is making sure to help those who trod the same steps he once took in Manchester.

Summer signing Carlos Baleba, who made his debut during the disappointing 1-1 draw with Tottenham at Old Trafford on Saturday night, recently revealed that Pogba was the first to congratulate him on his £70million switch from Brighton.

‘It was Paul Pogba,’ Baleba said when questioned on who first texted him after the move. ‘He said Manchester is a big club, a great city and he really enjoyed it here.’

If Baleba can produce similar moments of magic to what Pogba did in a Red Devils shirt, he will do more than just endear himself to the fans. The Frenchman will also want to rediscover that form when he eventually returns to the turf, to help rebuild a career that once threatened to flourish into one of the greatest we have seen but didn’t.

Sports.title: Matthias Jaissle hits out at Newcastle's lack of 'desire and hunger to score' after humbling at Coventry
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle hits out at Newcastle's lack of 'desire and hunger to score' after humbling at Coventry

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle has hit out at his side's lack of 'desire and hunger to score' after they suffered a demoralising 4-1 away defeat at Coventry.

The Magpies slipped to 11th in the Premier League table as they suffered their second defeat of the season, with Frank Lampard's side picking up their second win in as many games.

While the away side struggled defensively, they also came up short in attacking areas, with centre back Sven Botman the only away player on target with an impressive long-range effort.

Summer signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo missed a golden opportunity in the first-half at 1-0, and Jaissle has admitted he needs to address his forward players.

'We're frustrated definitely,' he said on Sky Sports after the game. 'The lads (are) as well in the dressing room, it's a feeling you don't want to have when you feel as though you should have won.

'We can only apologise to the fans that took the journey. We need to analyse it clearly, especially in the box, at both ends. The desire and hunger to score, to finish the attacks, that was missing.

Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle has admitted his team lacked 'the desire to score' in their defeat by Coventry

Matias Fernandez-Pardo missed a golden opportunity to level the score when it was 1-0

'There's something we need to look at for sure. We need to win these games in the boxes. Defensively we need to improve. On the offensive we need to be more sharp.'

Coventry hadn't scored in the league until their last match, but managed four on Monday evening.

The deadlock was broken when Jack Rudoni netted from the penalty spot, after goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek had brought down Sidiki Cherif in the box.

Cherif himself then made it 2-0, and Coventry added two more late on.

'It's something that can happen in football, especially when you're managing a young squad, but there can still be a possibility to go on and win that match,' Jaissle added of the penalty. 'The second goal there was a foul on Joe Willock but it wasn't whistled, in my eyes, he was then missing in that spot where the ball dropped after the throw in.

On the timing of Cherif's goal, he said: 'It's never nice to concede a goal but we had the approach after half-time to come out and turn it around.

'The lads believed so we made the first goal and momentum was on our side. That's something also we need to learn that in a risk zone you cannot lose the ball. You cannot invite the opposition to score the third one, then it's going to be difficult.'

Sports.title: 'I see you more than my missus!': Erling Haaland's hilarious reaction to cameraman after leading Man City to a perfect Premier League start at Liverpool - despite guilty verdict hanging over them
Sports.content:
'I see you more than my missus!': Erling Haaland's hilarious reaction to cameraman after leading Man City to a perfect Premier League start at Liverpool - despite guilty verdict hanging over them

Erling Haaland was in high spirits after helping guide Manchester City to a 3-0 thrashing of Liverpool, joking with the cameraman during the post-match celebrations at Anfield.

Haaland, 26, scored the opener just minutes after Ryan Gravenberch had been sent off by referee Chris Kavanagh, in a win that kept City three points clear of Arsenal at the top of the Premier League.

The Norwegian striker made sure to lap up the plaudits from the adoring away fans after the match, celebrating the victory alongside his team-mates as the rest of Anfield emptied quickly.

As Haaland walked off the turf, clearly in high spirits, he was followed by a cameraman, who appeared to say: 'Great goal, mate. Great goal.'

The City man then jokingly responded: 'You are everywhere. I see you more than my missus, I do.'

Haaland has been dating girlfriend Isabel Haugseng Johansen, who is regularly featured on the striker's now-famous YouTube channel, for five years, since his career began blossoming at Borussia Dortmund.

Haaland scored the first of Manchester City's 3-0 thumping of Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday

Haaland and Isabel Haugseng Johansen have been together for half a decade and the couple share a child together

'She sent me the message,' the Manchester City striker once told Norwegian TV. 'She played for the same club I played for, Bryne. She was the one who checked me out. I wasn't the one who checked her out.

'From my experience, you find your girlfriend when you least expect it. If you're always looking for a girlfriend, you'll never find one. Get out and socialise. Meet people and get to know people.'

The pair share an almost two-year-old son together, who was born back in December 2024.

The power couple will soon be living it up in a luxury property in Abu Dhabi after Haaland bought a property in the newly built Ohana Development on Yas Island in the United Arab Emirates' capital.

His 53-year-old father, Alf-Inge Haaland, has also purchased a residence at the same complex, with property prices reportedly costing up to £7.5million.

Ahead of the high-stakes clash with Liverpool, Haaland Jr publicly threw his support behind the club, urging fans to 'enjoy the ride' in a show of defiance that echoed the stance of City's Abu Dhabi owners, who are fiercely appealing the verdict.

Enzo Maresca's win over Liverpool was the club's first fixture since they were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018.

The club maintained their innocence and appealed against the verdict.

If City lose their appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

Sports.title: Coventry 4-1 Newcastle: Sky Blues show Man City what a win built on honesty and grit looks like, writes CRAIG HOPE - as Frank Lampard's men secure their first home Premier League win in 25 years against leaderless Magpies
Sports.content:
Now here was a Sky Blue victory built on honesty and decades of endurance - unlike the one at Anfield 24 hours earlier. Coventry City are not Manchester City, be that on the pitch or off it. During the years when Manchester City cheated their way to Premier League and European titles, Coventry were playing in all three divisions of the Football League. Their ascent to the top tier has not been particularly pretty, and neither at times was this first home win of the season. It lacked, for the large part, the silk and skill of Manchester City’s dismantling of Liverpool. But Frank Lampard’s side have different qualities - and Newcastle were no match for that hard work, grit and collective will. This win was pure, never to be contested in a court of law or the court of public opinion. The goal that confirmed elevation to 14th did not arrive until the 81st minute - on the back of a nervy period in which Newcastle threatened to steal a point - but when it did it was entirely deserved. ‘An outstanding performance,’ said Lampard. ‘We were really good at the basics - second balls, duels. Those actions are critical to the modern Premier League. It’s not all pretty patterns. Coventry secured back-to-back Premier League wins by earning a 4-1 victory over Newcastle Sidiki Cherif scored the pick of Coventry's goals with a driven effort from outside the box Matthias Jaissle has seen his Newcastle side concede four times in their last two away games ‘And yes, it's big thing coming out of the bottom three. We have to tap into that in a humble way. It’s the balance of confidence to over confidence now.' It was substitute George Simms who slammed into the bottom corner after an error from Joelinton for 3-1. Then, to give the scoreline a better reflection of Coventry’s superiority, fellow substitute Stephen Mfuni lashed home another belter four minutes from time. ‘You’ve seen the City, now **** off home’ chorused the home crowd, and a chunk of the away end soon heeded that advice. Newcastle have more problems than their opponents right now - a lack of leaders and identity, for starters. This was a second straight 4-1 defeat on the road and, beyond long balls that invariably come back, it is hard to determine what Matthias Jaissle is trying to achieve with his team. PLAYER RATINGS COVENTRY (4-3–2-1): Rushworth 7; Van Ewijk 7, Pinnock 6, Thomas 7, Dasilva 7; Yirenkyi 7 (Onyeka 78, 6), Grimes 7 (Torp 83), Rudoni 7 (Mfuni 83, 7); Cherif 8 (Simms 78, 7), Mason-Clark 6 (Sakamoto 61, 6); Thomas-Asante 7 Subs: Bentley, Latibeaudiere, Hamer, Gboho Manager: Frank Lampard 8 NEWCASTLE (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 4; Miley 5 (Dedic 59, 5), Thiaw 5, Botman 6, Hall5; Gonzalez 5, Willock 5 (Joelinton 59, 4); Murphy 4 (Toure 59, 5), Wissa 4 (Osula 78), Barnes 5; Fernandez-Pardo 3 Subs: Pope, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Burn Manager: Matthias Jaissle 4 Referee: John Brooks 7 ‘We can only apologise to the fans that took the journey,’ said Jaissle. ‘We need to analysis it clearly, especially in the box, at both ends. The desire and hunger to score, to finish the attacks, that was missing. We conceded the goals too easily and didn’t finish our chances.’ Even before kick-off, this did not feel like a stadium that had witnessed two defeats without a goal on their team’s return to the Premier League, such was the noise. The 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest before the break had clearly restored belief. But there is nothing quite like a home goal to raise spirits - and the volume - still further. Twenty-five years on from Coventry’s last, and just six minutes in, Jack Rudoni brought relief to that particular quest. The midfielder had Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek to thank for the opportunity to score his first Premier League goal from the penalty spot. The Czech looked like he was gathering a bar of soap when Ephron Mason-Clark’s low shot ran through bodies and into - and out of - his grasp. Hornicek should have cut his losses but instead chased redemption. His team were soon chasing the game when his recovery dive sent Sidiki Cherif skyward at the expense of the spot-kick. Coventry missed a couple of chances to extend their advantage - a lack of composure was their undoing - but that was also the case at the other end, and preservation of the lead was always Lampard’s chief concern. Jack Rudoni opened the scoring for Coventry from the penalty spot in the early stages Jaissle’s concern should be his £51million forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo, who does not look or play yet like a Premier League striker Sven Botman had given Newcastle some barely deserved hope with a rocket into the top corner Ellis Simms, pictured, and Stephen Mfuni came off the bench to score and seal Coventry's win Jaissle’s concern, meanwhile, should be his £51million forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo. The young Belgian wants to play as striker and he used that desire as part of his bargaining when agreeing to join from Lille last month. Except, he does not look nor play like a Premier League centre-forward. At least not yet. And so, in the short term, the head coach needs to ignore the wishes of the player and pick a better option in such a key position. The second half began as badly as the first for Jaissle’s side. Milan van Ewijk’s long throw-in was headed only as far as the edge of the penalty area by defender Malick Thiaw and, when the efforts to close down Cherif were slow, the Guinean teenager very quickly blasted back into the bottom corner. Sven Botman gave Newcastle some barely warranted hope with a 20-yard rocket into the top corner, but it was short-lived. Coventry’s stay in the Premier League, you suspect, might not be.’
