Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Captures His First World Title
Sports.content:
Chicago, Illinois – Floyd “Kid Austin” Schofield (20-0, 13 KOs) captured the vacant WBA lightweight world title Saturday night by defeating “Prince” Lucas Bahdi (20-1, 15 KOs at the Wintrust Arena.

Bahdi proved much more difficult than expected. Schofield told the media after the fight that he had surprising power: “I didn’t expect him to have as much power as he did. I was kinda sleeping on his power until he caught me, but then once he caught me I kinda want to get that back, but I was like what’s more important, showing I got ego or going to get the world title.”

Floyd won a unanimous decision victory but appeared much closer than what it was scored officially: Alfredo Gallardo had it 119-108, Dave DeJonge judged it 116-110, and Steve Weisfeld scored it the closest at 115-111.

Both fighters scored a knockdown, but the difference was in Schofield’s ability to land punches and utilize lateral movement effectively to evade Bahdi’s counterattack, which won him the fight. Lucas struggled with Floyd’s movement, saying, “He was really quick on his feet. He wouldn’t stop moving all f**king night. He didn’t want to engage, but he fought a smart fight.” Schofield outlanded Bahdi 117 to 74 in total punches landed, connecting on 37.2 percent of his power punches. Lucas was limited offensively and was only able to land 23.5 percent of his total punches (Compubox). It was a tough match for Kid Austin, but ultimately his tactical boxing won the match.

Floyd stated after the fight that he’s dedicated his life to boxing and that becoming a world champion was always a dream he strived for. Now that he’s become world champion, he’ll take some time to rest and assess who’s next for him. WBO lightweight champion Abdullah Mason has expressed interest in unifying and would like to fight Schofield in the near future. There’s also recently crowned WBC lightweight champion William Zepeda, who is also promoted by Golden Boy and would be the easiest fight to make in terms of negotiating a deal between fighters of the same promotional stable.

As to what promoter Oscar De La Hoya has in mind for the two, it remains to be seen. A fight between any of the lightweight champions would be highly entertaining and competitive, as all the current fighters are skillful. Shakur Stevenson took to X and provided his own personal assessment of the fight, posting, “A C-level fighter beat an F-level fighter!!” However, Kid Austin posted his own post stating, in essence, that the ship has sailed on that and would instead pursue fights against Zepeda and Gary Russell. Shakur Stevenson appears to have his eyes set on a super fight match against Devin Haney. As for Floyd, if he pursues a unification match against any of the other lightweight champions, he’ll begin an interesting championship reign.

Sports.title: Keith Thurman Sees Power as Sebastian Fundora’s Weakness
Sports.content:
Keith Thurman claims raw one-punch power offers the only realistic avenue to stop Sebastian Fundora, yet his own loss exposed the weakness of that approach. Fundora had him backpedaling from the opening bell, reducing him to full flight, defensive shelling, and wild, sporadic lunges instead of any organized attack.

That reality presents a massive hurdle for Jaron “Boots” Ennis if they meet in the ring. Carrying fight-ending power only solves part of the puzzle. Ennis must find a way to unleash that heat while navigating the endless jabs and relentless flurries that neutralized Thurman.

“Anybody who’s going to really beat Fundora, it’s best to have that one-punch ability,” Thurman said to Fighthype.

He questions whether anyone can easily outbox Fundora over twelve rounds. The towering southpaw brings relentless stamina, immense work rate, and superior reach, trapping rivals in defensive shells for long stretches.

“He’ll throw a five-punch combo, and then he’ll get back to his jab, and then where’s your offense?” Thurman noted.

Thurman lived that nightmare in the ring. For most of the bout, he retreated under heavy fire, absorbing punishment as Fundora dictated every exchange. The sporadic power shots Thurman threw did nothing to slow the onslaught. He could never plant his feet long enough to turn his power into a true equalizer. Thurman did not test Fundora’s chin; he did not test his gas tank, and he barely tested his guard.

Hunting strictly for one massive counter can backfire against someone with Fundora’s dimensions. A power puncher risks losing minutes off the clock, hoping for a lapse that never arrives while Fundora banks points behind his jab. One whiff on a counter, and the cycle of absorbing incoming combos starts right back up.

Thurman did spot a technical flaw, however. He noted that Fundora often drops his hands instead of returning them to his chin, even if his sheer length makes exploiting that lapse tricky.

Ennis has to explode across the pocket instantly, capitalizing on those defensive gaps before the jab resets. Thurman respects Boots’ lightning speed along with his lethal killer instinct, but connecting with that first clean bomb remains the ultimate test. Fundora smothered Thurman’s offense from distance, and Boots faces the heavy task of finding room where none existed before.

Sports.title: Bill Haney Turns Up Pressure on Shakur Stevenson
Sports.content:
Bill Haney is calling on Shakur Stevenson to back up his public words regarding a 145-pound clash with Devin Haney. Bill confirmed that Devin accepts the weight limit with zero rehydration restrictions attached.

With November 28 in Atlanta being discussed as the proposed date, the two sides still have work to do before the fight becomes official. Bill’s frustration is that Shakur’s public response made the weight issue look settled, yet they’re still waiting for a completed agreement.

“I think he came out and he said done deal at 145.0. So stand on it,” Bill said to 78SPORTSTV.

That puts pressure on Shakur to explain what remains unresolved. Accepting a weight publicly gives fans reason to expect the fight, especially when the other side says it accepts the same number. It doesn’t mean the date, money, and every other contract term have been agreed upon.

Bill made Devin’s position on the weight clear.

“145.0 cool with us. No hydration, no none of that. Straight up 145 cool with us.”

Removing a rehydration cap gives Devin full freedom to bulk back up after making 145. That reality presents serious tactical considerations for Shakur, though Bill stopped short of confirming whether both teams have formally agreed to that specific term.

Addressing how Devin is handling the prolonged talks, Bill brushed off the holdup as familiar territory.

“I think that the people now get a chance to see who’s really about it and who’s just talking,” he noted.

Bill also declined to get drawn into a discussion about Liam Paro. His focus remains on Shakur, and he said he isn’t trying to kill the fight.

The approaching proposed date makes the wait harder to ignore. A November 28 event would leave limited time to complete negotiations, promote the card, and prepare for an opponent of this level. Bill wants movement now, but the interview leaves the key question unanswered: what still needs to be settled before both fighters sign?

Sports.title: Mannix Expects WBA to Approve Teofimo Lopez–Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall could find himself waiting behind another bigger fight despite being promised an immediate title shot. Chris Mannix expects the WBA to simply clear the runway for Teofimo Lopez to face Ryan Garcia.

The WBA has had weeks since Teofimo defeated Rolando Romero to settle the mandatory situation. Teofimo immediately called out Garcia, while Catterall remains stuck in limbo. Mannix points to conflicting written assurances from the sanctioning body as the source of the mess.

“The [WBA] will do anything for a buck. And from what I understand, they have made some mistakes here,” Mannix said on the Mannix and Mora podcast. “They clearly told Jack Catterall in writing that he is owed an immediate shot at Teofimo or a vacant belt. But from what I understand, they have also put in writing to Teofimo that he doesn’t have to defend his title against Jack Catterall.”

Mannix’s expectation is obvious: the money fight gets the green light.

“The way I see this playing out, the WBA is not going to stand in the way of a unification between Teofimo Lopez and Ryan Garcia,” he said.

Catterall has good reason not to buy another promise. Shakhram Giyasov spent roughly two years waiting for his WBA opportunity before facing Catterall for the secondary welterweight belt, watching Romero chase other paydays despite direct orders to fight him.

Allowing Teofimo to bypass Catterall continues that exact circus under a new champion. Mandatory status becomes nothing more than a placeholder that popular names can ignore at will.

Mannix expects the WBA to approve Lopez against Garcia and order the winner to face Catterall. A unification has obvious commercial appeal, but that solution asks Catterall to trust a system that already left Giyasov out in the cold.

The WBA needs to deliver an enforceable route to the ring. Another promise of being next just leaves him waiting on whichever cash cow comes along afterward.

Sports.title: Lucas Bahdi Threatens To Put Shakur Stevenson To Sleep
Sports.content:
Lucas Bahdi turned Shakur Stevenson’s “F-level fighter” insult back on him, claiming he would knock Shakur out and telling him to focus on getting Zuffa Boxing to book his next fight.

Shakur is grading other fighters while his own next bout remains unsettled. Bahdi spotted the obvious opening: he has been in the ring with Floyd Schofield, while Shakur is still talking about who he might fight.

“Well this ‘F level fighter’ would put your little running ass on the canvas and to Zzzzzz,” Bahdi said on X. “Keep focused on Zuffa actually getting you a fight.”

That was his response to Shakur’s October 10 post: “A C lever fighter beat a F level fighter!!”

The knockout claim is something Bahdi would have to prove. Getting to Shakur would require cutting off the ring and landing against a fighter who gives opponents few clean opportunities. Bahdi’s willingness to trade with Schofield doesn’t tell us how he would handle that task.

His comment about Zuffa is harder to ignore. Shakur has been discussing potential opponents, but negotiations don’t keep a fighter active. Until those talks produce a date, Bahdi can point to the difference between fighting and commenting on everyone else.

The “F-level” label also looks excessive when placed beside Shakur’s own opposition at lightweight. He fought Shuichiro Yoshino, Edwin De Los Santos, Artem Harutyunyan, Josh Padley and William Zepeda. Zepeda is the best answer to criticism of that run. The rest leave room for an argument about how far below them Bahdi really belongs.

De Los Santos would be a difficult opponent for Bahdi because of his speed, power, and southpaw stance. Even so, there is a reasonable case that Bahdi could compete with several fighters Shakur faced at 135. Dismissing him with a letter avoids explaining what makes him so inferior.

Shakur has zero room to be handing out letter grades to anyone right now. That signature win over Teofimo Lopez gave him all the momentum in the world, but sitting on the shelf degraded that goodwill in a hurry. Fans have short memories, and prolonged inactivity turns yesterday’s masterclass into old news.

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol vs Callum Smith Confirmed For December 12
Sports.content:
Matchroom Boxing made it official: Dmitry Bivol defends his unified light heavyweight titles against Callum Smith on December 12 in Yekaterinburg, Russia. Everyone knew this matchup was coming, but now Smith finally has an exact calendar date locked in.

This marks Bivol’s second ring appearance following his brutal rematch win over Artur Beterbiev last year. A back procedure slowed his calendar down, which left Smith on standby while putting the trilogy on pause.

Smith brings solid credentials, yet he isn’t who the crowd was craving. Bivol holds one win, Beterbiev holds one win, so fight fans wanted that tiebreaker settled first. Beating Smith keeps Bivol active, but it won’t satisfy everyone holding out for chapter three.

The downtime hurt Smith’s momentum, too. He hasn’t competed since taking down Joshua Buatsi. Taking on David Morrell during the wait never appealed to him because a loss would have erased his title shot entirely.

Sitting tight preserved his golden ticket, though it leaves him walking into his biggest light heavyweight test with noticeable ring rust. Timing Bivol’s footwork without warm-up rounds will be tough.

Both guys share nearly identical ages, so youth won’t decide this one. Smith must capitalize on his height advantage alongside his trademark left hook. Lingering effects from Bivol’s spinal surgery could play a huge role as well.

Smith can’t just trail Bivol around the canvas. If the champion darts in, connects, then vanishes, Smith will quickly fall behind on the scorecards.

December 12 settles things for these two fighters. The true blockbuster boxing fans really crave still sits on ice.

Smith showed his ceiling against both Canelo Alvarez and Beterbiev. When the elite guys close distance, take away his range, or refuse to stand in front of his left hook, his plan disappears. Beterbiev wore him out by applying physical pressure and breaking his guard, while Canelo neutralized him by taking away the left arm and dictating every inch of real estate.

Against Beterbiev, Smith looked battered and overmatched. Now going up against Bivol, he risks looking flat-footed and technically outclassed. The problem for Smith is that sitting on the shelf for eighteen months while waiting for Bivol to heal from back surgery could backfire on him.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois–Fabio Wardley Rematch Carries Thin PPV Card
Sports.content:
Saturday’s DAZN pay-per-view puts nearly all the pressure on Daniel Dubois against Fabio Wardley. Look past that headline attraction, because the undercard barely gives fans an incentive to reach for their wallets.

The event lands at The O2 arena in London on October 17, featuring Dubois putting his WBO belt on the line. Priced at £24.99 across the UK alongside an expected $59.99 tag in America, the supporting cast leaves buyers wondering what their cash actually buys.

Fans online shredded the fight schedule, making an entirely fair point. Dubois vs Wardley 2 brings plenty of heat after their brutal eleven-round initial meeting, but the undercard fails to offer real backup.

Bakhodir Jalolov meeting Solomon Dacres stands out as the most recognizable heavyweight clash on the lower bill. Tracking an Olympic gold medalist develop is fun, yet watching a prospect work differs completely from getting an explosive co-feature.

Jalolov is thirty-two years old, still wading through the prospect phase after spending years hopping back and forth between the Olympics and small pro shows. Solomon Dacres got wiped out in a single round by David Adeleye not that long ago, and while he ground out a win against Sirenko, he remains British domestic grade at best

Further down, Louie O’Doherty squares off with Michael Gomez Jnr, while Nelson Birchall takes on Levi Giles. Both scraps could bring plenty of excitement, though neither matchup seals the deal for a hefty price tag.

The rest of the broadcast leans on developing talent alongside domestic pairings. Young talent deserves room to grow on massive platforms, but spotlighting them doesn’t automatically create genuine value for paying customers.

Subscribers with DAZN Ultimate get the card bundled into their monthly plan, which softens the blow. Everyone else facing a standalone purchase has to judge if a single scrap justifies the full cost.

Queensberry staked the entire night on the main event producing magic. Dubois versus Wardley could easily deliver pure entertainment, yet that thrill can’t rescue a thin supporting bill. Boxing fans can crave the rematch while demanding more substance across the whole night.

Sports.title: Jose Valenzuela Pushes WBA for Floyd Schofield Fight
Sports.content:
Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela wants the WBA to put him next in line for Floyd Schofield’s lightweight title, potentially complicating the new champion’s unification plans before his first defense is arranged.

“Let’s make it happen,” Rayo wrote on X, tagging the WBA in response to a post arguing that Schofield must first face a mandatory or leading available contender after winning the vacant belt.

Schofield defeated Lucas Bahdi in Chicago on Saturday to become champion. Oscar De La Hoya has discussed unifications, but Rayo is asking the sanctioning body to consider its own ranked contenders before moving forward with those plans.

The WBA’s September rankings listed Schofield first, Bahdi second, and Rayo third. With Schofield now champion and Bahdi coming off the defeat, Rayo has a credible case for consideration. His position does not automatically establish him as the mandatory challenger.

Rayo, 27, holds a 16-3 record with 10 knockouts and is coming off a second-round knockout win over Edwin De Los Santos on June 28. Some fans criticized the finish, believing he hit De Los Santos while he was down and arguing for a no contest or disqualification. The official result remains a knockout victory.

There is also a promotional and broadcast hurdle. Rayo fights for Zuffa Boxing on Paramount+, while Schofield is promoted by Golden Boy, whose events air on DAZN. Making the fight would require the promoters to agree on terms and a broadcast arrangement.

A WBA order could push those discussions forward, but it would not decide which platform carries the event or how the revenue is divided.

The post Rayo shared also overstated the vacant-title rule. The WBA rules version amended through April 2024 requires a non-heavyweight vacant-title winner to make his initial defense within 120 days. That provision does not itself say every voluntary defense is prohibited.

Golden Boy therefore cannot treat Rayo’s request as an official order, but neither can it assume Schofield has an unrestricted choice of opponents. Rayo has publicly asked for the opportunity. The WBA’s response will determine whether that request becomes an obligation.

Ghana News.title: Man City bananas ‘brought fun back’, says Varadi
Ghana News.content:
Former Manchester City striker Imre Varadi said it was "brilliant to see" the club's fans waving inflatable bananas at Anfield on Sunday and feels it "brought a lot of fun back".

Varadi was nicknamed 'Imre Banana' by City fans during his two-year spell with the club in the late 1980s and they began taking inflatable bananas to games when they played in the old Second Division.

The craze continued into the early 90s, with City fans taking bananas to games intermittently since, and dozens re-emerged at Sunday's game.

City's 3-0 win over Liverpool was the club's first game since being found guilty of 114 charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

With the club facing sanctions such as a points deduction or expulsion from the Premier League, City fans took bananas to Anfield as a nod to their yo-yo years in the 1980s.

Varadi, who now sells inflatable bananas via the club and whose X account is @imre_banana, told BBC Radio 5 Live Drive: "It was amazing, [it's] bringing a lot of fun back into the game.

"The game itself was a terrific game obviously but just to see the inflatable craze coming back from the 80s when I was playing at the old Maine Road, it was a joy."

Varadi joined City from West Brom in October 1986 and scored 26 goals in 65 appearances before moving to Sheffield Wednesday in September 1988.

"Somebody started to call me Imre Banana and then, the following game, there were 10, 20, 25 bananas and then it just grew and grew and grew until every football club had an inflatable," he added.

"I started it, but it was 40 years ago, and it's still going strong now, as we all saw at Anfield. I'm really proud of it.

"It's bringing a lot of joy to the game. It's great to see."

Ghana News.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: The CEO as Chief Decision Maker
Ghana News.content:
By Ernest De-Graft Egyir

Insight.

Decision-making is one of the CEO’s most important responsibilities. Every major decision about strategy, people, investment, operations, and risk influences the organization’s direction and performance.

Effective CEOs do not attempt to make every decision themselves. They establish clear decision-making principles, involve the right people, distinguish urgent matters from important ones, and ensure that critical decisions are made at the appropriate level.

Key Strategies:

Establish clear principles for making strategic and operational decisions. Distinguish decisions that require CEO involvement from those that can be delegated. Use reliable data, professional judgment, and relevant stakeholder perspectives. Assess the risks and long-term implications of major decisions. Review the outcomes of significant decisions and apply the lessons learned.

CEO Leadership Actions.

✅ Identify the decisions that require your direct attention this week.

✅ Clarify decision-making authority across the executive team.

✅ Review whether previous major decisions have delivered their intended results.

Actionable Tip.

Before making a major decision, ask: “Does this decision advance our strategy, create sustainable value, and position the organization for future success?”

Why This Matters?

The quality of an organization’s decisions shapes its performance, resilience, and competitive position. When the CEO establishes a disciplined decision-making culture, the organization can act with greater confidence, speed, and accountability.

About the Author.

Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee

Ghana News.title: Burnham had formal meeting with Man City chair while mayor
Ghana News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham had one formal meeting with Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak while mayor of Greater Manchester, according to the Greater Manchester Combined Authority.

A GMCA statement said the meeting took place in October 2021 at the UK Government's Global Investment Summit, arranged by the Department for International Trade.

He also met Al Mubarak informally in the stands at a City home fixture in September 2019, when attending Vincent Kompany's testimonial as a guest of the club.

Burnham said on Sunday he would release details of his meetings with senior figures at Manchester City.

It follows criticism of his comments in the wake of the club being found guilty of all charges related to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.

A GMCA spokesperson said Burnham had been a guest at City home matches on a "small number of occasions" and that the hospitality had been "declared in the usual way".

The GMCA also said representatives of Greater Manchester sporting clubs would "routinely join business delegations" on international visits during Burnham's time as mayor.

It noted this included Manchester United representatives travelling to Austin and Dublin, Lancashire County Cricket Club joining a delegation to India, and City staff supporting visits to China and Japan.

Shadow sports minister Louie French said that Burnham "cannot hide behind the GMCA" and "must take responsibility for this himself" and urged him to "come clean about his relationship with City Football Group".

"This is far from the full transparency that football fans deserve," French said.

"We have been given precious little information about these meetings, what was discussed and what may have been agreed. If Burnham has nothing to hide, why is he being so tight-lipped?

"His bizarre intervention in defence of Man City's owners has raised serious concerns among fans."

An independent commission found City had broken rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018 by creating "sham" contracts with commercial partners to secretly funnel more than £830m into their football operations.

Burnham's previous role as mayor of Greater Manchester has raised questions about his relationship with City's Abu Dhabi ownership, with Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch demanding that No 10 release all details of meetings between the prime minister and senior figures at the club.

"I've been asked by the leader of the opposition to publish details of my meetings, which I'm happy to do, and I'm going to," Burnham told the Rest is Politics podcast.

"I will quite clearly put out there everything that I have done working with them in my previous role as Mayor of Greater Manchester.

"None of it is recent, actually, in terms of the meetings I had. I only had one significant meeting, actually, and that was in 2021."

The prime minister initially told the BBC he would be "really concerned" if Manchester City's owners decided to sell up following the guilty verdict, before later denying that his reaction had "downplayed the seriousness of the findings".

However, some Premier League clubs were so "astonished" by Burnham's stance that, according to sources, they were "concerned" about political interference in the appeal process.

Sanctions are yet to be announced, and City have lodged an appeal against the verdict.

City returned to action for the first time since the guilty verdict when they played at Liverpool on Sunday, winning 3-0.

Burnham defends comments on Man City

Burnham was mayor of Manchester from 2017 until earlier this year and his tenure took place during a sustained period of success for City.

As mayor, he championed investment from the Gulf as a way of growing Manchester's economy, a strategy which was initially pursued by the city's leaders before Burnham became the inaugural elected mayor of the Greater Manchester Combined Authority.

"I don't think I misspoke," said Burnham of his past comments on Manchester City's owners.

"What I would say is my mind hadn't been on all of the issues. My mind had been on Labour Party conference and I was doing interviews in relation to it.

"And also, I didn't link those two things. You know, the questions linked those two things. What I would say is they're very separate.

"The football issues are different from the investment issues. People will try and conflate those two things, but they shouldn't, in my view.

"The football issues, the findings of the independent commission are serious, as I said in the interview."

The entire process involving the charges against Manchester City is independent of the Premier League.

An independent commission held a 42-day hearing in 2024 which led to the verdict announced last month, with City also guilty of all charges except one relating to non-cooperation with the Premier League investigation.

The commission's report said that "a number of important club witnesses gave false evidence in key respects and that some knowingly gave untrue and dishonest evidence".

A separate independent appeal board will hear City's appeal. The club continues to deny any wrongdoing.

Ghana News.title: Is Ghana producing too many lawyers? What is the best lawyer-to-citizen ratio?
Ghana News.content:
By Richard Nii Amarh, ESQ

On Friday, October 9, 2026, the General Legal Council of Ghana recorded the names of 1,568 individuals onto the roll of lawyers, marking the single largest number of individuals called to the bar since Ghana started training its own lawyers.

The prestigious flaunting of photos by the new lawyers, alongside their families and friends, has re-ignited an annual conversation. Many are asking whether Ghana is producing too many lawyers and if our economy can absorb them into meaningful jobs. Concerned commentators often compare the number of lawyers to engineers, doctors, and other professionals, questioning which field is most critical for national development. Others worry about the heavy representation of lawyers in politics, which feeds into the persistent—though statistically unfair—perception that both lawyers and politicians are trained to bend the truth.

This article explores and compares the lawyer-to-citizen ratios of various countries near and far, examines the diverse career paths available to lawyers, and sets the stage for an informed conclusion on whether Ghana's legal boom is a blessing or a burden.

A Global Perspective: Lawyer-to-Citizen Ratios

1. The United Kingdom (UK)

Population: ~70 million

Lawyer Population: ~217,000

Ratio: 1 lawyer to every 440 citizens

GDP: ~$3.4 trillion

Average Income: £60,000 ($80,000 USD) per year

2. The United States of America (USA)

Population: ~350 million

Lawyer Population: ~1,374,720

Ratio: 1 lawyer to every 240 citizens (one of the highest densities globally)

GDP: ~$32.5 trillion

Average Income: ~$170,000 USD per year

3. China

Population: ~1.4 billion

Lawyer Population: ~830,000

Ratio: 1 lawyer to every 1,700 citizens

GDP: ~$18 trillion

Average Income: ¥900,000 ($140,000 USD) per year

4. Nigeria

Population: ~242 million

Lawyer Population: ~225,000

Ratio: 1 lawyer to every 2,000 citizens

GDP: ~$290 billion

Average Income: ₦14 million ($10,000 USD) per year

5. West African Neighbors (Nigeria Excluded)

Benin: Population of 14 million | GDP: $24.4 billion | 500 active lawyers | Ratio: ~1:32,000 | Average Salary: ~7 million CFA ($13,000 USD).

Togo: Population of 8.6 million | GDP: $11.9 billion | 350 active lawyers | Ratio: ~1:30,000 | Average Salary: 2M–5M CFA ($3,300 to $8,300 USD).

Ivory Coast: Population of 32 million | GDP: $99.7 billion | 800 active lawyers | Ratio: ~1:40,000 to 1:50,000 | Average Salary: 2.4M–6.7M CFA ($4,000 to $11,000 USD).

Burkina Faso: Population of 23–24 million | GDP: ~$32.5 billion | ~300–400 lawyers | Ratio: ~1:65,000 to 1:75,000 | Average Salary: 2.4M–5.5M CFA ($4,000 to $9,000 USD).

Liberia: Population of ~5.5–6 million | GDP: ~$5.2 billion | ~600–900 lawyers | Ratio: ~1:7,000 to 1:9,000 | Average Salary: $4,000 to $12,000 USD.

6. Ghana

Population: ~35 million

GDP: $77 billion

Lawyer Population: Nearly 10,000 (according to Ghana Bar Association data)

Ratio: 1 lawyer to every 4,000 citizens

Average Income: Estimated at GHS 180,000 annually (~$15,000 USD)

The Local Reality: Courts, Judges, and Concentration

Legal services are tightly tethered to economic activity. Unsurprisingly, the vast majority of lawyers in Ghana are heavily concentrated in Accra, Kumasi, and Takoradi, leaving other regions and secondary cities underserved.

While hard scientific research on whether Ghana has an "excess" of lawyers is sparse, a few critical metrics helps clarify the picture:

Ghana currently has roughly 500 courts operating nationwide.

The Judicial Service Staff Association recently reported that there are about 130 courts without judges (currently only qualified lawyers can be appointed to the bench).

The bottleneck here isn't a shortage of lawyers willing to serve as judges; rather, it is a matter of financial clearance. Just like any other public sector employment, the Ministry of Finance must approve funding before judges can be appointed and paid.

The absence of judges in these 130 courts puts enormous pressure on the justice system, causing endless adjournments, delayed adjudications, and intense frustration for litigants. If Ghana is struggling to fund 130 more judges, why are we pumping 1,500 new lawyers onto the market every year?

Beyond Litigation: Where Do Lawyers Work?

A law degree is remarkably versatile. Beyond traditional courtroom battles, new lawyers enter a wide range of rewarding career paths:

Litigation Counsel: Representing individual, corporate, or institutional clients across all court levels (Circuit, High Court, Supreme Court) in civil, criminal, land, and human rights disputes.

Corporate & Commercial Practice: Advising businesses on corporate governance, mergers and acquisitions, regulatory compliance, and foreign investments.

Intellectual Property (IP) Practice: Managing trademark, copyright, and patent registrations, alongside IP licensing and disputes.

In-House Counsel / Legal Officer: Managing legal risks, drafting commercial contracts, and ensuring compliance for banks, telcos, mining firms, and fintechs.

Company Secretary: Serving as principal administrative and governance officer for corporate boards under the Companies Act.

State Attorney / Legal Counsel: Working within the Attorney-General's Department and Ministry of Justice to advise government bodies, prosecute state cases, and draft legislation.

Judicial Service: Serving as Magistrates, Registrars, or judicial research assistants.

Regulatory Bodies & Commissions: Enforcing sector-specific laws at institutions like the Bank of Ghana, SEC, NCA, and EPA.

Arbitrator or Mediator: Specializing in out-of-court settlements under Ghana’s Alternative Dispute Resolution framework.

Law Lecturer / Researcher: Teaching and training future advocates at faculties like UG, KNUST, GIMPA, UPSA, and the Ghana School of Law.

Advocacy & Policy Consultant: Driving public interest litigation, law reform, and human rights work with think tanks and NGOs.

Conclusion: Are We Producing Too Many?

To answer whether Ghana is producing too many lawyers, I will give a typical lawyer's answer: It depends.

Major Western economies can comfortably support large numbers of lawyers and sustain high-income jobs despite low lawyer-to-citizen ratios, largely due to the sheer size of their markets. In West Africa, however, Nigeria stands out as the only country with a lower lawyer-to-citizen ratio than Ghana—and it possesses a significantly larger economy.

If Ghana rapidly scales up its economic power to match the growing influx of annual law graduates, these numbers won't pose a problem. However, if economic growth remains stagnant, policymakers will inevitably need to take a hard look at the trajectory and regulation of legal education in Ghana.

Disclaimer: Most statistics used in this article were compiled from online sources and actual figures are subject to minor variations.

Written by Richard Nii Amarh, ESQ (Private Legal Practitioner and Head of the Legal Department, Centre for Legitimacy and Rule of Law)

Ghana News.title: NDC sinking Ghana’s democracy with Emelia Agbenyo’s appointment – Miracles Aboagye
Ghana News.content:
The Communications Director of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dennis Miracles Aboagye, has accused the National Democratic Congress (NDC) of undermining Ghana’s democracy over the appointment of Emelia Agbenyo as a Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission (EC).

He argues that Ms Agbenyo’s alleged political affiliations and previous roles linked to the NDC raise concerns about her ability to discharge her duties independently.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Monday, October 12, Mr Aboagye described the decision as a threat to the democratic principles of neutrality and accountability, which he said were essential to the work of the Electoral Commission.

“It’s a shame how low they are sinking this democracy that we’ve all been fighting for and working towards its growth,” he said.

"This lady is not just an advocate of the NDC. In fact, he is a die-in-the-wool NDC, even more NDC than Rashid Tanko himself. Are you aware that this lady was a special assistant to Honourable Ayariga when he was Deputy Education Minister during the John Mahama number one presidency?

"Is that the role for consultants? Is that a role for neutral people? That is not all. This is a lady who currently holds a political appointment, a partisan political appointment."

Mr Aboagye also referred to a political message attributed to Ms Agbenyo in support of John Mahama during the 2020 and 2024 election campaigns, which he said raised questions about her suitability for a position requiring independence.

“This is a lady that is being sold to us as somebody that can independently bear the affairs of our election, except a person who has openly taken sides,” he said.

He questioned why the NDC would nominate someone whose political history, in his view, could undermine public confidence in the Electoral Commission.

Mr Aboagye maintained that the appointment could affect perceptions of the Commission’s impartiality, insisting that "individuals appointed to oversee elections must be seen to be independent of partisan interests."

His comments follow criticism of Ms Agbenyo’s appointment, with questions being raised about whether her previous political roles are compatible with the neutrality expected of a Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission.

Ghana News.title: Seedorf back in football as Corinthians head coach
Ghana News.content:
Corinthians have appointed Clarence Seedorf as their head coach, with the former Netherlands midfielder taking on his first coaching role since 2019.

The 50-year-old has joined the club on a contract until the end of 2027, with the club 16th in the Brazilian top flight, one place above the relegation zone with eight games left.

Seedorf succeeds former Brazil interim national coach Fernando Diniz, who was sacked by Corinthians last week after the club lost seven consecutive league games.

Seedorf's last coaching role was with the Cameroon national team more than seven years ago, and he has previously had underwhelming spells at AC Milan, Shenzhen FC, and Deportivo La Coruña.

"Taking on this challenge is an honour, but also a huge responsibility. I am here to give my all and build a team that fights for every ball, every minute, every victory," said Seedorf of his Corinthians appointment.

Seedorf inherits a Corinthians squad which features former Manchester United players Memphis Depay and Jesse Lingard.

Dutch great Seedorf retired from playing in 2014 following a glittering career that yielded four Champions League titles, two with AC Milan, one with Real Madrid, and one with Ajax.

Seedorf remains the only player to win the Champions League with three different clubs.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Houthi missile attack targets Saudi capital Riyadh for third day in a row
World.content:
Saudi Arabia says it intercepted a ballistic missile fired towards Riyadh, as Houthis say they targeted the King Khalid airport.

The Saudi Arabia-led coalition fighting in Yemen has said its forces intercepted another ballistic missile launched by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital, Riyadh, as the city reels from attacks that have killed at least 14 people in recent days.

In a statement on X, Turki Al-Maliki, the spokesperson for the coalition, said the Houthis fired one ballistic missile at Riyadh and two towards Khamis Mushait, a city in the southwest.

All three were “intercepted and destroyed”, he said.

Residents of Riyadh reported several powerful explosions on Monday night, moments after a text message to their phones warned of an aerial threat.

The Houthis, who control Yemen’s most populous areas, including the capital, Sanaa, said their target in Riyadh had been King Khalid International airport.

Yahya Saree, a Houthi military spokesman, said the group had also sent a drone towards a military airbase at Khamis Mushait, near the Yemeni border. He again warned international airlines and travellers “against operating flights to airports” in Saudi Arabia, except in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, saying the facilities were “unsafe”.

The renewed attacks came as King Khalid International airport in Riyadh remains closed after a Houthi attack on Saturday that killed at least 13 people and wounded more than 300 others. Another strike on Sunday killed one person and wounded 11.

Saudi authorities said the airport would remain closed until this Saturday, and airlines have canceled flights. The Houthis have also struck Saudi oil facilities.



The attacks come as the Houthis fight forces aligned with Yemen’s internationally recognised government for control of the country. The Saudi-led coalition has carried out an air campaign against the Houthis and backed the government’s ground forces. The fighting erupted amid regional tensions set off by the United States and Israel’s war on Iran.

Speaking at an energy conference in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia’s Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman Al Saud said the attacks on airports over the last week have tested the kingdom’s resilience.

“The events of recent weeks are serious,” the minister said. “Our response must be equally serious.” He added that Vision 2030, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s plan to diversify the Saudi economy, “must continue. Investment must continue”.

Saudi authorities have meanwhile opened an investigation into why the country’s air defences failed to stop the barrage, according to two regional officials who spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity. An initial inquiry found that the Houthis first launched several drones to clear a path for a mix of cruise and ballistic missiles, which then reached the airport, the officials said.

The Houthis possess ballistic missiles with warheads that can change direction in flight, posing a challenge to the Patriot interceptors and other systems the Saudis rely on.

One official told AP that investigators also wanted to know why the defences had not given earlier warning of an attack in which missiles and drones flew more than 1,000km, or 620 miles, to reach Riyadh.

US President Donald Trump separately criticised the Houthis but gave no indication that Washington would intervene. “Well, the Houthis are misbehaving very badly. No good,” he told reporters when asked what he planned to do about the group.

A Houthi official warned that US involvement would bring retaliation.

“If the US becomes involved in the aggression against Yemen, we will not deliberate over the decision to respond; rather, there will be a swift and painful response targeting the US and all its interests in the region,” Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, a member of the Houthis’ political bureau, told the AFP news agency.

Al-Bukhaiti also warned “all employees and workers at Saudi oil facilities and airports to stay away from these sites, as they have become legitimate targets”.

The attacks have put events scheduled in Riyadh this month under pressure, including the kingdom’s flagship investment conference and the WPC Energy Congress, where several top oil executives were dropped from the programme.



The United Arab Emirates’s national carrier Etihad Airways announced on Monday that it was cancelling all flights to and from Riyadh until next week. It also suspended flights to Dammam and Jeddah.

Bahrain’s national carrier Gulf Air said it, too, was cancelling all Riyadh flights until Saturday.

US operator Delta announced it would delay the launch of direct flights from Atlanta to Riyadh, scheduled for October 23.

World.title: Two deaths reported as Hurricane Simon, storm Rachel batter Mexico’s coast
World.content:
Simon caps a Pacific season of record-breaking intensity, as deadly storms wreak havoc from Hawaii to Mexico.

At least two people have died in Mexico after Hurricane Simon and former tropical storm Rachel brought torrential rain and catastrophic flooding to Pacific coast communities.

At a Monday news briefing, Guerrero Governor Evelyn Salgado confirmed that a 71-year-old man had died during Hurricane Simon after a retaining wall collapsed under the weight of intense precipitation.

According to the Guerrero-based news agency IRZA, the man, identified by his family as Albino Moreno Jimenez, had been feeding his animals on the western outskirts of Chilpancingo when a wall came crashing down on him.

A second death was announced later in the day in the state of Baja California along Mexico’s western coast. There, Governor Marina del Pilar said that a young girl had died from the effects of what was once Hurricane Rachel, which peaked in early October as a Category 3 storm.

At least 10 more people remain missing in Baja California, according to the governor. Eight were reported missing in the city of Ensenada, on the Pacific coast, and two in the fishing town of San Felipe on the Gulf of California.

The figures remain preliminary, with local newspaper La Jornada reporting a higher death toll of two in Baja California and 11 missing.

Death toll expected to rise

Rachel made landfall in the Mexican state as a post-tropical cyclone, and its remnants have travelled north through southern California in the southwestern United States.

Hurricane Simon, meanwhile, has churned off the coast of Mexico since the weekend. By late Monday morning, it had weakened from a powerful Category 4 storm to a Category 2.



Its maximum sustained winds had slowed slightly to around 155km/h (100mph), according to the US National Hurricane Center. Its centre was about 115km west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes, a cape in the state of Jalisco, drifting west at 3km/h.

Forecasters predict Simon could make landfall on Thursday or Friday. Hurricane warnings remain in effect for western Mexico, which is vulnerable to landslides and deadly surf conditions as a result of the storm.

Experts warn the death toll from both storms could rise, and officials have called on residents to exercise caution amid the devastation wrought by downed trees, high winds and floodwaters.

The Spanish newspaper El Pais reported the death of a cliff diver, Juan Patines, who was killed in Mazatlan, the northwestern state of Sinaloa, after jumping into the sea on Saturday night.

According to Mexican media, the heavy surf hampered his efforts to return to shore amid dangerous coastal conditions associated with Hurricane Simon. Local authorities later halted cliff-diving at the site due to hazardous sea conditions.

Officials have yet to confirm whether his death was directly linked to Hurricane Simon.

A record Pacific storm season

Rachel and Simon have battered Mexico’s western coast as part of an extraordinary stretch of hurricane activity across the Pacific.

The northeastern and central Pacific Ocean has experienced a record storm season this year, fuelled in part by the El Nino weather phenomenon, which results in warming waters in parts of the region. Twenty-one named storms have been recorded in the Pacific so far.

On Sunday, Simon tipped the region to a historic high for accumulated cyclone energy (ACE), a metric of the combined strength and longevity of tropical storms. This year has already surpassed the previous high set in 2018.

The US island chain of Hawaii has been among the hardest-hit places. In August, Hurricane Lala unleashed ruinous flooding on Hawaii’s Big Island as a Category 1 storm, killing a 93-year-old woman and destroying some 100 homes, according to state officials.

A few weeks later, Hurricane Lowell, a Category 4 hurricane at its peak, struck the Hawaiian islands of Kauai and Niihau, where powerful winds, storm surge and flooding overwhelmed towns and roads.

Roughly 90 percent of Kauai’s power customers were plunged into darkness as a result of electricity outages. At least two deaths were linked to Lowell.

In late September, Hurricane Nolo brought another round of flooding and landslides to the Hawaiian islands, though it did not make landfall.

World.title: US archbishop says Catholics in army should not participate in firing squad
World.content:
Archbishop Timothy Broglio says the US plan to livestream the execution of the Fort Hood attacker is contrary to church’s teachings.

Share US archbishop says Catholics in army should not participate in firing squad on social media

United States Archbishop Timothy Broglio has urged Catholics who are members of the country’s armed forces not to take part in a planned public execution by firing squad, saying that it violates the teachings of the church.

Broglio released a strongly worded statement on Monday raising a series of concerns about the US military’s plan to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan, a former army major who killed 13 people during a shooting attack at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009.

“I oblige any Catholics assigned to the firing squad to request to be excused from this action contrary to the teaching of the Church,” Broglio said.

He also asked whether the US wants to “imitate the terrorists of this world and make a public spectacle of barbarically killing our adversaries”.

The plan to livestream the execution on December 3 was announced last week by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who characterised the spectacle as deterrence.

“We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public, because people need to understand that there are serious consequences for these types of things,” Hegseth told the right-wing media outlet Real America’s Voice.

But the proposal has sparked backlash from lawmakers, rights groups and critics who warn that a publicly broadcast killing is not only unethical but could also be used as anti-US propaganda.

Hasan, now aged 56, was shot by the police during the 2009 Fort Hood attack and is now wheelchair-bound. Critics fear livestreaming Hasan’s death could turn him into a symbol for armed groups that may be hostile to the US.

Cardinal Blase J Cupich, the archbishop of Chicago, also condemned the plan to livestream the execution in a social media post on Monday, questioning the example it could set for children.



“Capital punishment is unacceptable in any case,” he said. “The planned broadcast of the taking of a life by firing squad is nothing short of performative barbarism. Do we really want our children, who will inevitably view it, exposed to the pornography of a state-sponsored slaying?”

Hegseth has said he wants the execution to take place at the same time and location as the 2009 shooting spree, and described using military members to carry out the death penalty.

“It hadn’t been since World War II since we’ve done that,” Hegseth said of the firing squad. “Well, I kind of like the mentality we had in World War II, which was win.”

The last US military execution by firing squad was of Eddie Slovik, who was accused of desertion in 1945. He was the only US soldier to have such a sentence carried out for abandoning his post.

In Monday’s statement, Broglio also questioned the reasoning behind putting service members on camera to carry out Hasan’s death. He hinted that it could harm the US military’s image abroad.

“The US military generally enjoys a good reputation in the world,” Broglio wrote. “Is there really a value to throwing them in the same boat with terrorists by broadcasting the image of the execution of a man in a wheel chair to the whole world?”

Without mentioning Hasan’s case specifically, Pope Leo also released a statement on Saturday condemning the death penalty.

“The death penalty is inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person,” he said in a social media post.

“The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment: effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption.”

President Donald Trump, who oversaw an unprecedented spike in federal executions during his first term in office, has approved Hasan’s execution.

Still, on Saturday, he indicated that he has not decided whether to proceed with a livestream.

“There are two thoughts: Don’t show it and show it. Because, you know, by showing it, maybe other people won’t be doing what he did,” Trump told reporters. “I’ll make a decision.”

Since the start of his second term as president, Trump has pushed for the increased use of the federal death penalty. In April, he also approved additional methods to carry out the death penalty, including the firing squad.

In the past, Trump has also floated the death penalty as a punishment for crimes ranging from drug dealing to sedition, a term he has invoked against political rivals.

World.title: Poland says two Turks arrested over Russia-linked Starlink station fire
World.content:
Two Turkish citizens have been detained in Germany over a fire at a Starlink station in central Poland that Warsaw has branded an act of sabotage carried out on Russia’s behalf.

Polish officials announced the arrests on Monday, one month after the fire, which they say was aimed at disrupting internet services, including for Ukraine’s military. The fire, in Masovia in Eastern Poland, engulfed the Starlink station’s power system and backup generator.

Polish Minister of Interior Marcin Kierwinski said the two men would face charges in Poland of carrying out sabotage on the instructions of a foreign intelligence agency. German police made the arrests on behalf of Polish services, according to Deutsche Welle. Polish officials did not say where or when in Germany the men were detained.

“We have no doubt that Russian services are behind this act of sabotage,” Special Services Minister Tomasz Siemoniak said in a news conference. “It is worth adding that Russian services are increasingly turning to individuals linked to the criminal underworld,” he said.

The case is the latest in a string of incidents that officials across the European Union deem to be part of a Russian campaign of sabotage and hybrid attacks aimed at eroding support for Ukraine.

The Russian embassy in Warsaw did not immediately reply to a request for comment. Moscow has previously dismissed similar accusations as baseless and the product of anti-Russian hysteria.

Ukraine’s military relies on tens of thousands of Starlink terminals for battlefield communications and occasional drone operations. Starlink founder Elon Musk activated the service over Ukraine in 2022, days after Russia’s full-scale invasion, following a plea from Kyiv. Poland has said it pays for Ukraine’s Starlink subscription.



Musk has since clashed with Ukrainian officials over his views on the war. This year, he also agreed to switch off thousands of Russian “grey-market” Starlink terminals in Ukraine, causing problems for Russian forces. Ukraine is now seeking to use the terminals for attacks on Russian territory.

World.title: Why the Cornell gang rape case has raised concerns about fraternity culture
World.content:
Experts say many fraternities offer a sense of community, but some rely on hazing and coercive tactics to build loyalty.

Share Why the Cornell gang rape case has raised concerns about fraternity culture on social media

For more than 40 percent of US presidents, the fraternity hall was an early stop on the road to the White House.

Fraternal organisations, more commonly known as fraternities or frats, have a long and storied history on college campuses in the United States.

One industry group, the North American Interfraternity Conference (NIC), represents 58 fraternities spread across 600 schools. It claims nearly 200,000 undergraduate students as active members and an alumni population of 4.2 million.

The draw for college-aged men is the promise of brotherhood, a bond that transcends keg parties and late-night revelry. Like sororities and other members-only student organisations, fraternities are often touted as pathways to personal, academic and professional success.

But critics argue that some fraternities have leveraged their exclusivity to encourage and normalise violence, dangling social acceptance as a reward for compliance.

“This isn’t [some sort of] a hobbyist club,” said anthropologist Aldo Cimino, a Kent State University professor who studies fraternity hazing. “It is the seriousness of the affiliation that has generated the intensity of these induction rituals.”

In recent weeks, one case has renewed debate over fraternity culture and whether the campus organisations use their exclusivity to shield bad behaviour.

In September, an anonymous woman known as Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the Chi Phi fraternity at Cornell University and seven of its members, accusing them of gang raping her during a party on the night of October 19, 2024.



Doe’s sorority, Delta Delta Delta, and Cornell itself are among the co-defendants.

Her lawsuit raises questions about fraternity and sorority culture at US schools, collectively known as “Greek life” for the groups’ use of Greek lettering and symbols.

Upon her admission to Cornell, Doe argues she encountered a “glorified – yet materially false and misleading – facade” for Greek life.

“She arrived on a campus where the University actively promoted Greek membership as a ‘vital’ part of the campus community and endorsed these organizations as well-managed, worthy pathways to new friendships and improving one’s educational and professional opportunities,” the lawsuit said.

The complaint accuses the fraternities of instead perpetuating a pattern of sexual assault and abuse.

What are fraternities?

Now a multibillion-dollar industry, fraternities in the US trace their origins to men-only clubs established at some of the country’s oldest universities.

The tradition began at the College of William and Mary in 1776, when Phi Beta Kappa was founded as a secret society for debate and scholarly exchange.

Its adoption of the Greek alphabet, oath of secrecy, and arcane membership rites helped establish a blueprint for future fraternities and sororities. Often with houses of their own, fraternities eventually grew into informal extensions of the campus residential system.

Historian Nicholas Syrett wrote about the origins of such groups in his book The Company He Keeps: A History of White College Fraternities.

In an interview with Al Jazeera, he explained that fraternities have long embraced so-called masculine ideals. But those ideals have changed from generation to generation.

In the past, fraternities sought to position themselves in “opposition to boyhood” by embracing “independence, strength of character, handsomeness and loyalty”, Syrett explained.

But their modern iteration has shifted to include a greater emphasis on “athleticism, sexual success with women, and recklessness” as well as alpha-male posturing.

Syrett argues that the fraternity system’s cult of toughness reflects a wider matrix of gendered expectations and social hierarchies.

Early fraternity men, Syrett says, prized intellect and academic distinction, provided neither betrayed too much effort. But “this has largely taken a backseat in contemporary fraternities”, he explained.

“When [men] are initiated, they are taught that loyalty to the brotherhood is of the utmost importance,” Syrett said of fraternities today. “This leads to the keeping of all kinds of secrets, including things that are against the rules and/or the law.”



A mark of elite status

In the two and a half centuries since the first fraternities were formed, Greek life has expanded to include different races and identities outside of white men.

Some Greek groups have even eschewed the traditional gender divide altogether to better embrace transgender and non-binary members.

But fraternities and sororities overall tend to act as “microcosms of the larger society”, according to Elizabeth Allan, a professor at the University of Maine and director of its Hazing Prevention Research Lab, “with race, pretty privilege and economic segregation helping shape the system”.

“The [social] stratification that we see in the larger society is going to be reflected, in large part, in many of these organisations, unless they’re actively working to disrupt it,” she added.

Between membership dues and rent at fraternity chapter houses, Greek organisations can price out all but the more affluent students, according to Allan.

“Pretty privilege” – the social bias in favour of those deemed conventionally attractive – can add to the pressure, with sorority applicants in particular shelling out hundreds, if not thousands, of dollars for cosmetic treatments and outfits.

Experts say the sense of exclusivity that many fraternities and sororities cultivate is a powerful draw for incoming students, who see membership as a path to upward social mobility.

That perception is reinforced by the groups’ internal dynamics. Many sororities and fraternities encourage networking among members.

A 2021 Gallup survey commissioned by the NIC and the National Panhellenic Conference found that 42 percent of fraternity or sorority alumni said a fellow member had helped them find an internship or job.

Meanwhile, 51 percent of Greek members reported having a job waiting at graduation or found employment within two months. The rate was much lower among those who were not members of such fraternities or sororities, at 36 percent.

How hazing shapes fraternities

Critics often point to hazing rituals in particular as shaping a culture of violence at some fraternities and sororities.

Hazing is a process through which prospective Greek life members undergo humiliating and sometimes perilous tasks to secure admission.

The phenomenon is prohibited by law in most US states, though the definitions, penalties and scope of such laws vary. The consequences, however, can be deadly.

One of the earliest recorded deaths associated with fraternity hazing took place at Cornell in 1873.

At the time, a group of “pledges” – would-be fraternity members – were blindfolded and led far from campus at night, with instructions to make their way back on their own.
