At the same time, Riyadh residents received an alert on their phones stating: “The region is exposed to a hostile aerial threat. Please remain calm and stay at home or in a safe place, away from windows and doors, and continue to follow civil defense instructions.”

Subsequently, the coalition announced the “interception and destruction” of a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis, in a statement on X.

This incident did not seem to upset Ronaldo, who scored the 981st goal of his career just before halftime, as the Saudi champions secured a 3-1 win.

AFP

World.title: $1bn military arms was never paid into private accounts – Buratai
World.content:
Former Chief of Army Staff, retired Lt.-Gen. Tukur Buratai, has clarified that the one billion dollars earmarked for military arms procurement during his time was never paid into individual service accounts.

Buratai made the clarification while delivering a keynote lecture at the Defence Correspondents Association of Nigeria (DECAN) Conference and Awards Ceremony on Monday in Abuja.

He addressed the controversy surrounding the arms procurement funding as part of his presentation on technology, intelligence-led operations and Nigeria’s national security.

The former army chief said the clarification was important in understanding the administration and handling of the funds.

He argued that discussions on defence procurement should be grounded in accurate information about funding channels and institutional responsibilities.

Buratai’s remarks came amid broader discussions on the need to strengthen Nigeria’s military capabilities through modern technology, intelligence sharing and improved operational coordination.

He said the country’s security challenges required sustained investment in equipment and systems capable of supporting intelligence-led operations and responses to emerging threats.

The retired general also advocated greater use of technology, including artificial intelligence and integrated command systems, to improve surveillance, intelligence analysis and operational decision-making.

The conference, themed “Beyond Kinetic Warfare: Harnessing Technology and Intelligence-Led Operations for Nigeria’s National Security,” also featured the launch of DECAN’s maiden magazine, The Defence Correspondent.

(NAN)

World.title: 2027: Wike unites PDP, APC for Tinubu’s victory in FCT
World.content:
Key stakeholders from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the All Progressives Congress (APC) have formed a united political front dedicated to securing President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.

The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, unveiled the historic alliance during a stakeholders’ meeting of the Rainbow Coalition in Abuja on Monday, demonstrating cross-party unity.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the coalition brought together serving and former senators, party chairmen, National Assembly candidates, and grassroots leaders of PDP and APC from the six FCT area councils.

The party leaders unanimously agreed that Tinubu remains their sole presidential candidate for 2027.

Announcing his role as the coordinator and field commander of the president’s re-election campaign in the FCT and Rivers, Wike stressed that shared national objectives must take precedence over traditional party divisions.

“I want to let all of you know that we are going to work together. Nobody should say, ‘I am PDP’ or ‘I am APC.’ For the purpose of this election, we are together,” he said.

The minister cited the 2024 Edo State governorship election as clear proof that joint cooperation between APC and PDP elements could decisively shape electoral outcomes.

According to him, when political stakeholders align behind a singular, compelling goal, party labels become secondary to results.

He explained that the primary focus of the coalition is to ensure Tinubu’s victory at the polls.

According to him, the participating parties retain the flexibility to navigate other localised contests while remaining fully aligned at the presidential level.

Wike said that the coalition anchored its re-election campaign on the tangible achievements of the Tinubu administration across the FCT and the nation.

On infrastructure development, Wike cited extensive road construction, school rehabilitations, police station upgrades, and public facility enhancements across all six FCT area councils.

He also cited institutional reforms, particularly the creation of the FCT Civil Service Commission, the appointment of an internal Head of Service, and the establishment of dedicated Secretariats for Women Affairs and Youth Development.

According to him, the reforms have created opportunities for career progression among FCT civil servants and expanded participation in governance.

On economic reforms and security, the minister pointed at Tinubu’s long-term economic restructuring and vocal support for the proposed establishment of state police to strengthen national security.

“By establishing this bipartisan framework, the APC and PDP coalition aims to build a formidable political force that unites leaders and residents behind the continued development and leadership of Tinubu in 2027,” he said.

Earlier, APC State Chairman in FCT, Mr Ishaku Yamawo, pledged unalloyed support for Wike, declaring him the “pilot and commandant” of the territory’s electoral campaign.

Yamawo lauded the minister for bringing political opponents together under one umbrella to drive strategic victory.

His counterpart in the PDP, Usman Yahaya, said, “We are in PDP but we are going to support Tinubu’s re-election 100 per cent.” (NAN)

World.title: Nigeria’s debt interest payments surge 37.5% to N7.7trn in H1’26 — World Bank
World.content:
By Yinka Kolawole, with agency report

Nigeria’s debt interest payments surged by 37.5 per cent to N7.7 trillion in the first half of 2026 from N5.6 trillion in the corresponding period of 2025.

This indicates that the interest payments exceed the Federal Government’s revenue of N6.2 trillion during the period by N1.5 trillion, representing 24.2 per cent.

The World Bank disclosed this in its 2026 Nigeria Development Update (NDU), titled ‘Beyond the Federal Purse: How Higher Revenues Reshaped State Priorities’.

According to the report, interest payments rose to 3.1 per cent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the first half of 2026, from 2.5 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025, highlighting the growing pressure of debt servicing on public finances.

The increase came despite a significant improvement in Federal Government revenue, which rose by more than 72 per cent to N6.2 trillion, representing 2.5 per cent of GDP, from N3.6 trillion, or 1.6 per cent of GDP, in the first half of 2025.

The bank attributed the revenue growth to a recovery in oil receipts, stronger corporate tax collections and higher independent revenues, while customs revenues remained stable and Value Added Tax (VAT) collections were comparatively flat.

It stated: “Federal revenues rose to about 2.5 per cent of GDP (N6.2 trillion), from 1.6 per cent of GDP (N3.6 trillion) a year earlier, supported by a recovery in oil receipts, stronger corporate tax collections, and higher independent revenues, while customs revenues held stable and VAT collections stayed comparatively flat.”

On expenditure, the World Bank said interest payments increased to 3.1 per cent of GDP, or N7.7 trillion, from 2.5 per cent, or N5.6 trillion, amid high domestic borrowing costs.

The rising debt burden coincided with a sharp decline in reported capital expenditure, which fell to 0.3 per cent of GDP, or N700 billion, from 1.0 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025. Other expenditure remained unchanged at 1.3 per cent of GDP.

Meanwhile, total government expenditure rose to N16.1 trillion in the first half of 2026 from N14.6 trillion a year earlier, although it declined marginally as a share of GDP to 6.5 per cent from 6.6 per cent.

Personnel costs also increased to N4.2 trillion from N3.7 trillion following wage adjustments, but remained unchanged at 1.7 per cent of GDP.

The figures underscore the pressure of rising debt-servicing costs on the Federal Government’s fiscal position, with interest payments exceeding revenue and reported capital spending accounting for a smaller share of economic output.

World.title: Tinubu’s re-election crucial to Nigeria’s prosperity – Hamzat
World.content:
The Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat, says re-election of President Bola Tinubu and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates will be crucial to achieving the prosperity Nigerians desire.

Hamzat, who is also the APC governorship candidate in Lagos State for the 2027 general elections, spoke during the inauguration of the PBAT/KOH Lagos Central Campaign Office on Harden Str. Lagos Island on Monday.

He urged Lagos residents, particularly those in the Lagos Central Senatorial District, to turn out in large numbers to vote for Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections.

The deputy governor said residents have a responsibility to support the President’s re-election, noting that Tinubu’s longstanding political connection to Lagos State made its support particularly significant.

He added that re-electing the President would ensure continuity in the work his administration had begun.

Hamzat noted that Lagos had the highest number of registered voters in the country, stressing the need to translate the figures into actual votes to achieve the desired electoral outcome.

“We are commissioning this office today to take our campaign to the grassroots. We know Lagos Island has been doing really well in voting but that is not enough, as many people still do not vote.

“We are here to mobilise residents to come out and vote for our President because he is one of us.

“We must demonstrate our support by voting for his re-election so that he can continue the good works he has started,” he said.

Hamzat also urged party members to encourage residents to participate in the elections, citing Osun, where he said about 54 per cent of registered voters participated in the last election, as an example of the need to improve voter turnout.

The deputy governor urged the party members to mobilise others to vote, emphasising that political support must be demonstrated through participation at the polls.

“My charge to you is that, as you are all seated here today, on election day, make sure you take someone along to the polling unit to vote for Tinubu.

“It will be dangerous for us not to come out and vote for all our candidates if we truly say we love them,” Hamzat said.

The Lagos State Chairman of the APC, Pastor Cornelius Ojelabi, said the campaign office would serve as a strategic platform for strengthening ties between the senatorial district and the state leadership.

Ojelabi said the office would also facilitate the dissemination of the party’s policies and achievements across local governments, wards and polling units.

He urged party members to serve as ambassadors by taking the messages on the achievements of Tinubu and Gov. Babajide Sanwo-Olu to the grassroots.

Ojelabi also encouraged members who were yet to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) to do so promptly, while calling for peaceful campaigns, constructive, issue-based engagement and effective voter mobilisation ahead of the elections.

Sen. Wasiu Eshilokun-Sanni, representing Lagos Central Senatorial District, described the inauguration of the campaign office as a historic milestone and a symbol of unity, peace and the party’s determination to consolidate its achievements.

Eshilokun-Sanni urged party members and supporters to remain united in spite of their differences, engage constructively with their neighbours and maintain discipline throughout the electioneering process.

He called for grassroots mobilisation and a stronger party presence across communities, markets and households.

He expressed confidence that sustained engagement would help the APC achieve its electoral objectives in Lagos Central, Lagos State and Nigeria.

Earlier, in his address, the Director-General of the PBAT/KOH Lagos Campaign Organisation, Sen. Musiliu Obanikoro, described the inauguration of the Lagos central senatorial campaign office as a reaffirmation of the district’s political significance and strategic importance to the APC.

Obanikoro said the facility underscored the party’s commitment to strengthening its political structures and consolidating its presence across the senatorial district.

He urged party members and supporters to intensify campaign activities and grassroots mobilisation in support of Tinubu’s re-election and the electoral success of other APC candidates in the forthcoming elections.

(NAN)

World.title: NAPTIP ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‍​‌‍⁠‍​‌​receives 105 Nigerians rescued from Ghana cybercrime syndicates
World.content:
The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP) says it has received 105 Nigerians rescued in a coordinated operation against cybercrime syndicates in Ghana.

A statement issued on Monday by the agency’s Head of Press and Public Relations Unit, Mr Vincent Adekoye, says the rescue operation was in tandem with President Bola Tinubu’s citizen-focused policies.

Adekoye said that the operation was coordinated by the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) after the Cyber Security Authority of Ghana contacted NAPTIP.

He said that NAPTIP led the participating Nigerian Security and Law Enforcement agencies, including the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS), the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons (NCFRMI).

Others are the Department of State Services (DSS), the National Intelligence Agency (NIA), the Nigerian High Commission in Ghana, and the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria.

He said that the development was hailed by a cross-section of stakeholders, including Civil Society Organisations and collaborating international organisations.

Adekoye said the development underscored the commitment of the Federal Government of Nigeria to the safety of Nigerians, especially victims of human trafficking and irregular migration.

He quoted the Ghanaian government as saying that 119 Nigerians were rescued during the operation, of which 105 were repatriated, while the remaining 14 are being processed.

The statement also quoted the Director-General of NAPTIP, Hajia Binta Adamu-Bello, while receiving the survivors on-behalf of the Federal Government welcomed the returnees and assured them of their safety.

She encouraged them to remain calm while the Federal Government carries out profiling and reintegration processes, adding that NAPTIP’s engagement with the returnees reflected the agency’s commitment to protecting their dignity.

Adamu-Bello said that NAPTIP was committed to safeguarding their welfare and ensuring that each person received assistance suited to their individual circumstances.

She expressed NAPTIP’s appreciation to the Ghanaian authorities, particularly the Cyber Security Authority of Ghana, Ghana Immigration Service, and the United Kingdom’s National Crime Agency (NCA) for its operational support.

“The agency specially thanks the Office of the National Security Adviser, Nigerian security and law enforcement agencies, and all partners whose collaboration made the operation a huge success.

“NAPTIP reaffirms its commitment to strengthening national and international cooperation against human trafficking and related forms of exploitation.

“It will continue to ensure that individuals identified during such operations receive appropriate screening, protection and support according to their circumstances,” Adamu-Bello said.

The NAPTIP boss urged Nigerians to exercise serious caution when considering employment, scholarships or other opportunities abroad.

He specifically warned Nigerians to beware of offers that make unrealistic promises, give vague job descriptions, or involve suspicious recruitment arrangements.

(NAN)

World.title: Obasanjo urges increase in 13% derivation for oil-producing states
World.content:
Former President Olusegun Obasanjo on Monday advocated an increase in the 13 per cent derivation allocated to oil-producing states.

Obasanjo ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‍​‍​⁠‌⁠‌​spoke at the inauguration of the Crude Distillation Unit (CDU) of Azikel Refinery at Obunagha, Yenagoa Local Government Area of Bayelsa.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the one-billion-dollar refinery project is owned by Azikel Petroleum, under the Azikel Group.

The refinery is expected to produce 2.5 million litres of petrol and two million litres of diesel daily, alongside other petroleum products.

Obasanjo commended Azikel Group President, Dr Azibapu Eruani, for initiating the project and urged him to ensure its completion within 12 months.

He also appreciated the refinery’s technical and engineering team, African Finance Corporation (AFC) and Afreximbank for supporting the project.

The former president called for continued support to facilitate the refinery’s completion, noting that its development had progressed significantly since his previous visit.

Obasanjo also commended Gov. Douye Diri of Bayelsa for supporting the project and effectively utilising the state’s revenue, citing numerous development projects.

“I have told Dr Eruani that I will be officially 90 years by next March. It means I will take the boarding pass soon.

“He has to make sure the project is completed before I exit,” he said.

Addressing Diri, Obasanjo said Eruani had consistently acknowledged the governor’s critical contribution to the refinery project.

“You are right that the states and oil-producing communities have not got a fair deal so far. Thirteen per cent is the beginning.

“You can continue to talk. The most important thing is that even the little you have received, you have used it well,” he said.

Obasanjo challenged Eruani to complete the refinery within the next 12 months, adding that its capacity could subsequently be doubled.

Speaking earlier, Eruani said the refinery would kick-start industrialisation in Bayelsa and the wider Niger Delta region.

He recalled that Obasanjo laid the refinery’s foundation eight years ago, describing the installation of the CDU as a major step toward completing the project.

Eruani said the refinery was conceived to make the Niger Delta an active participant in the petroleum industry.

He described it as the country’s second-largest full-scale refinery and commended President Bola Tinubu for supporting indigenous refineries.

According to him, local refining aligns with the Federal Government’s vision of making petroleum products available and affordable.

Eruani also appreciated Diri, AFC and Afreximbank for their contributions to the project.

In his remarks, Diri said the refinery vindicated years of agitation by Niger Delta communities against perceived injustice in the petroleum industry.

He argued that communities producing crude oil deserved to become key participants in the industry and benefit more substantially from their natural resources.

The governor criticised the Land Use Act and the existing 13 per cent derivation formula, insisting that oil-producing states deserved a greater share of their resources.

“The Land Use Act is unfair. Surface resources belong to states, but what lies underneath belongs to the Federal Government.

“That law is obnoxious and not good for any just society,” he said.

Diri said the region was not seeking to take everything for itself but wanted to participate meaningfully in decisions concerning its resources.

“We do not want to take all to ourselves. We just want to be co-players in determining how it is done. Thirteen per cent is not enough for the states,” he said.

The governor expressed delight that the refinery would position Bayelsans to participate more actively in the petroleum industry.

He urged residents to equip themselves with the necessary skills to benefit from the opportunities the project would create.

Diri also stressed that Africa must process its own natural resources to maximise their economic benefits.

He called on oil companies operating in the Gbarain/Obunagha area to complement the state government’s efforts by rehabilitating the road leading to the refinery.

(NAN)

World.title: Domo Reinvents Corporate Retreat  In Lekki
World.content:
Bennett Oghifo

In a bustling city like Lagos that moves at full speed almost all round the clock, Domo, an urban retreat, offers you a refreshing sanctuary-something unique and increasingly rare: the space to pause tucked away from the distracting crowd.

Powered by an impressive assemblage of top notch facilities, Domo goes well beyond the norms but gives the beholder a holistic event with a range of curated experiences in an environment just for your team. It supports fun, focus and results.

Located in a tranquil environment at 12/14, Meadow Hall Way in Elegbusi -Lekki, about 30 minutes from the business districts of Victoria Island and Ikoyi, Domo is a small-scale urban retreat designed for corporate teams who want more than a conventional hotel meeting. It is close enough to be practical for a working day, yet deliberately removed from the noise, traffic and routine that can prevent people from thinking clearly.

Domo was created around a shared philosophy found in Edo and Japanese culture: respect for nature, precision, balance and beauty with purpose. It shapes the experience of the your stay – from the quiet rhythm of the Japanese-inspired garden and koi pond to the spacious apartments, considered interiors, restorative wellness treatments and Nigerian-Japanese cuisine at Edo Restaurant.

Unlike a regular hotel, DOMO is not built around crowds, busy lobbies or generic event rooms. Its scale is its strength. When your company comes to DOMO, the experience feels personal, focused and private. Your team has room to meet, share meals, recharge and reconnect in one coherent setting – without the distractions of a large, impersonal venue.

Whether for a leadership retreat, strategy session, workshop or team appreciation program, DOMO can create a tailor-made half-day or multi-day experience. A unique combination of meeting space, accommodation in spacious and luxurious apartments, dining with a relaxing view on the Japanese garden and spa treatments. But Domo offers more: a large collection of relaxation and team-building activities can be brought together around one aim: helping your team members to return to work with greater clarity, connection and energy.

DOMO is also an amazing and special location to relax with your partner, family and friends. Relax in our garden, at the poolside, in your luxurious apartment, or whilst enjoying treatments at the Ehima Cave Spa. The Edo Restaurant, which also serves a Sunday Brunch, and a special Japanese-Nigerian Fusion menu will make you want to come back for more.

World.title: Nigeria to Host World Polo Championship Qualifiers in Abuja November
World.content:
Oghenevwede Ohwovoriole in Abuja

The Nigerian Polo Association (NPA), has disclosed that it will host the World’s Polo championship qualifications in Nigeria between November 9 and 16, 2026, in Abuja.

The NPA Chairman, Suleman Abubakar, made the disclosure yesterday in Abuja when he and his team paid a courtesy call on the Chairman of the National Sports Commission (NSC), Malam Shehu Dikko, to intimate him on the hosting right given to Nigeria.

Abubakar said the hosting right was given to Nigeria because of the efforts made by the Association and Nigeria.

“The Nigerian Polo Association, I think the world has recognised the efforts of our administration, and they have granted us the right to host the World Polo Championship qualifiers for the first time in over 120 years of polo in Nigeria.

“This is a result of the efforts of our association and in recognition of the efforts that the chairman and his team, and indeed the country are making around the world. So, it is an announcement that indeed the world is taking note of Nigeria and the progress we are making, and they have granted us an opportunity,” he said.

The championships will take place in Abuja at the Guards Polo Club. Participating countries include; India, Iran, Pakistan, and the host nation, Nigeria in the constituted Zone E of the Federation of International Polo.

“There are 12 member-countries in Zone E, but only four of us have achieved this sort of level of advancement in our polo development to qualify at a graded handicap of 14 handicaps,” Abubakar explained.

He also noted that it was of great importance to brief the Chairman of NSC for assistance and support of the Commission, including granting considerable resources to help the NPA to promote the event that is of national and international significance.

In his response, the Dikko, assured him of the Commission’s support, saying, “it is quite exciting for us that now Nigeria is going to host the international polo tournament of this magnitude.”

Dikko added, “So, it is quite congratulatory for getting this opportunity. And I can tell you indeed what you are doing clearly speaks to what we are trying to do at the National Sports Commission. It is natural for us to see what we can do to provide you whatever is necessary we can, and whatever support we can within our own limited abilities to make sure this a success. We will not see it as just a polo association event. it is a Nigerian event and make it a brilliant event.”

Dikko noted that the NSC did not just see it as just as hosting an event, adding that it was also an economy in itself.

In her remarks, the Administrative Manager, NPA, Abari Anama, said, “The NPA is also considering opening a youth academy, so that they can also develop young players in the sport in the mould of Campioso or “Valentina, who started as a farm boy, and today sits in the Royal Box in the British Games International.”

World.title: Super Falcons Set to Seal Ticket to Third Round as Morocco Awaits Nigeria
World.content:
Nigeria’s Super Falcons expect to seal a place in the third of the five-round African qualification series for the 2028 Olympics Women’s Football Tournament when they confront Comoros senior women national team for the second time in four days time.

Goals by defender Michelle Alozie and forward Uchenna Kanu earned the 10-time African champions a 2-0 win on Friday, leaving them with an advantage as they push for a second successive appearance at the Olympics, after participating at the Paris 2024 Games – their first in 16 years.

The Indian Ocean islanders’ lack of a CAF-approved venue for international matches meant Nigeria have home advantage for both games of the fixture, at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne-Remo.

On Friday, interim Head Coach Augustine Eguavoen and his assistants opted to deploy Chiamaka Nnadozie in goal, with Glory Ogbonna and Michelle Alozie as wing-backs, and Christy Ucheibe and Shukurat Oladipo as centre-backs. Debutant Joy Igbokwe, Toni Payne and Jennifer Echegini were in midfield and captain Rasheedat Ajibade, Gift Monday and Uchenna Kanu were at the fore.

On Tuesday, the coaching crew may decide to try youngster Christiana Uzoma in goal, with the likes of Farida Abdulwahab and Tumininu Adeshina also available for defensive duties. Suliat Abideen was impressive when she came on in the second period on Friday, and could be given a starting role this time.

Former U17 team captain Shakirat Moshood and Folashade Ijamilusi are options at the fore, as well as Blessing Nkor and Blessing Okpe who both play in Belarus, and Sweden-based Joy Omewa.

The third-round fixture against Morocco will hold in March 2027.

World.title: Basketball Africa League Unveils Refurbished Courts in Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire, Senegal
World.content:
The Basketball Africa League (BAL), last weekend announced that the league is unveiling six newly refurbished basketball courts in Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire and Senegal in support of NBA Africa’s commitment to build or renovate 1,000 courts across the continent over the next decade.

Collectively, the courts are expected to reach thousands of youth and community members annually.

The first two courts were unveiled Sept. 30 in Saint-Louis, Senegal, in collaboration with Senegalese national oil and gas company Société des Pétroles du Sénégal (PETROSEN), and Oct. 3 in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, in collaboration with Wave Côte d’Ivoire.

Additional courts will be unveiled through December in Dakar, Senegal, in collaboration with Ville de Dakar; in Joal, Senegal in collaboration with Woodside Energy; and in Guédiawaye, Senegal, and Owerri, Nigeria, in collaboration with Qatar Foundation.

Each court features upgraded playing surfaces, spectator seating and new basketball stanchions, with select sites also featuring modernized changing rooms, sanitation facilities, and lighting.

“These newly refurbished courts reflect our commitment to investing in communities and making the game more accessible to young people across Africa,” said BAL President Amadou Gallo Fall. “Together with our partners, we are creating spaces where the next generation of African basketball players, fans, and changemakers can grow, connect and thrive,” he stated.

Marking the second BAL4HER court in Africa, the court unveiling will be supported by two-time WNBA All-Star and BAL Ambassador Chiney Ogwumike and her nonprofit organization, Queens of the Continent.

The court currently serves more than 300 participants across Imo State. The upgrades, including renovated changing rooms and bathrooms, improved lighting and enhanced drainage, will transform a gathering space into a dedicated venue for organized sport, youth development and community engagement.

The Basketball Africa League (BAL), a partnership between the International Basketball Federation (FIBA) and NBA Africa, is a professional league featuring 12 club teams from across Africa that concluded its sixth season in May 2026.

World.title: Arsenal Fans Club Nigeria Set for Official Launch in Abuja
World.content:
*Kanu, Saraki, Emir Sanusi, Dino Melaye, other supporters lined up to grace the ceremony

Marvelous David

Arsenal Fans Club Nigeria is set to be officially unveiled in Abuja this weekend, as the organisation prepares to strengthen the club’s fan base and promote community development through football.

Amongst the high profile personalities lined up for the unveiling ceremony include, business leaders, celebrities and notable Arsenal supporters like former Gunner, Kanu Nwankwo, former Senate President Bukola Saraki, Emir Sanusi Lamido Sanusi, Senator Dino Melaye amongst others.

The unveiling will form part of a two-day programme beginning on Friday, October 16, with delegates from state and city chapters expected to converge on the nation’s capital for the club’s second Annual General Meeting (AGM).

According to a press release issued on Monday by the organisation, the celebrations will feature sporting activities, a community sanitation initiative and a formal launch event attended by prominent personalities and Arsenal supporters.

National President of Arsenal Fans Club Nigeria, Charles Ojugbana, said the organisation draws inspiration from the achievements of Nigerian-descent footballers, including former Super Eagles striker Kanu Nwankwo and current stars Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze.

The former General Secretary of the Nigeria Football Association (NFA) said the club aims to improve the football fan experience while expanding support for Arsenal across Nigeria.

Activities scheduled for Saturday include aerobic sessions and a novelty football match before members proceed to Wuse Market for a clean-up campaign.

As part of the outreach, the club plans to donate refuse bins and other sanitation materials to the market’s leadership, in line with its commitment to philanthropy and community development.

Arsenal Fans Club Nigeria operates through a governance structure comprising a Board of Trustees, a National Executive Committee and a General Assembly, which serves as the organisation’s highest decision-making body.

The club also disclosed plans to promote awareness of Down syndrome among children in March 2027, as part of activities to commemorate World Down Syndrome Day.

The programme expresses the organisation’s ambition to extend its activities beyond football fandom to charitable causes and support for vulnerable members of society.

World.title: Atlético Coach Defends Misfiring Ademola Lookman, Says It’s a Phase
World.content:
*Warns that Red Devils sluggish EPL form not reason to be taken for granted

Duro Ikhazuagbe with agency report

Ahead of tonight’s UEFA Champions League league phase clash between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United at the Metropolitano, Head Coach of the Spanish outfit, Diego Simeone, has come to the defence of his misfiring Nigerian international, Ademola Lookman.

The Argentine gaffer stressed that what Lookman has been passing through while another player (Álex Baena) is excelling is nothing unusually.

“Every player goes through their own phases, obviously, I don’t think there’s a player who can maintain a level of 10 all the time,” Simeone explained. “There’s always a dip, and it’s clear that Ademola Lookman is going through a phase where he’s not performing as he’d like to and as we’d like to see him, because he’s shown us what he’s capable of, but he works every day to become that player, the dribbler.

Simeone however restated that the Super Eagles forward must strive to be at his best after this phase this season.

“He needs to keep dribbling, he needs to lose the ball, he needs to keep pushing forward, because he’ll do well, because he’s got what it takes and because he’s a goalscorer,” emphasised the coach.

He poured encomiums on Baena for keeping the flag flying at Atlético.

“Álex Baena, on the other hand, comes from a different situation: a season marred by injuries, perhaps not as consistent as he would have liked in his first season,” Simeone continued. “(He’s since demonstrated) a world-class performance, confidence, assurance, a great run of form, and (I’m) trying to manage the best moments of each player for the good of the team.”

On tonight’s clash with Manchester United, Simeone speaks on why Atlético need to pick up points in the Champions League

“We know the difficulties of this competition. This format means you have to try to pick up points, whether at home or away, in the first match or the last. We need points, just as every team that wants to stay in this competition does.”

“I think, as I was saying after Saturday’s match, we read the game very well. We played well on Saturday and tomorrow (Tuesday) we’ll be facing an opponent who apply great pressure in your half, very good pressure, very aggressive, very intense, with very precise movements to buy time when pressing high. And they’ve got quick players, as Dávid Hancko rightly pointed out; regardless of the results, which have mostly been draws for them so far this season, they’re producing the same kind of performance they did last year. It’s Manchester United, a strong side, but we’ll have to steer the match in a direction where we believe we can cause them problems.

World.title: WHY ARE GOVERNORS GETTING WORSE?
World.content:
PAUL C NWABUIKWU reckons that Nigerians are not impressed by the current set of governors across the country

The 4th Republic kicked off in 1999 with a bunch of impressive governors across the country. In Cross River, 37-year-old Donald Duke turned the famous hospitality of his people into a highly effective revenue generating strategy after the state lost its oil wells to Akwa Ibom via a Supreme Court judgement. Within a couple of years, the state became a favourite destination for government and private sector conferees as well as local and foreign tourists. In Bauchi, the urbane Muazu did similarly innovative things with the Yankari Game Reserve but also left notable legacies in education (increasing primary school enrolment from under 500,000 to over 1.2m; taking Bauchi from 34th to 3rd in WAEC) in addition to massive road construction.

In Enugu, the Chimaroke Nnamani era will forever be tarnished by widespread state-sponsored violence against opponents but even he notched up some significant milestones in health and education including ESUT medical school. Rabiu Kwankwaso, also stood out in scholarships and establishment of educational infrastructure and granting of scholarships. Victor Attah achieved regional impact as Mr Resource Control for his principled advocacy for a larger share of the cake for the South South. Kogi’s late governor, the mercurial Abubakar Audu is still considered by many the state’s best so far. This is by no means an exhaustive list.

Babatunde Fashola was outstanding among the second set of governors elected in 2007. He accomplished great things in urban renewal, infrastructural development and administrative innovation. His can-do approach and a methodical approach famously described by Soyinka as the methodical approach of a“skilled mechanic” continues to be a reference point. Sadly, under Buhari, he was far from a star in Works and Housing. The late Daura general cum president had a talent for dimming any stars that strayed into his firmament.

Peter Obi, despite the disruption of two impeachments by a state legislature captured by Chris Uba, left arguably the best legacy in the history of the state in a multiplicity of areas: education, investment, prudent and innovative governance in many areas. A couple of other governors in the 2007 set also left strong records, including Sullivan Chime in Enugu (roads, security, investments) and Godswill Akpabio (transformative infrastructure) in Akwa Ibom.

The current set of governors, as a group, are, by comparison, quite disappointing. If a poll on the performance of governors across the country is conducted today, it will, no doubt, confirm that Nigerians are unimpressed by the current occupants of government houses across the country. And that’s putting it mildly. A significant percentage of the curses and “fire prayers” that Nigerians hurl at politicians daily are directed at governors. Apart from a few exceptions, the public perception is that they are ineffective money-miss-roads who hide their incompetence behind a phalanx of sycophantic aides, long convoys and elaborate titles including the redundant “Executive Governor”. Alex Otti of Abia is, of course, a notable exception.

And there’s little evidence the majority of governors are doing anything significant with the huge increases in the allocations they are receiving from FAAC. However, no doubt, bureau de change operators and other key players in the lucrative forex supply chain are enjoying the benefits that Their Excellencies are denying indigenes and residents.

A thought: perhaps the reason many governors insist on being addressed as “Executive Governor” is because they know, deep down in their underperforming hearts, that they are doing very little useful execution outside the elaborate façade. Some time ago, a now deceased former Oyo State governor added a comical dimension to this craze for titles when he reminded the audience, in the course of tense confrontation with students, that he was not only the Executive Governor but also the living and breathing Constituted Authority, the embodiment of all official and terrestrial power within the geographical boundaries of the state. The expression of power in Third World democracies is often blunt and very blunt.

There are many other examples of similar actions and statements by imperial gubernatorial majesties. In August 2025, Governor Mohammed Umar Bago of Niger State ordered the shutdown of Badeggi FM, a private radio station in Minna for daring to highlight lapses in the state’s security operations. In another controversial incident captured in a viral video, Bago instructed a security detail to slap an Islamic cleric during a public event for the crime of “impersonating” an Imam.

Former Ebonyi governor and current works minister, Dave Umahi earned similar notoriety during his spell as governor. For instance, he didn’t bother to hide his hostility and disdain for media platforms which dared to publish anything that did not meet his specifications. He often ordered the arrest and detention of journalists from such media platforms. In some cases, he banned them “for life” from entering Government House, Abakaliki. As he declared during a public event at Abakaliki: “If you think you have the pen, we have the koboko (horsewhip).”

It would be interesting to find out if Umahi’s successor is keeping faith with the decision of his cantankerous godfather. If so, will the state house of assembly explore enacting a law to ensure that the life ban remains in effect even if the reporters outlive their excellencies? The possibilities are ridiculously endless.

Bago and Umahi are, of course, not the only governors in the category largely defined in the public space by arbitrary exercise of power rather than public service. There are quite a few others.

The obvious question: what is responsible for the decline in the quality of governors? What accounts for the downward trajectory in performance? Naturally, many explanations have been offered. One theory articulated by a friend is that the progressive decline in governance can be traced to the progressive decline in the quality of the public service since independence. According to him, the failure of successive leaders to maintain the standards bequeathed by the British is responsible for the across-the-board deterioration in many facets of national life. This reminds of Achebe’s assertion in his book, There Was a Country that, while colonialism was inspired and sustained by exploitation, the British left a decent foundation of institutions and policies that Nigerian leaders failed to build on.

Some have also suggested that escalating corruption is responsible for the decline in the performance of governors. Those who hold this view say that the Second Republic which the military toppled because of massive corruption is a tea party compared to what obtains today. Most governors, so the theory goes, are so focused on stealing that there is no appetite or space left for governance. The problem with this theory can be compared to the problem of the chicken and the egg: which came first?

These theories may have some tangential relevance but the most persuasive explanation for the decline in the performance of elected state executives, in my opinion, is that godfathers across the country have learnt a negative lesson from their post 1999 experience with godsons who became governors. The lesson is: it is safer and more profitable to support underachieving individuals with little or no capacity into Government House than to support capable and high performing godsons who can become difficult to control after becoming popular and earning public goodwill in their own right.

Godfathers seem to have learnt that mumu godsons are better “sure bankers” than independent minded “I too know” godsons. It’s a very cynical view but in a political system in which thuggery, rigging and other machinations often decide electoral outcomes, godfathers who pull the strings can get away with this calculation. The results can be seen in states like Edo, Ebonyi and Kogi where obedient godsons are officially in charge but powerful godfathers hold the aces. The situation in Rivers where Sim Fubara tried and failed to shake off Nyesom Wike has strengthened such calculations and the influence of godfathers.

*Nwabuikwu is a member of THISDAY Editorial Board

World.title: AKPABIO AND PARLIAMENTARY DIPLOMACY
World.content:
The election of a new IPU President provides useful moment for the National Assembly, contends KEN HARRIES

Nigeria’s President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, was at his parliamentary diplomacy best at the 153rd Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) Assembly in Arusha, Tanzania, on Friday, 9 October 2026. He reached deep into his parliamentary tool kit to muster support for Mr. Milton Dick, Speaker of Australia’s House of Representatives, who emerged as the organisation’s 32nd President, securing 56 per cent of the votes in a three-candidate contest. Dick succeeds Dr Tulia Ackson of Tanzania, whose three-year tenure concluded with the Assembly.

The event offers a timely opportunity to examine the place of Nigerian parliamentary diplomacy in global affairs. The significance of the election for Nigeria extends beyond the person of the successful candidate. It lies in Nigeria’s diplomatic engagement in support of his candidacy, its efforts to rally parliamentary partners around a shared choice and the opportunity to translate those relationships into enduring national and continental influence.

The Nigerian dimension of this development centres on Akpabio, who is also Chairman of the National Assembly and a member of the IPU Executive Committee. His position within the organisation gives Nigeria an institutional platform from which to contribute to its direction and cultivate relationships across its membership.

Before the election, Mr Dick visited Abuja to solicit the support of the Nigerian Parliament. Akpabio assured him of Nigeria’s backing and pledged to advocate for his candidacy within the African Group of the IPU. The engagement also addressed stronger Nigeria–Australia cooperation in mining, agriculture, education, renewable energy, technology, security and capacity building. Support for an international candidacy thus became an occasion to explore a broader bilateral relationship.

That engagement illustrates an important principle of parliamentary diplomacy: influence is often exercised before a vote is cast. It begins with consultations, the cultivation of confidence, the identification of shared interests and the ability to bring stakeholders into a common conversation. In multilateral institutions, where countries bring competing priorities and perspectives to the table, the capacity to facilitate consensus can be consequential.

Nigeria’s support and its commitment to mobilising African backing belong within that diplomatic context. The election was conducted by secret ballot; its result does not disclose how individual delegates voted or permit a precise calculation of Nigeria’s contribution. Nigeria’s initiative can therefore be recognised without attributing the outcome to any single country.

The importance of the initiative lies in Nigeria’s willingness to move from institutional presence to purposeful engagement: taking a position, reaching out to partners and helping build support around it.

The Inter-Parliamentary Union’s relevance to Nigeria is practical. Peace and security, migration, climate change, economic inequality, technological disruption and the protection of democratic institutions cannot be addressed exclusively through domestic legislation. They require international cooperation, to which parliaments contribute through legislation, oversight, representation and the exchange of policy experience.

Parliamentary diplomacy also creates channels of communication that can remain useful when political differences complicate relations between governments. The deliberations in Arusha reflected this broader purpose. The Assembly’s theme—Enhancing good governance and empowering communities through inclusivity, trust and opportunities for all—connected international parliamentary dialogue to the everyday responsibilities of legislatures: ensuring that public institutions respond to the people they represent.

One of the most important dimensions of the Nigerian engagement is the effort to mobilise support through the African Group of the IPU. The Group comprises 52-member parliaments, providing a substantial platform for continental cooperation. Its size, however, should not be mistaken for an automatic voting bloc or agreement on every issue.

Nigeria’s demographic scale, regional relationships and experience in multilateral engagement give it a basis for contributing to such coordination. But leadership within a continental grouping must be earned through consultation, credibility, respect for other members and a willingness to pursue shared objectives beyond individual contests.

Nigeria’s engagement at the IPU is not occurring in an institutional vacuum. The National Assembly’s wider international parliamentary relationships provide channels for legislative cooperation, capacity building and regional dialogue. Akpabio’s membership of the IPU Executive Committee adds a further dimension to that engagement, placing Nigeria within an important part of the organisation’s governance structure.

Such positions offer access to discussions, relationships and institutional processes. But access is only the starting point. The real test is whether it produces benefits that can be identified and sustained.

Those benefits may include stronger legislative cooperation, improved oversight practices, exchanges on economic reform and digital governance, and greater visibility for Nigerian and African policy priorities. Where discussions concern education, technology or investment, parliamentary relationships can help open doors and encourage follow-through by the relevant public institutions and private-sector partners.

The distinction between representation and results is crucial. A parliament may attend high-level assemblies and occupy positions within international bodies, yet fail to realise their full value if engagement is episodic, poorly coordinated or disconnected from domestic priorities.

The election of a new IPU President provides a useful moment for the National Assembly under Akpabio’s leadership to consolidate its parliamentary diplomacy.

First, participation in international institutions should be linked to defined national objectives. Policy briefs, negotiation priorities and mechanisms for reporting outcomes would give delegations a clearer mandate and enable the legislature and the public to assess what their engagements achieve.

Second, consultations with African parliamentary partners should continue beyond electoral contests. Common positions do not require uniformity on every question. They require the discipline to identify shared interests, respect differences and coordinate where cooperation can deliver practical value.

Third, international parliamentary relationships should feed into domestic legislative work. Exchanges on budget scrutiny, public accountability, digital governance, climate legislation and institutional transparency become useful when the lessons are examined by relevant committees and adapted to Nigerian circumstances.

Fourth, the professional capacity supporting parliamentary diplomacy should be strengthened. Research, international law, protocol, strategic communication, negotiation and regional expertise are indispensable to effective engagement. Personal relationships can open doors, but institutions must sustain the work beyond the tenure of individual office holders.

Finally, Nigeria should measure the results of its international engagements. The relevant questions are whether it advanced identifiable interests, secured commitments, opened avenues for cooperation or contributed to improvements in legislative practice and governance.

These measures would give continuity to the diplomatic initiative surrounding Dick’s candidacy and help embed parliamentary diplomacy more firmly within national strategy.

Milton Dick’s emergence as President of the IPU offers Nigeria a moment to reflect on the strategic possibilities of parliamentary diplomacy. Akpabio’s engagement with the Australian Speaker and his commitment to mobilising African support illustrate the importance of consultation and relationship building in multilateral affairs.

The country has an opportunity to exercise influence through the purposeful use of its democratic institutions and leadership. Its parliament can serve as a bridge between domestic priorities and international deliberations, between national interests and continental cooperation, and between political representation and the practical work of multilateral engagement.

In the final analysis, diplomacy is not merely the art of being present where decisions are made. It is the capacity to contribute meaningfully to the conversations that shape those decisions, while remaining faithful to the interests and responsibilities one represents.

For Nigeria, the task is to turn institutional access into strategic engagement, strategic engagement into practical cooperation, and practical cooperation into lasting public value.

That is the promise of parliamentary diplomacy—and the standard by which Nigeria’s influence in the international parliamentary community should ultimately be judged.

· Harries Esq is an Abuja- based development communication expert.

World.title: Mbuso Zulu on growing up in a ‘family of prisoners’ even his grandmother [video]
World.content:
In a resurfaced clip from Skeem GP’s podcast, Mbuso Zulu, an ex-convict from KwaZulu-Natal, revealed that he and most of his paternal family members, including his grandmother, father, and uncle, have been imprisoned at some point in their lives.

FAMILY OF PRISONERS

In a Facebook clip shared by Chromocloud, Zulu told Skeem GP that although he does not blame his father for his criminal past, it was the stories he heard about his father’s influence that ultimately drove him down that path.

Mbuso’s grandparents were hardly around during his childhood. His grandmother was sentenced to 10 years in prison for selling marijuana, while his grandfather was often away because he was a polygamist.



This vacuum forced his father, Mafuku Themba Ncanana, to embrace crime as a means of survival, since his own mother was now imprisoned.

Ncanana was already serving his 15-year prison sentence when Mbuso was born. His crimes included business robberies and cash-in-transit heists.

According to Mbuso, he grew up around drugs and AK-47 firearms, which his father kept at home.

LIFE AFTER PRISON

Mbuso’s life has taken a positive turn since his release in September 2024. The 34-year-old recently joined SABC 1’s Uzalo as Cash Money.

He has also established the Usengashintsha Foundation and serves as a brand ambassador for Xap Xap Clothing.

Before his father passed away, Mbuso said he always encouraged him to prioritise education, as he did not wish his son to follow in his footsteps.

World.title: Bernard Parker drops bombshells about marriage, ‘addictions’
World.content:
Bernard Parker has dropped a bombshell statement about his private life. Images via IG

Former Bafana Bafana player and current TS Galaxy head coach Bernard Parker has dropped a bombshell about his personal life, including that he has a relationship with another woman, who is not his wife, Wendy Parker.

The retired Kaizer Chiefs player also confessed to having an “addiction” that has impacted his life and loved ones.

The shock statement comes on the eve of TS Galax’s clash against Orlando Pirates on Tuesday, 13 October.



BERNARD PARKER DROPS BOMBSHELL STATEMENT

On his social media platforms, Bernard Parker posted a statement announcing his split from a woman named Kacha Stepanovic.

The 40-year-old claimed to have been in a three-year relationship with the businesswoman, who is the ex-wife of Teargas member Ntukza, also known as Bantu Hanaba.

Bernard – who has two sons with wife Wendy Parker – admitted to having six children, whom he would continue to coparent with Kacha.

Bernard Parker hinted at having been unfaithful to Kacha, who is half Serbian.

He shared: “I want to be honest about my part in our journey. I have made mistakes and struggled with personal addictions that have affected my life and the people I love.

“Kacha, I’m truly sorry for the times I hurt you, let you down, and caused you pain. You gave me love, support, patience and kindness that I’ve never received before. I take responsibility for my mistakes, knowing that some things cannot simply be undone with an apology”



He added: “Thank you for the 3 years, the memories, the lessons, the love, and for being part of my story. I will always respect you as the mother of our children and appreciate the chapter we shared”

‼️Kaizer Chiefs legend and TS Galaxy coach, Bernard Parker, admits to personal addiction a day before playing Pirates‼️ pic.twitter.com/tffQtl4RSa — Xoli Zondo (BScHONS, MBA, PDM) (@XoliswaZondo) October 12, 2026

ADDICTED TO ADULTERY?

On her social media account, Kacha Stepanovic reposted Bernard Parker’s statement.



She also hinted at his alleged infidelity.

She shared on her IG Stories: “Lust and addiction will strip you of your family, your work, your name and everything you built.

“If betrayal was so easy, the devil would be next seated at the throne.. Make sure whatever you do is worth losing it all”.

Kacha is the ex-wife of muso Ntukza, the father of her two sons.

WHAT ABOUT WENDY PARKER?

Bernard Parker’s statement about his personal life and new relationship has left many asking – Where is his wife, Wendy Parker?

The former Bafana Bafana player and the Diski Divas reality TV star married in 2012 and have 2 sons together.

The couple’s last Instagram post together was in 2024 – just two years ago. They have made no mention of a divorce or separation.

Wait a minute 😳 this was 2024!! When did the 3 years start? Rather when did you end things eBoksburg? pic.twitter.com/LHsig48Kxm — Qiniso (@bosslady_za) October 12, 2026

Wendy still uses the IG handle @Mrs_WParker.

World.title: Planning a coastal trip? Here’s what Tuesday’s tides look like
World.content:
Tuesday’s high and low tide times for eight coastal locations across South Africa. Image: Unsplash

If you’re heading to the coast on Tuesday, check the tide times before planning your activities, as spring tides bring changes to water levels along South Africa’s coastline.

However, tides are only part of the picture. Wind, waves and swell and the shape of the seabed can also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.

When to expect the next spring tide

Spring tides are important to watch out for because they bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual, changing conditions along the coast.



The most recent spring tide coincided with the new moon on Saturday, 10 October. The next spring tide is expected around the full moon on Monday, 26 October 2026.

These changes can affect swimming, surfing, fishing and other coastal activities. Higher tides can cover rocks and reefs, while lower tides expose more of the shoreline.

Check the tide times and the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: ‘Orlando Pirates won’t win a trophy’ – Tso makes bold prediction
World.content:
Orlando Pirates legend Benedict ‘Tso’ Vilakazi has cast doubt on his former club’s chances of winning silverware this season following their MTN8 final defeat to Mamelodi Sundowns.

The Buccaneers suffered a 2-0 loss to the Brazilians, who claimed their first MTN8 title in five years.

Pirates enjoyed a successful campaign last season, winning a treble, but their hopes of defending their trophies have already suffered a setback.



With Sundowns showing impressive form, the Soweto giants face a tough challenge in their pursuit of more silverware.

Vilakazi, who has previously praised Abdeslam Ouaddou’s team, believes Pirates will struggle to win trophies this season, particularly if they come up against Sundowns in cup competitions.

“Orlando Pirates won’t win a trophy this season. My reason is I’ve watched Sundowns this season, especially their past two games against the champions of Saudi Arabia (Asia) and against Orlando Pirates in the MTN8 final. I don’t see any team stopping Pirates except for Sundowns,” he said on the Omniaudio Africa podcast.

Tso Vilakazi backs Sundowns to dominate over Orlando Pirates

Vilakazi went further, predicting that Sundowns would have the upper hand if the two teams meet again in a cup final.

“If Pirates play Sundowns, they will lose. I see Sundowns taking everything this season. If they play the way they are playing now, I don’t see anyone stopping them, including Pirates.

“I love Pirates with all of my heart and it is my home, but looking at Sundowns’ performance, they look unstoppable,” he added.



Orlando Pirates will now have to regroup after their MTN8 disappointment as they turn their attention to the remaining competitions.

Meanwhile, Sundowns will look to build on their cup success as they pursue further honours this season.

Will the Buccaneers end the season empty-handed?

World.title: SK Khoza delivers a riveting debut on ‘The Four of Us’ [video]
World.content:
Sthembiso SK Khoza has finally made his highly anticipated debut on e.tv’s The Four of Us, where he delivers a riveting debut as Hitman.

The telenovela, which replaced the long-running soap opera Scandal! in June 2026, is produced by the renowned Tshedza Pictures.

It boasts a star-studded cast including Sindi Dlathu, The Polygamist’s Sdumo Mtshali, Dumisani Dlamini, Thembinkosi Mthembu.



PAPI AND VLADIMIR RECONNECT

On Thursday evening, Papi received an unexpected visit from Vladimir, an old acquaintance flanked by two heavily armed bodyguards.

Vladimir had heard through the grapevine that Papi’s business was struggling, leading him to suggest taking down the “problematic” Hitman by stealing his brand-new bakkies.

However, Vladimir isn’t entirely genuine, as he expects a cut of the car sales, a condition Papi agrees to.



VLADIMIR’S NOT-SO-TRUSTED SPY

Vladimir’s “trusted” inside man within Hitman’s camp, Cobra, tipped him off that the camp recently hijacked a truck carrying new bakkies.

Vladimir then suggests to Papi that they steal the vehicles during the weekend, since Hitman will be at home in Bergville for an ancestral ceremony, which means his warehouse will be left unguarded.

SK KHOZA DELIVERS RIVETING DEBUT

A first look at Hitman already paints a dangerous picture of him. He is seen kicking and punching Cobra after discovering that he is Vladimir’s spy.



“So, you thought I didn’t know that you were Vladimir’s spy? That you’ve been following me around and snitching?” he asks.

Hitman then instructs his ally to contact MaNgwaneni back home and call off the traditional ceremony. Instead of killing Cobra, Hitman decides to use him as bail to get back at Papi and Vladimir.

Believing the warehouse is empty, Papi, Vladimir and their crew walk right into Hitman’s trap. When they realise the bakkies are not there, they immediately suspect there’s a traitor among them.



Thereafter, Hitman and his crew storm in and shoot Cobra, their spy. A deadly shootout soon erupts but comes to a halt when Hitman takes Papi’s brother-in-law hostage.

Confronted by his former protégé, Papi is forced to surrender and drop his gun.

Hitman then asks, “How do you feel right now? Your right-hand man, whom you taught everything, is about to kill you. I’m going to kill you today. How do you feel?”



Hitman then shoots Papi in the chest, but did he die?
