World.title: Estonia's bailiffs afraid for their safety, expect state to act
World.content:
Threats against bailiffs have become more frequent in Estonia. The Chamber of Bailiffs and Trustees in Bankruptcy calls for action from policymakers and the police.

There have been cases in Estonia in which bailiffs' property has suffered varying degrees of damage. The incidents do not always involve physical attacks, with bailiffs frequently facing insults, threats and humiliation. The situation has worsened in recent years, said Arvi Pink, a board member of the Chamber of Bailiffs and Trustees in Bankruptcy.

"The question here is how the state can assert its authority in such a situation. These 35 bailiffs are an integral part of our state governed by the rule of law," Pink said.

Pink added that while law enforcement agencies respond to physical violence, they tend not to respond to threats and intimidation.

"Is the attitude that this simply comes with the job and should be considered normal or is it actually unacceptable? Our position is that it is unacceptable," Pink stressed. He also gave an example.

"A mother of two receives a photo of knives and brass knuckles from a debtor who works as a butcher, along with a message saying, 'I intend to use these on you!' When we contacted law enforcement, the response was that this comes with our job, that it does not constitute a real threat and so on."

Police recommend reporting all threats, regardless of the circumstances. If there is an immediate danger, a police patrol should be called to the scene. In the case of a written threat, it should be documented and forwarded to the police who will then decide what action to take, explained Anders Allandi, head of the investigation unit at the Ida-Harju Police Station.

"If the elements of a criminal offense are present, we will initiate criminal proceedings. However, when it comes to threats, it is very important for an independent third party to assess the situation objectively and determine how credible the threat is and whether there is reason to believe it will actually be carried out. A bailiff's work is inherently somewhat confrontational: When an ordinary person faces debt collection proceedings, it creates tension and they may often make emotional statements that they do not necessarily mean," Allandi said.

In its appeal, the chamber also noted that bailiffs today face so-called sovereign citizens who believe that the government and other institutions constitute a "malicious elite" conspiring against citizens. As a result, sovereign citizens believe they are not obliged to comply with laws, regulations or court rulings. The Chamber of Bailiffs and Trustees in Bankruptcy stressed that this issue must be addressed and limits must be set.

"Bailiffs exercise public authority, which is state authority. If people are allowed to treat bailiffs the way they are sometimes treated today, debtors and citizens more broadly will come to believe that such behavior is acceptable. This, in turn, undermines the very foundations of the rule of law and, ultimately, our entire state," Pink said.

The Chamber of Bailiffs and Trustees in Bankruptcy has also proposed a meeting with the minister of justice and digital affairs to discuss ways to prevent or mitigate dangerous situations. The meeting has yet to take place, but Minister Liisa-Ly Pakosta said in a written response that she is willing to discuss possible next steps.

World.title: Record art auction spares Estonian Artists' Association from property sales
World.content:
The Estonian Artists' Association (EKL) says its record €2.3 million fundraiser art auction will spare the union from having to sell some property after a €700,000 fraud loss.

EKL president Maarin Ektermann told ETV's "Terevisioon" Monday morning that the three-day weekend auction raised nearly three times the amount they lost to fraud this spring, giving the organization more options for recovering financially.

Of the 162 works offered from its historic collection and donated by artists, only three went unsold. Starting bids ranged from €100 to €40,000, to make the auction accessible to a broad audience, though some prices climbed as much as 13-fold.

Several works also fetched six-figure sums, including a record €205,000 for Jaan Elken's painting "Juhikabiin" — the highest ever for a work by a living Estonian artist.

"When we started working on this over the summer, it was one of our plans for getting out of our [financial] crisis," Ektermann said. Thanks to the successful auction, the union can certainly leave some of its planned real estate unsold.

"The rest we can provide more details on at the extraordinary general meeting in mid-November," she added.

Maarin Ektermann. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Even so, Ektermann said the EKL has no intention of becoming a regular player in the art auction market.

"After the financial fraud, we quickly decided not to ask the state for help; we wanted to try to manage on our own," she explained. "Our art collection was one of the assets we had to sell."

The union president hopes the fundraiser auction sparks greater interest in buying and owning art, including among those who previously saw them as elitist or felt art auctions weren't for them.

The EKL will first pay artists their agreed shares — 5 percent for works from its collection and 15 percent for newly donated works — and review the auction's operating costs.

After repaying its loans and restoring its financial stability, the union will draw up recommendations for its council on how best to use the remaining funds to support Estonian art, in line with the EKL's statutes.

Ektermann said she hopes to outline some priorities at the meeting next month.

Gallery owner: They know what they're paying for

Commenting on the recent auction's record-setting Elken sale, Haus Gallery owner Piia Ausman said the price reflected the rarity of works from the artist's hyperrealist period — and competition between informed buyers.

Piia Ausman. Source: ERR

"I don't know who took part in the bidding, but I can only assume anyone willing to pay up to €100,000 for a work in today's Estonian art market — and in this case more than €200,000 — knows what they're paying for," Ausman said. "Even the artist himself no longer has any works from that period."

She also credited the auction's extensive media attention, which was amplified by the major union fraud loss behind it.

"This has been an extraordinary auction," Ausman said. "It has generated a huge amount of publicity itself, with the €700,000 fraud scandal playing a major role in that. All these factors came together to make the auction a phenomenon in its own right."

The gallery owner said the auction could have a lasting impact beyond the proceeds, including by prompting the EKL to improve its management and public profile.

She also hopes the union will invest in making its historic art collection more accessible online, potentially including information about the works' market value.

"You could say this has been one of the most profitable losses in Estonian society," Ausman added.

World.title: Alar Karis: Ingenuity what makes Estonians who they are and guarantees survival
World.content:
In his farewell speech to the Riigikogu, Estonia's outgoing President Alar Karis emphasized the country's resilience in the face of successive crises, called for greater trust and cooperation in politics and urged bold decisions to address future challenges.

Five years ago, in this very spot here in the Riigikogu, I pledged to uphold the Constitution, to defend the internal and external peace enshrined in its preamble and to listen and observe with patience. I spoke about a nation of people who cope, who are not afraid to face the unknown.

This we have had to do a surprisingly large number of times in recent years: the pandemic, war, inflation, the climate and energy crises and the aggressive development of new technology in the form of artificial intelligence.

None of these challenges originated here in Estonia, but have reached us from further afield. And, as a small nation, we are affected by them even more than larger countries.

We have had to familiarize ourselves with these unknowns and, where needed, change the way we think and behave. In so doing, we have adapted and managed to cope.

What is the role of the head of state in the midst of these crises?

It is their job to be observant, to know how to listen, to unite rather than to divide, to strike a balance, to maintain diversity, to champion peace at home and abroad. At least, this is how I have understand my role.

It is easy to talk to friends, but you must also speak with those whose views differ from your own. It is easy to reel off talking points, but you have to think and act for yourself, taking local circumstances into account.

It may be memorable and impressive to be outspoken, even combative in your words, but it is achieving results that matters. And while it can be nice to hear the sound of your own voice, it doesn't make you any smarter.

In maintaining peace abroad, we can rely not just on soft diplomacy, but also on our friends and allies — particularly those closest to us, our Nordic and Baltic neighbors. But when it comes to maintaining peace at home, we have no one to rely on but ourselves.

That internal peace begins with trust and a sense of belonging, with the attitude taken by the state, with comprehensible laws, with efforts to avoid over-regulation, with the responsibility of lawmakers and their consideration not just for those who vote for them, but also for the wider impact of those laws and the interplay of them.

Constant grappling with new crises, petty squabbling among politicians and the never-ending need for attention characteristic of instant gratification culture and the attention economy have fired up society — and, in the process, undermined its ability to think critically and, where necessary, to hold a dissenting view.

Election debates will soon be upon us which seek to highlight the differences between the candidates, with experts then assessing who was best at putting the others in their place.

But what impact might it have on the performance of our elected officials if, instead, we were to reward teamwork and recognize the passes that led to goals as well as the goals themselves?

Our culture of debate needs culture. If it is starved of it, then society's mental health will suffer and the self-censorship characteristic of this silent era will take hold.

I have been asked many times, especially in the last week, what I will be taking away from my five years in office.

My answer has been the same each time: a firm conviction, in fact the certainty, that the people of Estonia have it in them to cope, to adapt to crises and difficulties. It is precisely in our ability to deal with any situation that the wisdom of our nation lies. It is our ingenuity, that which makes us who we are and that which guarantees our survival.

The knowledge, indeed the joy, that we live in a free country that offers such quality of life, including a good education and a safe place to live, outweighs all difficulties and drives us to press ahead in our day-to-day lives and make important decisions. Therein I would like to see politicians and officials showing more mettle in their decision-making. If they don't, then things simply won't get done and problems will pile up.

Estonia, like the rest of Europe, is both aging and shrinking and needs new approaches: bold decisions, clever solutions, the courage to take risks and, where necessary, to rethink decisions, listening to and trusting the younger generation.

One benefit of being a small country is the ability to be flexible. The modernization of education and the economy is boosting Estonia: the introduction of new technologies, enhanced productivity, expansion into foreign markets and utilizing our advantages and experience as a digital nation. All of which can be summarized as focusing on the intelligence economy, be it human or artificial.

Alongside security, AI has become a core issue around the world. We have three options in regard to it: ignore, outlaw or adapt.

I don't believe in bans. There is no restricting development. Instead, it must be guided and a balance struck. We must provide a safe environment and put technology to work for the benefit of people.

AI has arrived as a great unknown and Estonia is setting an example of how to deal with it. With the support of schools and the Ministry of Education and Research, an idea born from a meeting with unicorns in Kadriorg has grown into a nationwide educational reform that cements Estonia's status as a digital nation, attracting both attention and interest and opening even the farthest-flung doors to us.

Most importantly, it provides youngsters with an education that will prepare them for the future.

I will continue to work on AI from an educational perspective after my time in office, as both a patron of AI Leap and a member of the UN's global 'AI for Good' commission.

And as a former president, I shall continue to champion curiosity and a knowledge-based approach, diversity and uniqueness, internal and external peace and the preservation of balance and freedoms.

I would like to thank my advisers, the director and staff of the Office of the President and all those I have worked with who, in sharing my values and vision, have helped make the past five years possible.

I also thank, of course, my wife Sirje, without whom none of this would have been possible and who took the lead in assisting Ukrainian children and speaking out on young people's mental health.

President-elect Madise,

The office of head of state of Estonia is a great honor, but an even greater responsibility.

May you have the ability to observe, to notice, to ask the right questions and to find the time to think about things as well.

More than anything else, however, may you remain ever true to yourself and unafraid of encountering the unknown. I wish you strength, wisdom and resolve in carrying out your role.

World.title: Iraq, Saudi Arabia discuss energy cooperation as electricity and oil ministers meet in Riyadh
World.content:
Riyadh (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Oil Minister, Basim Mohammed Khudair, and Iraq’s Electricity Minister, Ali Saadi Waheeb, met with Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman in Riyadh to discuss extending bilateral energy cooperation and boosting coordination between the two nations.

The meeting was held on the sidelines of the 25th WPC Energy Congress, sponsored by Saudi Arabia and attended by energy ministers, industry executives, and representatives from major international energy firms.

According to Waheeb, the talks focused on ways to increase energy cooperation and create tighter coordination in accordance with Iraq and Saudi Arabia’s interests.

The Iraqi electrical minister emphasized Baghdad’s desire to continue discussions with Riyadh and expand areas of collaboration, particularly in ways that could help improve the stability of Iraq’s power system.

The meetings brought together Iraq’s two senior energy ministers and their Saudi counterparts at a time when regional energy security, infrastructure investment, and dependable power supply are still top considerations.

Iraq has been attempting to modernize its electrical infrastructure, diversify energy suppliers, and establish regional alliances in response to local power constraints and rising demand.

The Riyadh meeting was part of a larger series of engagements by Iraqi energy officials at the congress, which included talks with neighboring countries about electrical interconnections, technical cooperation, and investment prospects.

Additionally, the high-level meeting came after a separate high-level energy meeting in Baghdad on Saturday, when Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi welcomed TotalEnergies CEO Patrick Pouyanné and ConocoPhillips CEO Andy O’Brien, along with their teams.

The talks in Baghdad centered on investment in oil production and related gas at Basra’s Bin Umar oilfield, including deadlines for raising output and chances to extend production in adjacent locations.

World.title: Tom Barrack meets Iraq’s top judge Faiq Zaidan in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US Envoy Tom Barrack met with Iraq’s top judicial leadership in Baghdad on Monday, as Washington and Baghdad strive to rebuild their bilateral relationship in the face of regional tensions and a shifting security situation.

Barrack met with Judge Faiq Zaidan, President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, to explore ways to strengthen bilateral legal and judicial collaboration.

The meeting comes at a difficult time for the region, after fatal assaults on Riyadh’s international airport over the weekend, which Saudi officials blamed on Yemen’s Houthi movement.

In a statement issued after the negotiations, Barrack praised his meeting with Zaidan as positive and emphasized the necessity of an independent judiciary for Iraq’s future.

“A strong, independent judiciary is the bedrock of sovereignty, the rule of law, and the stability that lets Iraq turn its potential into prosperity,” Barrack wrote, thanking Zaidan for his partnership.

Barrack also met with Steve Fagin, the United States’ chargé d’affaires in Baghdad, and praised his diplomatic skills while emphasizing Washington’s aspirations to broaden its relationship with Iraq beyond security cooperation.

He regarded the present time as a watershed point in bilateral ties, stating that the United States was moving toward a more comprehensive relationship based on economic cooperation and common interests.

The Baghdad talks follow Barrack’s weekend conversations with Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein in Turkey, during which the two sides discussed bilateral ties and regional events.

The diplomatic contacts follow the completion of the US-led coalition’s military mission in Iraq, signaling a move toward a bilateral partnership based on political, economic, and security cooperation.

World.title: British airbase plot ‘almost certainly directed’ by Iran Guards: UK PM
World.content:
London – Britain’s government Monday accused Iran’s Revolutionary Guards of being behind a major scare at a UK airbase used by the United States, as allies including Washington warned Tehran against hostile acts.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the British parliament that Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) “almost certainly directed” an incident at Royal Air Force Fairford in southwest England last month.

The US, which had been using the base for its war in Iran, abruptly withdrew all its B-1 bombers from the site last week after the mysterious episode on September 27.

Burnham said Britain’s assessment of the incident was that it “is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard”.

“We will not tolerate these threats on our soil. We will crack down on Iran’s use of criminal networks, using our full range of powers to target them and their funding streams,” he told MPs.

Shortly afterwards, 29 countries, including the US, Britain, Australia, Canada, France and Germany, released a joint statement denouncing “in the strongest terms Iran’s use of violent attacks”.

The statement said such attacks included “acts of lethal plotting, arson, sabotage, cyber-attacks, and other hybrid activities against us and our partners”.

“Any attempt by Iran to threaten, silence, intimidate, harass, harm, or coerce people on our territories through proxies or any other means is unacceptable,” it read.

The Foreign Office confirmed in its own statement Monday that Iran’s ambassador to the UK had been summoned for talks.

“We are also announcing the designation of two Iranian nationals for their role in facilitating or engaging in hostile activity on behalf of the Iranian regime, with the clear intent of threatening, planning or conducting attacks overseas,” foreign minister Ed Miliband said.

The foreign ministry said the individuals included Ruhollah Bazghandi, the IRGC’s head of counterespionage operations, who is “now subject to an immediate asset freeze, travel ban and director disqualification”.

Speculation has swirled about the incident since police were called to the base after a local farmer reported a group of men with several white vans engaged in “suspicious” activity.

– ‘Major’ incident –

Despite a major counter-terrorism probe, seven suspects arrested in the days following, including a British-Iranian national, have all since been released on bail. None has been charged.

The incident was declared “major” by British authorities and triggered the evacuation of a nearby village.

But the source and nature of the threat have remained shrouded in mystery.

Investigators did not find any explosives in the vans, but did recover some petrol, according to officials.

Burnham has previously said there were “strong indications that Iran played a part” in the incident, which Tehran has rejected.

Britain gave Washington permission in March to use Fairford for “specific defensive operations into Iran,” and US bombers and other planes had been seen taking off and landing at the base.

US President Donald Trump has said Washington withdrew its bombers because of “threats” he believed were linked to Tehran.

In the foreign ministry statement, Miliband noted that the UK had already “designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) under our new state threats powers, and imposed major sanctions on those responsible for Iran’s malign activity”.

World.title: Iraq’s Minister of Electricity visits Riyadh to attend WPC Energy Congress
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Minister of Electricity, Ali Saadi Waheeb, attended the 25th WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh on Monday, where he met with key international energy authorities and discussed ways to develop Iraq’s electrical industry and promote regional collaboration.

Waheeb attended the event with Iraq’s Minister of Oil, Basim Mohammed Khudair, as Saudi Arabia welcomed ministers, industry executives, and officials from international energy corporations to discuss energy security, investment, and technological innovation.

The visit comes amid heightened security concerns after the weekend’s fatal strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport by Yemen’s Houthis.

According to Saudi police, an assault on Saturday killed at least 12 people and injured over 300, while another on Sunday killed one person and injured 11 others.

The attacks hampered airport operations as the monarchy continued its international energy meetings.

Waheeb accompanied Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman for the opening of the congress exhibition, which displayed advances in energy technology, infrastructure, and investments.

On the sidelines of the conference, the Iraqi minister met with Turkey’s Minister of Energy and Natural Resources, Alparslan Bayraktar, to discuss extending collaboration on power infrastructure.

According to Bayraktar, the two nations have agreed to speed power interconnection lines and transmission projects, as well as increase bilateral investment to boost regional energy security.

In a statement on X, the Turkish Minister said that Ankara and Baghdad planned to expand their energy relationship beyond oil and gas to include the electricity sector.

Waheeb also spoke with Algeria’s Energy Minister, Mohamed Arkab, on technological cooperation, renewable energy, and potential for developing power generation, transmission, and distribution projects.

Waheeb met separately with Jordan’s Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources, Saleh Ali Hamid Al-Kharabsha, to explore ways to increase bilateral energy cooperation, exchange technical skills, and improve power infrastructure.

The young Iraqi Minister also attended the 16th meeting of the Arab Council of Ministers for power in Riyadh, where officials addressed regional power integration, renewable energy, energy efficiency, and increased collaboration among Arab nations.

Waheeb stated that Iraq was looking to use foreign experience and attract investment to upgrade its energy infrastructure, extend regional power connections, and enhance electricity supply.

World.title: Federal agents search home of Trump critic Ilhan Omar: government
World.content:
Washington – US federal agents searched the Washington home of Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar on Monday as part of a criminal investigation, officials said, marking a dramatic escalation in President Donald Trump’s confrontation with the outspoken lawmaker.

The search was conducted by agents from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the investigative arm of US immigration enforcement, according to Fox News, citing sources familiar with the matter.

The operation, just three weeks before Omar seeks re-election in the November 3 midterms, raised concerns about longstanding Justice Department practices intended to prevent law enforcement actions from influencing elections.

The cable network reported that the operation was linked to a criminal fraud investigation concerning immigration paperwork submitted on behalf of the Somali-born congresswoman by her late father when she was a child.

Trump’s border enforcement chief Tom Homan told Fox News he was unwilling to give details ahead of any official announcement but confirmed that an “investigation was ongoing for a while” and that “there was a warrant executed this morning.”

US media quoted the Justice Department confirming that agents had carried out a court-authorized search in the Washington area, but officials did not identify Omar or disclose the nature of the investigation.

The search reportedly began around 6:00 am. Video footage apparently taken by a member of the public and posted to X showed several agents wearing HSI jackets outside Omar’s Washington residence.

Omar, 44, is a leftist Democrat and fierce critic of Trump, particularly his administration’s sweeping crackdown on immigration.

The Republican president has repeatedly clashed with Omar, who came to the United States from Somalia as a child and has frequently been the target of his political attacks.

– Rare offense –

In September, Homan said that Omar was the subject of an ongoing criminal investigation, but again declined to provide details.

Omar said at the time that Homeland Security officials had not contacted her about any investigation, dismissing the allegations against her as politically motivated attacks.

There was no immediate public response from Omar to Monday’s search. AFP has sought comment from her office and the Trump administration.

But Xochitl Hinojosa, a former director of public affairs at the Justice Department, criticized the timing of the search.

“There’s a longstanding rule at DOJ that you don’t take overt actions like this before an election, especially when there’s a candidate on the ballot,” she wrote on X.

Aaron Reichlin-Melnick, a senior fellow at the American Immigration Council, wrote on X that the “precedent set by this action is chilling,” warning that raids targeting political candidates shortly before elections could become more common.

Omar was first elected to Congress in 2018 and represents a district including Minneapolis, home to one of the largest Somali communities in the United States.

She is a member of the group of left-wing Democratic lawmakers known as “The Squad,” who have been among Trump’s most vocal opponents in Congress.

No charges against Omar were announced in connection with Monday’s search.

Trump and his Republican allies have for years argued that non-citizens vote in significant numbers in US elections, a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment and deportation.

But studies consistently find non-citizen voting to be too rare an offense to have affected the outcome of any federal election.

An election fraud database kept by the conservative Heritage Foundation, dating back decades, contains just 1,619 cases of election-related offenses — of which non-citizen voting makes up a tiny 5.5 percent.

World.title: Iraq to increase electricity imports from Turkey to 2,000 megawatts
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Electricity revealed that it imports 600 megawatts of electricity per day from Turkey, with plans to reach 2,000 megawatts during the second phase of the electrical interconnection project.

The spokesperson for the Electricity Ministry, Ahmed Turki, said that one of the key principles of the strategy to strengthen the national grid’s supply is electricity interconnections with other countries. He added that the Ministry is actively working on electrical interconnection projects with the Gulf States, Turkey, and Jordan.

Iraq’s electricity interconnection project with the Gulf States is currently around 98 percent complete, according to Turki. He added that the project has a capacity of 500 megawatts.

The Iraqi official mentioned that during the visit of Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, the Iraqi electricity minister requested an increase of 300 megawatts in the electricity supply from the Turkish company. This additional capacity has already been integrated into Iraq’s national grid.

Iraq now imports 600 megawatts per day from Turkey, with a deal in place for a second phase that will increase imported capacity through the Turkish line to almost 2,000 megawatts.

In terms of the electricity interconnection project with Jordan, Turki said that Iraq was getting between 50 and 100 megawatts from the Jordanian side until the contract expired in mid-September, with expectations that it would be renewed next summer.

World.title: Saudi says resilience tested, vows response after deadly airport attacks
World.content:
Riyadh – Saudi Arabia’s energy minister on Monday said the country had been tested but would mount a “serious” response after a string of attacks on Riyadh’s international airport by Yemen’s Houthis that left 18 people dead.

Lethal airport strikes since last week have rocked the world’s top oil exporter, which is pursuing an expensive economic reform drive aimed at attracting foreign investment.

Yemen’s civil war, where a Saudi-led military coalition supports the government against the Iran-backed Houthis, has reignited months into the US-Iran conflict that has roiled energy markets and plunged the Middle East into crisis.

“Energy security can’t be taken for granted,” Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman told an energy conference in Riyadh, as oil prices topped $105 a barrel.

“The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious.”

“For Saudi Arabia, these circumstances have tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people, and our resilience,” he added.

On Saturday, Houthi strikes killed 13 people and wounded hundreds at King Khalid International Airport — the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade.

Four people died in earlier attacks on Wednesday and Thursday, and another was killed on Sunday. Operations remained suspended at the sprawling airport on Riyadh’s outskirts on Monday.

CCTV footage of Saturday’s attack released by Saudi authorities showed Muslim pilgrims in religious attire waiting in departure lounges before a sudden flash tore through the building and brought down flaming debris.

– ‘The whole house shook’ –

The atmosphere in Riyadh remained tense on Monday, as state broadcaster Al Ekhbariya said the military coalition was responding to drone and missile threats, and Australia’s embassy warned its citizens in the city to shelter in place.

The Houthis on Sunday claimed multiple attacks over the previous 24 hours, including on the airport, and threatened to keep targeting Saudi transit hubs, calling them “a theatre of operations for our forces”.

Hours later, the coalition said yet another projectile had struck Riyadh airport, sparking a fire, while air defences intercepted a missile nearby.

AFP journalists and locals reported hearing multiple blasts in the capital on Sunday.

“The whole house shook,” said one resident of the Al-Aarid neighbourhood in the city’s north.

Riyadh’s airport was not the only one to suffer a deadly attack: early on Monday, officials said one person had been killed and 11 wounded in a strike on Dammam airport.

The Saudi-led coalition said Monday that it had also “intercepted and destroyed” a Houthi ballistic missile heading for the southern city of Khamis Mushait, home to a major military base.

Riyadh hosts a packed calendar of events at this time of year, including its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference, which draws foreign leaders and business titans.

– ‘Full-fledged war crime’ –

Despite vast spending on military hardware, the Houthi attacks on oil, military and transport facilities across the large, mostly desert country are stretching Saudi defences.

“Saudi air defences have been able to intercept some Houthi missile and drone attacks, but Saudi Arabia is so large that it’s simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves,” said Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University.

The anti-Houthi coalition called Saturday’s attack a “full-fledged war crime” and vowed to “respond decisively”.

The attack drew condemnation from the United Nations and leaders including US President Donald Trump, who said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis.

Iran, which backs the Houthis, said Monday it was “deeply concerned” over the recent escalation.

Witnesses to Saturday’s strike described chaos in the aftermath.

“Some had lost a hand or an arm. People were running while carrying injured people, covered in blood,” a 32-year-old Riyadh resident told AFP.

Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa.

Ottawa University’s Juneau said the Houthis now “want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them”.

World.title: Alcaraz exits Shanghai Masters in straight-sets loss
World.content:
Shanghai – Carlos Alcaraz fell to Zizou Bergs in straight sets at the Shanghai Masters on Monday, interrupting the former world number one’s in-form return to the professional Tour after being sidelined for months by injury.

The 39th-ranked Belgian beat the second-seeded Spanish star 7-5, 7-6 (7/4) in the third round to land the tournament’s biggest upset yet, and will play either Tommy Paul or Valentin Vacherot next.

“It’s a little disbelief and not feeling too much,” Bergs, 27, said afterwards.

“You’re just really in the moment, being focused on the points you have to play,” he added.

“I’ll be very happy.”

Alcaraz started with more quality until Bergs broke the Spaniard’s serve to go up 3-2 in the first set.

The 23-year-old grabbed back that break in the next game but was uncharacteristically off-target, sending a mess of shots into the net.

He double-faulted to hand Bergs a critical break point in the 11th game, and lost the first set when a volley went short.

Alcaraz was visibly frustrated during the second set as he vented to his corner following a series of misfired shots that left him with no points in the fourth and eighth games.

Alcaraz forced a tie-break but could not reach a third set as Bergs closed things out just past the two-hour mark on his first match point.

– Fritz fumbles –

Earlier, Stefanos Tsitsipas came back to beat Taylor Fritz 3-6, 7-5, 6-3 and earn fourth round meeting with Daniil Medvedev, who brushed aside qualifier Dalibor Svrcina 6-2, 6-3.

A wardrobe malfunction delayed victory for the Greek world number 43 when a tennis ball tumbled out of the American’s pocket a second time and forced the men to replay a match point.

A tired-looking Fritz, seeded 11th, hung on for a bit longer to save the eighth game but could not stick around beyond that, with Tsitsipas holding serve to win at the fifth time of asking.

“I could have done a few things easier, but I ended up being my biggest enemy,” Tsitsipas told the crowd afterwards.

“I turned things around really well towards the end and became friends with myself and played some incredible tennis,” he said.

Felix Auger-Aliassime, Casper Ruud and Rafael Jodar also went through to the last 16.

World.title: 60% of 33 lakh who received SIR notices in Delhi are now verified
World.content:
Disposal of SIR notices expedited after mid-September

NEW DELHI: Over 60% of the 33 lakh voters who got SIR notices in Delhi have been verified after the Election Commission eased the verification process late last month.BLOs are now visiting homes to collect documents, instead of requiring people to appear for hearings at govt offices. Also, BLO have been empowered to make corrections for minor issues, such as spelling mistakes, without seeking extensive documentation.About 33 lakh voters, including chief minister Rekha Gupta, AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal, external affairs minister S Jaishankar and BJP veteran LK Advani got notices in Sept.While over 19 lakh voters were flagged for "logical discrepancies", including mismatches in names and age-related inconsistencies, nearly 14 lakh were classified as "unmapped" because their records could not be linked to the 2002 SIR. The notices sought clarification and supporting documents to verify eligibility for inclusion in the final SIR roll, scheduled for Dec 4.The office of the chief electoral officer of Delhi, in a post on X Monday, said: "We had started a proactive campaign to resolve these issues (discrepancies). By now around 20 lakh cases out of 33 lakh have been resolved. If any person has any grievance, please feel free to contact any of the 14,947 BLOs, 902 AEROs, 70 EROs, 13 DEOs or the CEO.No eligible voter will be excluded from the voter list."An official told TOI, "The disposal of SIR notices was very slow until the third week of Sept but picked up after we introduced new measures. Nearly 15,000 BLOs have been asked to clear at least 10 notices daily. In cases involving logical discrepancies, they have been instructed to verify the voter's age, Indian citizenship and ordinary residence in the constituency. Eligible voters will not be removed merely because of logical inconsistencies in their records. "A few BLOs told TOI they are using BLO declarations to verify voters with minor discrepancies, such as a missing letter in the name, after checking documents and getting the voter's signature on the declarations. Some BLOs said they had been using such declarations for quite some time now.AEROs, meanwhile, have been asked to upload details of resolved cases without delay. "We found that some AEROs were not uploading the cases they had already verified, partly because the deadline for completing the exercise was still weeks away. They have been instructed to ensure that resolved cases are uploaded promptly," said the official.In cases where voters could not be mapped to the previous electoral rolls, BLOs have been asked to clear the cases promptly after taking and checking prescribed documents, such as a voter's date of birth and other documents.Delhi's electoral roll listed 1.56 crore voters in January 2025, days before the assembly elections. In June, when the SIR began, this number had shrunk to 1.45 crore. The draft electoral roll published on Aug 31 had 97.5 lakh voters, with around 47.6 lakh names deleted.EC said a majority of these people had shifted homes and failed to submit enumeration forms. Those who have received SIR notices are among the 97.5 lakh voters. The disposal of SIR notices and completion of verification will continue until Nov 30.

World.title: Steelmaker to steer 440 crore revamp of 9 ITIs
World.content:
NEW DELHI : A Rs 440-crore overhaul will put ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India (AM/NS India) in charge of nine govt Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in Gujarat and Andhra. The company will hold a 51% stake in entities managing the institutes under PM-SETU.

Skill development ministry Monday signed shareholders' agreements covering five ITIs in Surat and four in Visakhapatnam. Rs 240 crore is earmarked for Surat and Rs 200 crore for Visakhapatnam. Centre and state govts will each hold 24.5% equity. SPVs will manage modernisation and operations. AM/NS India will implement the projects with New Age Makers' Institute of Technology as partner. Plans include modern workshops and laboratories, new trades, revised courses and more practical training.

PM-SETU has Rs 60,000-crore outlay and aims to upgrade 1,000 govt ITIs and strengthen five National Skill Training Institutes. Funding includes Rs 30,000 crore from Centre, Rs 20,000 crore from states and Rs 10,000 crore from industry.

World.title: As Jantar Mantar loses protest site tag, CJP plans get disrupted
World.content:
The CJP leaders recently approached the Delhi Police to organize a protest addressing issues with the electoral roll

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Monday gave Delhi Police 24 hours to set a date for its proposed protest at Jantar Mantar against alleged electoral roll revision irregularities, offering the force the choice to decide when it could be held.However, just as the green light was sought, police announced the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, throwing CJP's plan into uncertainty and prompting it to slam the move.Hours before party co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka came to Parliament Street police station to submit a letter regarding its demand, barricades and security personnel had taken over adjacent roads.Even Firoz Shah Road, around 10 minutes away, had barricades and police personnel stationed along it.Closer to Parliament Street, access was restricted, with loudspeakers repeatedly warning: "Section 163 of BNSS is in place. Please abide by law and order. Stay away from barricades on the road." Just outside the police station, security was even tighter, with announcements also spelling out restrictions for media personnel.Ranka said, "We have come to police with a letter giving them the option to suggest a date on which we can hold our protest.The DCP came into the room, but left when he saw us sitting there. So, we could not meet him. The additional DCP and SHO are not present. It appears the entire police station has been vacated since CJP members arrived. Anyway, we have submitted the letter."In its communication, CJP claimed that over 55,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across Delhi over the past three days, disrupting normal life.It alleged arbitrary detentions, physical aggression and prolonged custody involving common people and journalists, besides flagging financial losses suffered by businesses forced to down shutters.The party blamed road closures, barricades and the refusal to allot Jantar Mantar as a protest site for growing public distress. It demanded a scaling down of security deployment, an end to alleged illegal detentions and harassment of independent journalists, and permission to protest at a designated site.Das said, "Protesting peacefully is our democratic right. What happened in the past day (was akin to govt) waging a war against its own citizens."The party said that students, youth and other citizens cannot be prevented from exercising their constitutional right to assemble and protest peacefully.Soon after Jantar Mantar's denotification was announced, Ranka posted on social media, "Why not declare Mt Everest as the designated protest site? Thirty minutes after we went to Delhi Police asking for a date when we can go to Jantar Mantar, it was denotified."CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke wrote on social media, "Today, Modi denotified Jantar Mantar... Tomorrow, he will denotify democracy itself... Anyway, Jantar Mantar was turned into a war zone... Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega!"

World.title: Rahul Gandhi venting electoral frustration through protests: BJP
World.content:
NEW DELHI: It is not

(EC) but Congress's own "visionless" leadership that is behind its long run of poll defeats, BJP said Monday, stating that an "unstable, anarchist and unserious" Rahul Gandhi has turned to street protests to vent his frustration over popular rejection.

Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan quizzed Congress over its losses even in recent bypolls and factional fights besetting its state units from Karnataka to Punjab and UP, asserting that the party had lost people's trust for long.

BJP MP Anurag Thakur questioned INDIA bloc's decision to submit a memorandum to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant following its march Monday, saying it amounted to Rahul and his party threatening the judiciary over a sub-judice matter.

Hitting out at Rahul, Anurag said it was unfortunate for the country that the leader of the opposition has total disregard for facts and rules, and can only spread anarchy, denigrate constitutional institutions and defame India globally. "Vote chori is on his lips, but what he is doing is belittling popular mandate," he said.

BJP also flayed Rahul for projecting the protests as "Shivji ki barat", recalling the previous Congress govt's decision questioning the existence of Lord Ram.





In fact, it involves a collection of hooligans determined to stoke disorder with support from foreign forces inimical to India, the party alleged.

Asked about Rahul's claims like half of police personnel sympathising with Opposition's protests, Chouhan cited a Hindi proverb to allege that the Congress MP was worth lakhs of liars. "If the Opposition is levelling allegations, then it is also its job to offer proof.

It should support an independent probe into its claims. Democracy does not give one the licence to denigrate public mandate," Anurag said, adding that, unlike Congress, BJP has a history of defending the Constitution, as in the Emergency.

Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra said "Rahul Gandhi, who once tore up a bill introduced by his own govt, has disrespected the dignity of Supreme Court today, proving that he has become the most anarchic leader in the country."

"By disrespecting the dignity of Supreme Court and the Chief Justice of India today, Rahul Gandhi has forfeited the moral right to file a petition before Supreme Court," he added. "His anarchic conduct today has established that if he dislikes any verdict of Supreme Court tomorrow, he will take to the streets against it as well".

BJP ally Chirag Paswan, who has at times taken a position different from BJP's, also hit out at Rahul, saying SC has already given its judgment on SIR and asking if he was not pressuring the court with street protests.

World.title: SC to government: Cap prices of non-patented medicines
World.content:
NEW DELHI: With the Centre failing to give even "one justification" to the satisfaction of the court in favour of patients for keeping the maximum retail price of medicines at exorbitant levels but also accepting that profit margins for drugs and medical consumables reach up to 1,000%, Supreme Court on Monday said that the price of all non-patented drugs and consumables should also be controlled and it should not be confined only to anti-cancer medicines as done by govt recently.

As solicitor general Tushar Mehta and ASG Aishwarya Bhati informed SC about the decision to cap the trade margins on anti-cancer drugs at 30% of the maximum retail price, the court appreciated govt's decision but raised questions on why pricing of other medicines should not be capped. The bench pointed out various examples to drive home the point that patients are fleeced because of sky-high pricing.

SC to government: There is a great divide... why canât you control the entire range of drugs

This relates to only cancer drugs. What about the overall? For an ordinary cardiac stent, Indian made stent, price to retailer (PTR) is Rs 5,000 but MRP is Rs 25,000...

This is not even a tip of the iceberg. It (decision) has come only because of harsh observation from the court,â the bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta asked SG Tushar Mehta and also applauded his intervention resulting in a quick decision.

It said the price of a drip line for saline for the retailer is Rs 11 but the MRP is around Rs 270. It said MRP for Azithromycin is Rs 78.29 but the PTS (price to stockist) is Rs 28.5.





âThere is a great divide... There are thousands of examples,â court said, asking govt to explain why all non-patented medicines shouldnât be brought under price control.

âGive me just one justification in favour of patients (for not controlling the prices). Why canât you control the entire range of drugs?â the bench asked the ASG.

Bhati submitted that areas with lower sales, such as rural areas, may require higher margins for the retailer so as to provide sufficient income and livelihood to the retailer, failing which the access to and availability of drugs in such areas may be adversely affected.

She told the bench the Indian drug market is fairly competitive, with a large number of pharmaceutical companies in every drug segment, resulting in one of the lowest prices in the world.

âIf there is too much intervention by govt, it will lead to the market suffering. It will affect availability.â

But court said all the justifications given by govt were not in favour of patients who had to pay the higher price. Intervening in the proceedings, the SG submitted govt was not averse to the plea and the bench also made it clear that its proceeding was only intended to âstrengthen the hands of the govt and nothing elseâ.

Govt, in its affidavit, said, âAnother area of concern in the sector is supply of consumables in hospitals, where margins of 100-1000% or more are prevalent, along with a tendency of hospitals to purchase consumables that have a high MRP, with a low price to the distributor/hospital.â

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

It admitted that patients have a very low bargaining position vis-a-vis the hospital, and a patientâs knowledge of drugs, their substitutes and their prices is also limited.

âThese bargaining and information asymmetries result in malpractices despite strong competition among manufacturers, leading to the need for regulation. That hospitals purchase medicines from manufacturers who provide the highest trade margin and then sell those to patients at the MRP, with margins ranging from 170% to 700% or more in the case of anti-cancer (oncology) drugs,â the affidavit said.

The apex court thereafter adjourned the case for Oct 27.

World.title: Morning Digest: INDIA bloc rally takes SIR protest to Supreme Court; Delhi police accused of beating, assaulting detainees, and more
World.content:
Delhi police accused of beating, assaulting detainees, denying them basic rights

Detainees’ accounts of beatings, assaults, and excessive force used by the Delhi police over the last few days have raised concerns about post-detention practices of law enforcement personnel. Thousands of protesters have been detained by the police in the national capital on October 10, 11, and 12, including journalists, members of youth organisations, and minors.

INDIA bloc marches through Delhi, takes SIR protest to Supreme Court

On a day when Delhi Police denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, a sizeable crowd walked down arterial roads in the capital, tailing a procession of buses carrying INDIA bloc leaders from Constitution Club to the Supreme Court, where Rahul Gandhi and other top leaders of the coalition filed a petition over the alleged large-scale voter deletions and irregularities in the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Doval speaks to Iran NSA, discusses ‘latest developments’ after ships attacked in Hormuz

National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval spoke to his Iranian counterpart Mohsin Rezaei on Monday evening, the Iranian government said, a day after two merchant ships with Indian crew members were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.

Restrictions on firecrackers: Supreme Court urges balance between religious sentiments and public health

The Supreme Court on Monday highlighted the need to balance religious sentiments with public health concerns while considering restrictions on firecrackers in the national capital and neighbouring regions. “We will not hurt religious sentiments but at the same time, people should themselves come forward and opt for it. The whole exercise should involve a balancing approach,” Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, heading a three-judge Bench, said.

DMK says no need for it to join Congress-led protests after exit from INDIA bloc

The DMK on Monday said it had no reason to participate in protests organised by the Congress after the latter “betrayed” it for the sake of power, forcing the DMK to leave the INDIA bloc. The DMK said Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president Manickam Tagore should question Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s absence from the agitation if he (Mr. Tagore) had any self-respect or sensitivity.

Arlekar new full-time Governor of T.N., Sudha Yadav to take charge in Karnataka in new gubernatorial appointments

President Droupadi Murmu on Monday effected some changes in Governors across six States, with Rajendra Arlekar to now serve as full-time Governor of Tamil Nadu, where he had been holding additional charge along with Keralam till now, and O.P. Mathur, who was serving as Governor of Sikkim to now serve as Governor of Keralam.

The 2026 Nobel-winning insights into how governments should stabilise economies

The 2026 Nobel Prize for Economics has been jointly awarded to American economists Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford for providing an empirical formula to help government devise policies that are aimed at stabilising the economy by incorporating household demand behaviour and the supply behaviour of companies.

Supreme Court wants cap on trade margin for all essential medicines and medical products

Even as the Centre informed the Supreme Court on Monday that it had decided to cap trade margins at 30% for non-scheduled cancer drugs, the court questioned why the benefit of such price regulation should be confined to cancer drugs and not extended to other essential medicines and medical products.

Delhi Police mentally tortured me and my family, says CJP fouder Abhijeet Dipke

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday accused the Delhi Police of mentally torturing him and his family after informing him of his grandmother’s death during his preventive detention last week. He alleged that the police did not allow him to speak to his cousin about his grandmother’s death and instead asked him to call his grieving parents. He also called Prime Minister Narendra Modi a “coward dictator”.

RJ Mitte, ’Breaking Bad’ actor and disability rights champion, dies at 34

Breaking Bad actor and disability rights advocate RJ Mitte died on Monday (October 12, 2026) at age 34, authorities and his representatives said. Cameron County Justice of the Peace Cyndi Hinojosa told The Associated Press she declared Mitte dead at about 1.30 p.m. at what she believed was his home in Brownsville, Texas.

World.title: Berlin to BITS Pilani: How Nobel-winning optogenetics connects to parasite research in Hyderabad
World.content:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, awarded to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel “for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics”, has brought renewed attention to using light to investigate fundamental biological processes. These include memory formation, feelings, and behaviours relevant for neurological and psychiatric disorders, as well as processes involved in infectious disease.

Editorial | Let there be light: On the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology/Medicine

For Nishith Gupta, professor of Biological Sciences at BITS Pilani, Hyderabad, and founder of the Intracellular Parasite Education and Research Labs (iPEARL), the recognition has a personal significance in his own scientific journey.

Mr. Gupta’s decades-long collaboration with Hegemann at Humboldt University of Berlin, where Hegemanna is Hertie Senior Professor of Neuroscience, helped extend optogenetic approaches beyond neuroscience into his study of Toxoplasma gondii, an intracellular parasite that infects humans, mammals, and birds.

Interactive Guide | Nobel Prize 2026

Optogenetics enables scientists to control selected cells or biological processes using light-sensitive proteins.

The Nobel Committee for Physiology or Medicine stated: “It all began with Peter Hegemann’s curiosity. He wondered how Chlamydomonas, a single-celled alga, is able to swim towards a light source. In the early 2000s, he and Georg Nagel discovered channelrhodopsin, an algal protein with unique properties, found on the surface of the cell. When it is illuminated by blue light, a channel opens through the protein. Charged ions then flow into the cell, creating an electrical impulse. They found that regardless of which cell they put the protein in, those cells became light sensitive.” In 2005, Deisseroth showed that introducing channelrhodopsin into rat neurons allowed blue light to trigger nerve signals. In 2007, he showed light-based control in mice.

In contrast, Mr. Gupta, Mr. Hegemann and others used light-regulated enzyme adenylate cyclase, which converts adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the primary energy of a living cell, to produce cyclic Adenosine Monophosphate (cAMP). This molecule acts as messengers, helping transmit signals within cells.

Put simply, the researchers showed that light controls the enzyme, the enzyme produces cAMP, and cAMP helps regulate what happens inside the parasite (Toxoplasma gondii): how it enters cells, moves, and exits cells. This landmark study was published in the Journal of Biological Chemistry in 2013.

While Mr. Deisseroth, Mr. Hegemann, and Mr. Nagel’s optogenetics “solves one of humanity’s great mysteries, how our incredible brain works”, Mr. Gupta, Mr. Hegemann and others’ found light-regulated signalling to investigate parasite’s lifestyle, and infection.

Mr. Gupta says that working alongside Hegemann in Berlin, with their laboratories in neighbouring departments, was an important part of this scientific journey. Joint funding from the German Research Foundation (DFG) supported their collaboration.

After Mr. Gupta relocated to India, Mr. Hegemann continued to support his research through Mr. Gupta’s Wellcome Trust–DBT Senior Fellowship project at BITS Pilani. Researchers from his team continued to visit Hegemann’s group in Berlin.

For Mr. Gupta, the Nobel Prize awarded to Mr. Hegemann and his fellow laureates underscores the far-reaching consequences of fundamental research. A protein that evolved to help an alga sense light has become a tool for probing the brain, investigating infection and understanding how cells function. He says the broader lesson is that technologies developed to answer one biological question can open entirely new avenues of research.

“Light has become more than a means of observation; it is a way to intervene, test, and uncover cause-and-effect relationships,” Mr. Gupta says.

World.title: Mehbooba Mufti opposes motorable boulevard on western side of famous Dal Lake
World.content:
Opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti on Monday (October 12, 2026) opposed a proposal of ruling National Conference (NC) legislator to construct a motorable boulevard on the western shore of the Dal Lake, a major attraction for tourists travelling to Kashmir.

“The proposed Western Foreshore Road from Hotel Mamta to Habbak via Cherry Park is a deliberate attempt to mislead and push a vote-bank agenda. The Tourism Department developed the Proposal, but Cherry Park should be preserved as an ecopark, not sacrificed for political appeasement. Why destroy Nigeen Lake’s tranquillity? Kashmir needs ecological protection, not divisive politics,” said Ms. Mufti.

The Opposition to the move came when NC legislator Tanvir Sadiq moved a private members’ Bill, ‘The Right to Dignified Eco-Housing in Lakeside Areas Bill, 2026’, before the J&K Assembly earlier. It aims to rehabilitate the Dal dwellers in and around the lake, in contrast to the 2000 policy of 2000 of both the Centre and the local government to relocate the dwellers from over 7526 kanals of land on the city outskirts. However, Mr Sadiq also proposed a boulevard on the western shore of the lake “to ease traffic for the Dal dwellers”.

The proposal also attracted criticism from the Environmental Policy Group (EPG), a local advocacy group. It highlighted the findings of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) that recorded a decline in the size from 15.40 square kilometres in 2007 to 12.91 square kilometres in 2020 of the lake, “a reduction of 10.15%”.

“There is the need to ensure dignified living conditions and protect the legitimate interests of families who have historically lived around water bodies. Housing rights should not compromise the ecological integrity, carrying capacity and public character of lakes and wetlands,” said the EPG.

It warned that the Dal lake was not an ordinary residential settlement but a living ecological system, a natural flood buffer and one of Kashmir’s most important environmental assets. “The answer to decades of administrative failure could not be to retrospectively legitimise activities that had contributed to the deterioration of the lake,” it added.

The advocacy group also opposed attempts of land filling, reclamation for roads, residential structures or other infrastructure. “Any legislative intervention should address the causes of degradation rather than merely recognise the consequences of years of weak enforcement,” it added.

It demanded a detailed environmental, legal and technical scrutiny of the proposed legislation. “The Assembly must not create a framework under which the degradation of the lake becomes a fait accompli and then receives legislative protection,” it warned.

Meanwhile, J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Monday highlighted the need for “a practical and balanced approach to sustainable mountain development”.

Speaking at the 13th Sustainable Mountain Development Summit in Srinagar, Mr. Abdullah drew attention to climate change, erratic snowfall, water scarcity, extreme rainfall and landslides affecting Jammu and Kashmir.

“These developments are the new reality. The challenge was to determine how Jammu and Kashmir could continue to develop while adapting to growing environmental risks. Development is essential, but it must be sustainable,” said Mr. Abdullah.

He said environmental responsibility had to be shared by the government, residents, businesses and visitors alike. He urged locals to avoid littering, reduce the use of single-use plastic and conserve water and energy.

Highlighting the need for environmentally sound infrastructure, the J&K Chief Minister said unscientific hill cutting during road construction had contributed to landslides and repeated damage to roads, particularly in far-flung areas of Jammu and Kashmir. He asked the Forest and Environment Department and the Public Works Department to work together to ensure that development projects incorporated sustainable engineering practices and reduced the risk of landslides.

World.title: Musk has spent $276 million on midterms to help Republicans retain control of Congress
World.content:
Elon Musk has spent roughly $366 million ​in the 2026 U.S. midterm election cycle so far, $276 million of it since July ‌to help Republicans retain control of Congress, even as Democrats’ chances ​of retaking the U.S. House and Senate have improved.

Mr. Musk’s largesse, ⁠which was reported earlier by the New York Times, makes the world’s richest person likely the single-biggest political donor in this year’s races, according to campaign finance records.

There is ‌a lot at stake for Mr. Musk with Democrats in the U.S. House of Representatives calling for investigations into his government contracts as ‌CEO of aerospace company SpaceX, as well as his work running the ‌Department ⁠of Government Efficiency under President Donald Trump.

A breakdown ⁠of his political spending, which was confirmed by a spokesman for his super PAC America PAC:

Mr. Musk has spent $366 million so far this election cycle, which began January 1, 2025. At ​least $276 million so far has ‌gone to Republican groups and his own super PAC since July. Of the $276 million in third-quarter donations:

$158 million went to the Senate Leadership Fund, the super PAC set up to help elect Republicans to the Senate ‌that is aligned with Senate Majority Leader John Thune, a Republican from South ​Dakota.

$20 million went to the Congressional Leadership Fund, the super PAC set up for House Republicans that is aligned with House ⁠Speaker Mike Johnson, a Louisiana Republican.

$76 million went to Musk’s America PAC. $10 million went to the Lone Star Liberty PAC, which is supporting Republican state ‌Attorney General Ken Paxton’s run for the U.S. Senate in Texas, where recent polls have him in a dead heat against Democrat James Talarico.

$10 million went to the Republican Governors Association. $2 million went to the Republican Attorneys General Association.

America PAC is helping Republican candidates in seven battleground states and nearly three dozen House races. The new giving will be publicly disclosed ‌when many super PACs are required to disclose their third-quarter spending on Thursday (October 15, 2026).

Mr. Musk has ​also donated more money through groups that do not disclose their donors, according to the New York Times report.

Roughly $90 million spent ⁠this cycle paid for work done in the prior election or supported other ⁠issues, including an unsuccessful candidate for the Wisconsin Supreme Court and a controversial program paying $1 million to registered voters who signed a petition supporting ‌free speech and gun rights, according to an America PAC spokesman.

Mr. Musk spent roughly $290 million during the last election cycle in which Mr. Trump won ​the presidential election race against former Vice President Kamala Harris.

World.title: Restrictions on firecrackers: Supreme Court urges balance between religious sentiments and public health
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Monday (October 12, 2026) highlighted the need to balance religious sentiments with public health concerns while considering restrictions on firecrackers in the national capital and neighbouring regions.

“We will not hurt religious sentiments but at the same time, people should themselves come forward and opt for it. The whole exercise should involve a balancing approach,” Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, heading a three-judge Bench, said.

During the hearing, Justice Joymalya Bagchi questioned the religious basis for bursting firecrackers.

Health risks

Senior advocate Aparajita Singh, who is the amicus curiae in the case, expounded on the health risks associated with air pollution, particularly for children, senior citizens, and those suffering from health vulnerabilities. Ms. Singh suggested that the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), the statutory body responsible for air quality management in the region, should be asked to turn its attention to the medical concerns related to air pollution.

The Bench, however, cautioned against imposing restrictions that could prove difficult to enforce on the ground. “We have to make people wiser, bring awareness, and tell them which firecrackers are harmful and which are less harmful,” the CJI said.

He suggested promoting a culture centred on traditional practices, such as lighting lamps and using sparklers, along with restrictions on the availability of more harmful cracker varieties.

The matter will be heard next on October 15.

World.title: Delhi police accused of beating, assaulting detainees, denying them basic rights
World.content:
Detainees’ accounts of beatings, assaults, and excessiive force used by the Delhi police over the last few days have raised concerns about post-detention practices of law enforcement personnel.

Thousands of protesters have been detained by the police in the national capital on October 10, 11, and 12, including journalists, members of youth organisations, and minors.

There was a fresh slew of detentions on Monday (October 12, 2026) as youth organisations, including the Naujawan Bharat Sabha, Revolutionary Workers’ Party of India (RWPI), and Disha Students’ Organisation, carried out a flash mob rally at Barakhamba Road, protesting the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a protest site. They were stopped by the police at Sansad Marg and detained.

Physical, verbal abuse

“We were put inside a prison-looking van, beaten up, and taken to a detention centre. Women protesters were abused verbally and held by the neck by the police,” said RWPI member Vishal.

Another RWPI member, Nishu, said that the police denied requests for water, even after detainees fainted inside the police van. “One of our members fainted and another was feeling dizzy after police detained us brutally from near Jantar Mantar. We shouted and screamed for water but despite having several water bottles with them, they did not give us water,” she said, also displaying the multiple bruises and marks on her hands, face, and legs.

Pattern of violence

This pattern of police violence against detainees caught the spotlight on October 10, when Disha member Aranya was held by the throat by two policewomen inside one of the buses used for detainees, swept off the streets after a rally at Raj Ghat.

The next day, on October 11, she was again detained along with other Disha members from Connaught Place. This time, however, the police isolated her and allegedly beat her up. Her fellow activists could hear her screaming from inside a moving prison-van, they said.

“They were beating us up and stealing away our phones from our pockets. Then they isolated Aranya and she was made to lie down on the ground. A police woman was sitting on her and choking her. Another police woman was hitting her with her elbow. We told her she was facing difficulty breathing but instead of listening to us, she threatened us for making videos and recording the police action on our phones,” said Naureen, a Disha member.

Aggression in an isolated police camp

Another group of detainees taken to Pandwalan Khurd alleged that they were made to sit down in rows inside the van and hand over their phones before they were thrashed by the police.

Arjun Unnikrishan said he, along with fellow protesters, had been transported by bus to an “isolated, enclosed police camp near the LIC building to cut off contact with the public and media.”

“At the camp, we were forced to sit in execution-style rows while police officers aggressively confiscated mobile phones and deleted video footage without regard for privacy. Despite an officer claiming to be an ASI or DCP, offering deceptive reassurances to secure cooperation, officers, including one identified as Mr. Arvind Kumar, severely assaulted us,” he said.

The prison-van was described by detainees as a vehicle with seven to eight compartments each holding about ten people. The detainees also included four minors. “The police mercilessly slapped, punched, and struck the first few batches of people on their faces and private parts in the cramped space,” Mr. Unnikrishnan said.

Systematic beatings

One of the detainees was environment journalist and author M. Rajshekhar, who witnessed the assaults on other detainees though he himself was not beaten. He said the group was taken to a community centre at Pandwalan Khurd, adding that while detainees were released late on Sunday (October 11) night, many did not get their phones back.

“The manner in which these beatings took place inside the ‘convict-van’ was pretty systematic,” he explained. “Each person who went inside was beaten up by three cops, each cop taking his turn for about 30 seconds and beating up each detainee ruthlessly. The leaders were cherry-picked from the group. Their phones were snatched away, which created problems for many later as they were dependant on their phones to go back home after their release,” Mr. Rajshekhar said.

“I was saved because I told them I was not a protester, only a photographer merely covering the protest,” he added.

World.title: Demolition of tribals’ houses in M.P. draws Shivraj’s anger; says ‘Mohan ji became CM with their votes’
World.content:
Demolition of houses of several tribal families in Madhya Pradesh’s Budhni has prompted Union Agriculture Minister and former Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan to push back against the State’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government and say that “the limits of oppression and injustice have been crossed” in his constituency and that his successor Mohan Yadav had become the CM “with their very votes”.

Mr. Yadav said on Monday (October 12, 2026) that the matter had come to his attention and that an inquiry will be conducted into it.

In a visibly angry address late on Sunday (October 11, 2026), Mr. Chouhan said, “My constituency has witnessed the height of oppression and the extreme limit of injustice. Homes that were thriving until this morning—where the joyful sounds of children once echoed—are now filled with their screams. Women are weeping and beating their chests in anguish. Their homes have been demolished and their crops buried under the rubble. The fruits of their hard labour are crushed, and their wells are filled in. These were homes that had stood for years, yet today, these people have been left destitute and displaced.”

Mr Chouhan, who visited the spot in Sehore district’s Kosmi and met affected families on Sunday night (October 11, 2026), said that after speaking with State Chief Secretary Ashok Barnwal and M.P. BJP president Hemant Khandelwal to inform them of the matter, he would also raise it with CM Yadav. He also sought strict action against the officials responsible for the action.

On Sunday (October 11, 2026), houses of about 12 tribal families in Kosmi village were demolished by the Forest Department over alleged encroachment. The department says the houses were built on forest land after a 2021 plantation was destroyed.

The village falls under the Budhni Assembly seat, which he represented for nearly two decades. Budhni also falls under the Vidisha Lok Sabha constituency, which Mr. Chouhan currently holds for the BJP.

After meeting the families, Mr. Chouhan said, “The Chief Minister needs to be apprised of this injustice. I will convey everything to him. This appears to be a conspiracy to tarnish the Chief Minister’s reputation as well. These are the very people who consistently vote for the BJP; they voted for us in both the Lok Sabha and the Assembly elections. This is a plot by certain officials to tarnish the party’s image. It is their votes that secure our victories, and it was their votes that made Mohan ji the Chief Minister. This is truly deeply distressing for me.”

“I had requested that, since they have held possession of this land for years, they should not be harassed,” he said, expressing anger that no senior official from the Forest Department or the local administration was present during his visit.

A close aide of Mr. Chouhan told The Hindu that the former CM had spoken to Mr. Yadav about this matter on Sunday morning (October 11, 2026), requesting him to halt the drive, as the Forest officials had earlier served eviction notices to the families.

“The CM had assured him [Mr. Chouhan] that the action would be stopped. But it seems the drive went on anyway without the CM’s knowledge,” the aide said, requesting anonymity.

“The houses were in the interior and were not obstructing any development work. The families also have receipts and records showing that they have been living there since before 1989,” he said, denying the forest department’s claims.

The question was put to Mr. Yadav during a press conference on Monday (October 12, 2026), to which he responded, saying, “The matter has come to my attention, so I have said that we will get it inquired. If a senior leader of our party has said something, we will look into it.”

Meanwhile, the Opposition Congress has taken the incident to attack the ruling party and has alleged that the incident was a result of the BJP’s “internal power tussle”.

Leader of the Opposition in the State Assembly, Umang Singhar, took to X and said, “Mohan Yadav ji, when your own former Chief Minister is raising questions, you too must clarify when the government will take concrete steps. Is the internal power struggle within the government overshadowing even questions of public interest?”

“Shivraj ji, merely raising questions about the injustice done to tribal families is not enough; it is also essential to establish accountability. The public deserves a clear explanation: on whose orders were the homes of poor families demolished? Who is behind this action, and whose protection do the responsible officials enjoy?” Mr. Singhar asked.

Mr. Chouhan, who helmed the State for nearly 17 years, has on several occasions publicly countered his successor in the past three years.

In July 2026, Mr. Chouhan issued a public letter to Mr. Yadav to counter his government’s claims on moong pulse procurement, in the midst of a farmers’ protest in the State capital, Bhopal, with demonstrators laying siege near the Chief Minister’s residence.

World.title: Collect fee by 24-hour cycle, not on day basis at parking stands, demand public
World.content:
The public has demanded the Salem Corporation to strictly instruct the staff at the parking stands, especially at the New Bus Stand, to collect parking fees for 24 hours instead of collecting it on a day basis.

The Salem Corporation provides tenders to private individuals to operate parking stands at various locations in the Corporation, including at the Salem New Bus Stand and Old Bus Stand. Earlier, ₹15 was collected for two-wheelers for 24 hours of parking at these stands. However, seven months ago, the Corporation increased the fee for two-wheelers from ₹15 to ₹25 for 24 hours. Later, they started to collect the fee on a daily basis (12 a.m. to 12 a.m.).

A. Kumar, a resident of Ammapet, said that he parked his two-wheeler at the parking stand of the New Bus Stand at 9 p.m. on October 8 and paid ₹25. At 6 a.m. on October 10, when he returned, the parking stand staff demanded him to pay an additional ₹50. “While I pointed out that only 33 hours had passed, the staff adamantly demanded ₹50, claiming that the fee is now collected on a daily basis,” Mr. Kumar said, adding that he had to pay the ₹50, without a choice, and left the stand. “If Corporation officials verified the CCTV footage at the stand, they will find that the my claims are true, Mr. Kumar added.

Similarly, R.
